```
❯ cat docs/mcp-app-url-options.md
# `APP_URL` and the MCP-safe URL constraint

**The one-line version:** TREK will not run its MCP OAuth server on an arbitrary
URL. If `APP_URL` is neither `https://…` nor `http://localhost…`, MCP silently
falls back to `http://localhost:3000` — the *container's* view — and every agent
client fails to complete the OAuth handshake. The web UI is unaffected.

Discovered 2026-07-29 while moving this instance from the Mac to `david_ubuntu`.
It is not documented in TREK's README; the only signal is one line in
`data/logs/trek.log`:

```
[WARN] APP_URL: not MCP-safe (requires https:// or http://localhost) — MCP will use http://localhost:3000.
```

## How to tell you have hit it

```bash
curl -s "$APP_URL/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" | head -c 200
```

`"resource"` and `"authorization_servers"` must echo **your** `APP_URL`. If they
say `http://localhost:3000` while you set something else, MCP is broken — even
though `/api/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`, `/mcp` returns `401`, and
`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` returns `200`. **All three of those look
healthy in the broken state**, which is what makes this worth writing down.

Why it exists: the MCP authorization spec inherits OAuth 2.1's requirement that
issuer URLs be HTTPS, with `localhost` exempted for development. TREK enforces it
rather than emitting a subtly broken discovery document.

---

## Option 1 — Tailscale HTTPS + `tailscale serve` ✅ chosen

Real Let's Encrypt certificate for the tailnet name, valid in any browser, no CA
to import on clients, and MCP-safe. Reachable from every tailnet device.

```
APP_URL=https://david-ubuntu.tail7f7fc5.ts.net
TREK_BIND=127.0.0.1      # serve fronts it; no need to publish on the tailnet IP
TREK_PORT=39100
```

**Two privileged one-time steps** (neither can be done over a non-interactive SSH
session, so they are yours to run):

1. **Enable HTTPS on the tailnet** — <https://login.tailscale.com/admin/dns> →
   *HTTPS Certificates* → **Enable**. This is a tailnet-wide switch and affects
   every device on it, including the other person's. Verify afterwards:

   ```bash
   ssh david_ubuntu 'tailscale status --json | grep -i certdomains'
   ```
   It reported `CertDomains: None` before enabling — that is the "off" state.

2. **Let the non-root user drive tailscale** (once, on the box):

   ```bash
   sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER
   ```

Then, unprivileged:

```bash
ssh david_ubuntu 'tailscale serve --bg --https=443 http://127.0.0.1:39100'
ssh david_ubuntu 'tailscale serve status'
```

Update `.env` on the box (`APP_URL`, `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, `TREK_BIND=127.0.0.1`),
`docker compose up -d`, then re-point the client:

```bash
claude mcp remove trek -s project
claude mcp add --transport http trek https://david-ubuntu.tail7f7fc5.ts.net/mcp -s project
claude mcp login trek
```

**Bonus**: `COOKIE_SECURE=false` can finally be deleted — that line only ever
existed because everything was plain HTTP.

**Caveats**: the certificate is issued for the tailnet name, so it only resolves
on the tailnet (MagicDNS). Tailscale must be running on any client that browses
it — already true for the Mac. Enabling HTTPS certificates also makes tailnet
device names appear in Let's Encrypt's public Certificate Transparency logs.

## Option 2 — SSH tunnel + `http://localhost`

Zero sudo, zero admin-console changes, works today.

```
APP_URL=http://localhost:39100
TREK_BIND=127.0.0.1     # or leave on the tailscale IP for direct UI browsing
TREK_PORT=39100
```

On the Mac, whenever you want the agent to reach TREK:

```bash
ssh -N -L 39100:127.0.0.1:39100 david_ubuntu &
claude mcp add --transport http trek http://localhost:39100/mcp -s project
claude mcp login trek     # browser hits localhost:39100 -> tunnel -> box
```

**Costs**: the tunnel has to be up for MCP to work — an easy thing to forget, and
the failure looks like a dead MCP server rather than a dead tunnel. Any link TREK
*generates* (share links, email/notification URLs) will say `localhost:39100`,
which is wrong for anyone but you. Fine for a single-operator agent workflow, bad
once other people are invited to co-edit — which is an explicit goal of this
project.

## Option 3 — Caddy with `tls internal`

The box already runs native Caddy with a staged `~/infra/caddy/Caddyfile` using a
`<service>.home.arpa` convention.

```caddyfile
trek.home.arpa {
        tls internal
        reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:39100
}
```

```
APP_URL=https://trek.home.arpa
```

**Costs**: `sudo cp` into `/etc/caddy/` + `systemctl reload caddy`; `sudo caddy
trust` on the box; and the internal CA root must be imported on **every** client
that browses or agents against it — a browser that does not trust the CA will
also fail the OAuth redirect. Worse, `*.home.arpa` resolution over Tailscale is
**unverified** (it depends on AdGuard on that box serving DNS for the tailnet); if
it does not resolve on the Mac, `APP_URL` points at a name the client cannot
reach. Check `dig trek.home.arpa @100.77.43.16` from the Mac before committing.

Strictly worse than Option 1 unless you specifically do not want the tailnet-wide
HTTPS switch flipped.

## Option 4 — leave MCP on the Mac

Run the box instance as the human-facing web UI only, keep an agent-facing
instance on the Mac at `http://localhost:3100`.

**Why this was rejected**: two live SQLite databases, both accepting writes, with
no sync between them. TREK's scheduled jobs (trip reminders, AirTrail sync) write
on their own, so the two copies diverge even when nobody touches them. It defeats
the "single canonical itinerary store" premise the whole architecture rests on.

## Comparison

| | Tailscale HTTPS ✅ | SSH tunnel | Caddy internal | Split |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sudo / admin console | 2 one-time steps | none | sudo + CA import per client | none |
| works without setup on Mac | yes | tunnel must be up | needs CA + DNS | n/a |
| generated links correct | yes | **no** (`localhost`) | yes | n/a |
| usable by collaborators | yes | no | tailnet + CA only | no |
| lets `COOKIE_SECURE=false` go | **yes** | no | yes | no |
| single canonical DB | yes | yes | yes | **no** |
```

## Repo conventions for where a new tailscale helper belongs

**The decision boundary observed across the repo:**

**Shell function in `dot_config/shell/NN_*.sh`** — for thin wrappers around an existing binary, ~1–30 lines, no state, no argument parsing beyond `$1`. Numbered-prefix modular files auto-sourced by both bash and zsh via `load_modular_dir`. `50_networking.sh` is the natural home for tailscale wrappers (it already holds `ipgeo`/`vpncheck`/`lanscan`/`tv-lan`/`wifiscan`/`tv-wifi`). Use `.tmpl` only when OS/prompt gating is needed (see `49_homelab.sh.tmpl`, `54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl`). Conventions from the `49_homelab.sh.tmpl` header: `# shellcheck shell=sh`, POSIX-portable, all public functions accept `--help`, internal helpers get a `_prefix_` name, root-needing paths elevate via a single `sudo -v`. **Every new alias/function must get a row in `docs/shells/aliases.md`** (and the `aliases` tv channel picks it up from there).

**In-house CLI in `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_<name>`** — for real programs: subcommand dispatch, JSON output, caching, TUI. Almost all are Python with a **PEP 723 `# /// script` header + `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script`** shebang (see `executable_appsrc`, `executable_fleet`). Deploys to `~/.dotfiles/bin/` (rationale recorded in `backlog/bin-migration.md`). `CLAUDE.md` L28 states the hard requirement: **a new CLI here must ship tab completion for both shells** — `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`, kept in sync, plus a row in `docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md` § F. Also expects a `docs/tools/<name>.md` page and an `mkdocs.yml` nav entry.

**Python module in `scripts/<tool>/*.py`** — only for **multi-module** implementations behind a thin `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_<tool>` dispatcher. Exactly the `fleet` pattern: `executable_fleet` dispatches into `scripts/fleet/{apply,exec,hosts,info,pueue,tmux}.py`, each with its own PEP 723 header. `scripts/adhoc/` is for one-off audits, `scripts/lib/` for shared code.

**Television channel** — a `.toml` in `dot_config/television/cable/` with `[metadata] name/description/requirements`, `[source]`, `[preview]`, `[keybindings]` (Alt+ namespace to dodge tmux/TV conflicts), `[actions.*]` with `mode = "execute"|"fork"`, plus a top-of-file comment block documenting usage/source-cycling/keys. Heavy logic goes into a sibling `dot_config/television/executable_<name>-source.sh` / `-preview.sh` / `.py`, often with a TSV cache under `~/.cache/tv/` and `watch = N.N` for streaming (the `lan-devices` + `lan-scan.sh` pattern). Add `tv-<name>` + scan aliases to `50_networking.sh`, a row in `docs/shells/aliases.md`, and a section in `docs/tools/tv.md`. Use `.toml.tmpl` only if the channel needs OS gating.

**Given the existing footprint, a tailscale utility fits most naturally as:** a `50_networking.sh` function set (`ts-*` / `tsip` / `tsssh`) + a `tailnet` tv channel with a `dot_config/television/executable_tailnet-source.sh` backed by `tailscale status --json`, mirroring `lan-devices` almost exactly. An `executable_tailnet` Python CLI would only be warranted if you need caching, cross-host aggregation, or `--json`/AI-summary output like `fleet`/`pqsum`. Note that a Linux install path would have to be added to ansible first (probably `networking_tools`), since none exists today.
```

**Loading**: `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl` both define `load_modular_dir()` with the same signature; zsh calls `load_modular_dir "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell" sh`, so every `dot_config/shell/*.sh` is sourced by both shells at startup.

### CLI interface
```
Usage: ssh-setup-remote [user@]host
```
Exactly one positional arg; no flags. `[ $# -ne 1 ]` → prints usage to stderr, `return 1`.

### Steps (fully interactive — ~10 `read -r` prompts, no `--yes`/non-interactive mode)
- **Step 0** — lists `~/.ssh/*.pub` (portable nullglob: `setopt localoptions nullglob` on zsh / `shopt -s nullglob` + restore on bash), asks "Use an existing key? [Y/n]".
- **Step 0b** — if creating: prompts algorithm (`ed25519` default, also `ed25519-sk`/`rsa`), key name (default `id_${algo}_${remote_host}`), comment (default `${USER}@$(hostname -s) -> ${remote_host}`), passphrase y/N. Runs `ssh-keygen`; adds `-b 4096` for rsa.
- **Step 1** — `ssh-copy-id -i "${key_path}.pub" "$target"`.
- **Step 2** — optional `scp` of the key **pair** to `$target:~/.ssh/`, then `chmod 600/644` remotely; optionally appends a `Host github.com / IdentityFile` block to the *remote's* `~/.ssh/config`.
- **Step 3** — local `~/.ssh/config` wiring. Two modes:
  - **Mode B (alias already configured)** — edits the existing `Host` block *in place*, in whichever file it actually lives in (follows `Include` recursively). Offers `[r]eplace / [a]dd another / [s]kip` for an existing `IdentityFile`, and optional `IdentitiesOnly yes`. Validates with `ssh -G "$alias"` afterwards.
  - **Mode A (new host, or no python3)** — prompts alias / HostName / User / IdentitiesOnly, then **prefers `~/.ssh/config.d/host_${host_alias}`** if that dir exists, else appends to `~/.ssh/config`. `chmod 600`. If it wrote a drop-in that isn't reachable via `Include`, it offers to add one.

### Exit codes
Only `return 1` (usage error, key-not-found, key-already-exists, `ssh-keygen`/`ssh-copy-id`/`scp` failure) and implicit `0`. **No distinct exit codes.**

### The embedded Python helper — this is the most reusable piece for you
`_ssh_cfg_py()` in the same file (lines 33-241) is a heredoc'd `python3 -` script. It is the repo's only real SSH-config parser/editor:

```
find <alias> [keypath]                 kv lines, "---BLOCK---", then the block. rc 0=found, 3=not found
insert <file> <alias> <key> <action> [--identities-only]   action: insert|replace|add, atomic, mode 0600
ensure-include                         rc 0 if ~/.ssh/config.d is reachable via Include, else 1
add-include                            prepend `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` (idempotent)
```
Key properties worth reusing: honours `$SSH_CFG_ROOT` (defaults `~/.ssh/config`), `resolve_includes()` walks `Include` recursively with glob + `~`/relative/absolute expansion and realpath cycle-detection, `write_atomic()` uses `mkstemp` in the same dir + `os.replace` + `chmod 0600`, `tildify()` rewrites `$HOME/...` back to `~/...`, and `block_matches()` deliberately **skips wildcard patterns** (`re.search(r"[*?!]", p)`). Returns **127 when `python3` is absent** so callers fall back to plain append.

### Tab completion for `ssh-setup-remote`
**None.** It's absent from the § F table in `docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md` and there is no `*_ssh_setup_completion.*` file. It is documented as a row in `docs/shells/aliases.md:567` (type: `function`) and has a tutorial section at `docs/tutorials/setup_ssh_key_on_remote.md:223` ("Automation: `ssh-setup-remote`").

## 2. SSH config management — yes, `~/.ssh/config` IS chezmoi-managed (create-only)

`git ls-files dot_ssh` → exactly three files:

| Source | Target | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ssh/create_private_config` | `~/.ssh/config` | `create_` = seed once, never overwrite; `private_` = 0600 |
| `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ssh/private_config.d/create_private_00-defaults` | `~/.ssh/config.d/00-defaults` | dir is `private_` (0700) |
| `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ssh/private_config.d/create_private_01_git` | `~/.ssh/config.d/01_git` | |

`chezmoi managed` confirms: `.ssh`, `.ssh/config`, `.ssh/config.d`, `.ssh/config.d/00-defaults`, `.ssh/config.d/01_git`. The live `~/.ssh/config.d/` currently contains exactly `00-defaults` and `01_git`.

- **There is no `private_dot_ssh/`, no `dot_config/ssh/`, and no `modify_`-prefixed SSH file anywhere.** All three are `create_` — meaning **chezmoi will never touch these files again after first apply**. A generator that rewrites SSH config must therefore be a *runtime tool*, not a chezmoi template.
- **The drop-in `~/.ssh/config.d/` pattern is real and load-bearing.** `create_private_config` line 9 is `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` and it is deliberately the **first directive**, documented in its own comments:
  > "To opt a host out, set `ControlMaster no` in a `~/.ssh/config.d/` file: `Include` is the first directive in this file and ssh takes the first-obtained value for each keyword, so config.d always wins."
- Naming convention in `config.d/` is lexical-ordered `NN-name` / `NN_name` (both dash and underscore in use: `00-defaults`, `01_git`). `ssh-setup-remote`'s Mode A writes `host_${host_alias}` (no NN prefix).
- `Host *` in the root config sets `ServerAliveInterval 60`, `ServerAliveCountMax 3`, and **connection multiplexing** — `ControlMaster auto`, `ControlPath ~/.ssh/cm-%C`, `ControlPersist 10m`. (`%C` is used specifically because macOS rejects unix socket paths over ~104 bytes.)

### `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` re SSH
**No SSH-related entries at all** — `grep -n "ssh" .chezmoiignore.tmpl` returns nothing. The critical line for you is **line 93: `scripts/**`** — anything under `scripts/` is never deployed to `$HOME`.

## 3. Fleet host inventory

### Inventory file
`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` → `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`, `create_` + `private_` (0600, seeded once). It's a template only because of `no_root_machine = {{ .noRoot }}`. It ships one real host (`self`, `local = true`) plus six commented example blocks.

### Schema (the parser is `load_hosts()` in `scripts/fleet/apply.py:132`)
`@dataclasses.dataclass class Host` at `scripts/fleet/apply.py:64`:

```python
name: str
ssh_alias: str | None = None
hostname: str | None = None
user: str | None = None
port: int | None = None
identity_file: str | None = None
no_root_machine: bool = False
chezmoi_path: str = "auto"
local: bool = False
extra_env: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
password_source_type / password_source_arg / sudo_password
ssh_login_password_source_type / ssh_login_password_source_arg / ssh_login_password
```

TOML shape: a `[defaults]` table (`chezmoi_path`, `connect_timeout`, `command_timeout`) merged into each `[[hosts]]` (host wins), plus `password_source = { type = "plain"|"prompt"|"bitwarden"|"none", value=|item= }`.

Validation rules in `load_hosts()`:
- `name` required; duplicates raise.
- **Unknown TOML keys are silently dropped**: `host_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(Host)}` then `{k: v for k, v in merged.items() if k in host_fields}` — so adding e.g. a `tailscale_id` field to machines.toml would be discarded unless you add it to `Host`.
- Non-local hosts must have `ssh_alias` **or** `hostname`.

`DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH` (apply.py:107) honours `$FLEET_CONFIG`, else `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`.

### `scripts/fleet/` modules
| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `scripts/fleet/__init__.py` | Re-exports `DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH`, `Host`, `load_hosts`, `connect_host`, `resolve_passwords`, `resolve_ssh_login_passwords`, `_connect_kwargs` from `apply.py` so submodules do `from scripts.fleet import ...` |
| `scripts/fleet/apply.py` | The SSOT: `Host` dataclass, `load_hosts()`, asyncssh connection, `chezmoi update --init` fan-out, readiness/status/tail/compact |
| `scripts/fleet/hosts.py` | **Most relevant to you** — inventory introspection + picker + SSH exec |
| `scripts/fleet/exec.py` | Cross-host argv-list command runner |
| `scripts/fleet/info.py` | Cross-host system snapshot |
| `scripts/fleet/pueue.py` | Cross-host pueue summary |
| `scripts/fleet/tmux.py` | Cross-host tmux session summary |

`hosts.py` is the model for a "generate a list, feed a tv channel" tool. Its output modes: `--list` (plain), `--list-tsv` (`name\ttarget\tkind`), `--list-json`, `--describe NAME`, `--probe NAME`, and bare `NAME` → `os.execvp("ssh", ...)`. Note `_cmd_list_json` defensively pops `sudo_password`/`ssh_login_password` and redacts `type="plain"` args.

Also note `hosts.py`'s docstring explicitly names your problem space:
> "Mirrors `dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml` (which is sourced from `~/.ssh/config`), but reads `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml` instead…"

### `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet`
Deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/fleet`. PEP 723 header (`asyncssh`, `tyro`, `rich`), a `USAGE` string, and `_source_path()` which resolves the chezmoi source dir at runtime via `chezmoi source-path` with a `~/.local/share/chezmoi` fallback — **this is the standard workaround for `scripts/**` being chezmoi-ignored**. It then `sys.path.insert(0, str(src))` and dispatches via a plain dict:
```python
dispatch = {"chezmoi": ..., "edit": ..., "tmux": ..., "info": ..., "pueue": ..., "exec": ..., "hosts": _dispatch_hosts}
```
Each `_dispatch_*` sets `sys.argv = ["fleet hosts", *forwarded]` then imports and calls `main()`.

### `justfile` `fleet-*` recipes (line ~514-631)
`fleet *ARGS` (calls `uv run --script ./dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet`), then direct `./scripts/fleet/apply.py`-backed recipes: `fleet-apply`, `fleet-edit`, `fleet-status`, `fleet-status-quick`, `fleet-apply-dry-run`, `fleet-diff HOST`, `fleet-apply-file PATH`, `fleet-apply-branch`, `fleet-apply-branch-force`, `fleet-apply-one HOST`, `fleet-apply-kill`, `fleet-apply-status`, `fleet-apply-watch`, `fleet-apply-tail HOST`, `fleet-apply-compact`. Note `just fleet-edit` duplicates the seed template that also lives in `executable_fleet:_SEED_TEMPLATE` — a known two-copy drift risk.

## 4. `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` — the model

Full file quoted below (it's 84 lines, no `.tmpl`):

```toml
[metadata]
name = "fleet-hosts"
description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]

[source]
command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"
display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[preview]
command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:connect"
alt-t = "actions:probe"
alt-s = "actions:status"
alt-i = "actions:info"
alt-p = "actions:pueue"

[actions.connect]
description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "execute"
```
The other four actions follow the same shape, each suffixed with `; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _` because `mode = "execute"` returns to the picker.

**Design rule stated in its header comments** (worth honouring in your new channel):
> "The actual TOML parsing lives in Python — this cable shells out to `fleet hosts --list-tsv` / `--describe N` / `N`. So this file stays small and the picker tracks any inventory changes automatically (no parallel TOML parser to keep in sync)."
>
> "Enter lands you in an attach-or-create tmux session (`fleet`) on the remote… That lives in `fleet hosts` itself, NOT here — do not inline an `ssh` invocation into this cable or the two will drift."

**`<mod>+<letter>` convention**: `Alt+` is mandatory for new actions. Stated in the cable header ("Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts"), in `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`, and as a hard rule in `CLAUDE.md:31` ("tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner apps; prefer `Alt+` for new actions"). `CLAUDE.md:22` adds: the paired-TUI rule that a launcher's single-letter `BINDINGS` and the channel's `<mod>+<letter>` actions must use **the same letters**.

Current Alt-key usage across all 48 cables (for picking free letters): `alt-r` ×14, `alt-t` ×13, `alt-c` ×13, `alt-s` ×11, `alt-p` ×10, `alt-e` ×9, `alt-y` ×8, `alt-d` ×6, `alt-o` ×5, `alt-j` ×4, `alt-x/k/i/a` ×3, `alt-m/h/b` ×2, `alt-v/u/n/l/g/f` ×1. `ctrl-y` ×32 is the universal "copy to clipboard (OSC 52)" binding.

**Sibling cable** `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml` is the `~/.ssh/config`-sourced twin: its `[source]` is a shell `for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*` loop piped through `awk` that emits `<source-file>\t<hostname>` and skips wildcard `Host` patterns (`if ($i !~ /[*?]/)`), then `sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2`. Its preview greps `ssh -G` output. Bindings: `enter`=connect, `alt-t`=probe, `alt-a`=offline scan_all.

**Cable channels are auto-discovered** — `channels.toml` awks `~/.config/television/cable/*.toml` for `[metadata] name/description`. No registration file to update.

A good precedent for a *cached, background-refreshed* host list is `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/lan-devices.toml` + `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/executable_lan-scan.sh`: TSV in `~/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv`, `watch = 2.0`, `no_sort = true`, multi-element `command = [...]` arrays for `Ctrl+S` source cycling and `Ctrl+F` preview cycling, and `mode = "fork"` actions that pair with `reload_source`. Its shell aliases are at `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh:87-94` (`lanscan`, `tv-lan`).

## 5. In-house CLI conventions (`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*`)

21 tools. Mix of bash and Python; **every Python one uses PEP 723 inline script metadata** with a `uv run --script` shebang.

**`fleet`** — Python, PEP 723:
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "asyncssh>=2.18",
#   "tyro>=0.9",
#   "rich>=13.9",
# ]
# ///
```
Arg parsing: **hand-rolled dict dispatch** at the umbrella level (`dispatch.get(sub)`), delegating to submodules that use `argparse` (`hosts.py`) or `tyro` (`apply.py`). Big triple-quoted `USAGE` constant printed on `-h`/`--help`/no args; unknown subcommand → prints usage to stderr and returns `2`.

**`mi-router`** — Python, PEP 723 (`tyro`, `httpx`, `rich`, `platformdirs`). Uses **tyro** (Strategy A completion). Credential precedence documented in its docstring: CLI flags → `~/.config/mi-router/config.toml` → env vars → **interactive `getpass` prompt (TTY only; offers to save to config)**. That last one is the repo's canonical interactive-prompt pattern for a Python CLI.

**`pqsum`** — Python, PEP 723 (`rich` only). `argparse` with positional subcommands defaulting to `text`. Interactive prompts via `--clean` (y/N per group) with a `--yes` escape hatch — note the safety design: `--yes` "still only acts on `safe-to-clean`".

**`x`** — plain `#!/usr/bin/env bash` + `set -euo pipefail`, a `usage()` function built from `printf '%s\n' \` with one arg per line, and an `err()` helper (`printf 'x: %s\n' "$*" >&2`).

**`wake`** — `#!/usr/bin/env python3` (deliberately **not** uv/PEP723): *"Pure stdlib (socket + tomllib) — no external dependency, so it works on a fresh box."* `argparse`. Its host list is `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`, seeded by `dot_config/wake/create_private_hosts.toml` — **this is the closest existing template for a new host-inventory-backed CLI**, and it exposes `wake --list-names` purely so its completion function can shell out to it.

**`dotcfg`** — bash wrapper whose header explains the whole `scripts/**`-is-ignored problem and why a thin deployed launcher is the answer.

### Logging
Your intuition is correct. `scripts/lib/log_shared.sh` header states it explicitly:
> "`scripts/**` is listed in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so this file is never deployed to `$HOME`. Its only runtime existence is the inlined copy or a source from the checkout."

Its two consumption mechanisms are (1) `{{ include "scripts/lib/log_shared.sh" }}` inside `run_*.sh.tmpl` chezmoi scripts, (2) `. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/lib/log_shared.sh"` from `scripts/*.sh`. **Neither is available to `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*`.** So the bin CLIs each hand-roll their own tiny output helpers (`err()` in `x`, `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` in the Python ones). `CLAUDE.md:14` codifies this: *"`$HOME`-deployed files can't use it."*

API for reference: `info` / `success` / `warn` / `error` / `skip` / `die`, plus `step` / `hr` / `dim`, plus verification-mode `ok`. Editing it rehashes every `run_onchange_after_*` that inlines it → batch edits.

## 6. Tab completion convention

**Doc**: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md` § F "In-house CLIs (this repo)" (line 140). It's a table of CLI / source / framework / strategy / files, followed by a **decision flow**:

1. tyro → Strategy A (lazy autoload, gen + mtime check, one file in `dot_config/shell/<NN>_<name>.sh`, plus a `<tool>-update-completion` helper in `10_aliases.sh`).
2. argparse → either `argcomplete` + Strategy C, or hand-write Strategy B.
3. Hand-rolled/shell → **Strategy B**: "One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers."
4. Update the § F table + `docs/shells/aliases.md` in the same commit.

### Example pair — `fleet` (NN=45)
`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh` — guard is `(( $+commands[fleet] )) || return 0`, ends with `compdef _fleet fleet`. Structure: dynamic helpers → per-subcommand `_arguments` funcs → top-level `_fleet` with `_arguments -C '1: :->subcommand' '*::arg:->args'` and a `_describe -t subcommands` list.

The dynamic-host pattern you'll want to copy verbatim:
```zsh
_fleet_hosts_one() {
    local -a hosts
    hosts=( ${(f)"$(fleet hosts --list 2>/dev/null)"} )
    (( ${#hosts} )) && _describe -t hosts 'fleet host' hosts
}
_fleet_hosts_csv() {
    local -a hosts
    hosts=( ${(f)"$(fleet hosts --list 2>/dev/null)"} )
    (( ${#hosts} )) && _values -s , 'fleet host' $hosts
}
```

`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/bash/45_fleet_completion.bash` — guard `command -v fleet >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0`, ends `complete -F _fleet_completion fleet`, uses `_init_completion -n =`, `compgen -W`, `COMPREPLY`, `_filedir`. Its CSV helper hand-rolls the `${cur%,*},` / `${cur##*,}` split since bash has no `_values -s ,`. Header says: *"Mirrors dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh — keep both in sync."*

## 7. Tests

**bats only. There is no pytest anywhere** — `pyproject.toml` is docs-build-only (`name = "chezmoi-docs"`, mkdocs deps), and grepping `pytest` across `pyproject.toml`, `justfile`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, and `.github/workflows/*.yml` returns zero hits. No `tests/**/*.py`.

**Layout**:
- `tests/test_helper.bash` — deliberately minimal ("No bats-assert / bats-file / bats-support — plain bats built-ins are enough"). Provides `setup_path_stub` (mktemp dir prepended to `PATH`, exported as `$BATS_STUB_DIR` — *not* via stdout, because command substitution would discard the export), `cleanup_path_stubs`, `REPO_ROOT`, and a default `teardown`.
- `tests/unit/`: `agent_overlays.bats`, `claude_plans_here.bats`, `copilot_proxy.bats`, `ghget.bats`, `lan_scan.bats`, `log_shared.bats`, `x_cli.bats`, `zsh_proxy.bats`.
- `tests/smoke/docker_install.bats`.
- `just bats` → `bats tests/unit`. `just check-all` → `lint bats docker-test`.

**The convention for testing an in-house CLI** — `tests/unit/x_cli.bats` is the template:
```bash
load "../test_helper.bash"
X_BIN="$REPO_ROOT/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x"
setup() { setup_path_stub; X_TMP="$(mktemp -d ...)"; export X_TMP; }
```
It tests the **source-tree file directly** (not the deployed `~/.dotfiles/bin/` copy), and stubs external binaries (`pbcopy`, `osascript`, `uname`) by writing executable shims into `$BATS_STUB_DIR`. `tests/unit/lan_scan.bats` shows how to unit-test a script that dispatches at the bottom: source it with a harmless subcommand (`source '$LAN_SCAN' clean`) against an isolated `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, then the function definitions remain in scope.

**Note the gap**: there is **no test for `ssh-setup-remote`**, none for `fleet hosts`, and none for any `dot_config/shell/*.sh` function. Lint coverage: `just lint-shell` runs shellcheck over `dot_config/shell/*.sh dot_config/bash/*.bash scripts/*.sh scripts/lib/*.sh` at `--severity=warning`; the pre-commit hook `shellcheck-shared` (`files: '^dot_config/(shell/[^/]+\.sh|bash/[^/]+\.bash)$'`) runs errors-only. **`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*` is not shellcheck'd at all.**

## Things that will bite your Tailscale utility

1. **`~/.ssh/config` and `config.d/*` are `create_`-only.** chezmoi seeds them once and then never touches them. Your generator must write at runtime, into `~/.ssh/config.d/<something>` — that directory already exists, is 0700, is `Include`d as the *first* directive of the root config (so it wins every keyword), and is loaded in lexical order. Taken names: `00-defaults`, `01_git`.
2. **`scripts/**` is chezmoi-ignored (`.chezmoiignore.tmpl:93`)**, so any Python module you put there is only reachable through the `_source_path()` → `chezmoi source-path` trick used by `executable_fleet`, or by inlining. That also means `scripts/lib/log_shared.sh` is unavailable to a deployed `~/.dotfiles/bin/` binary.
3. **`load_hosts()` silently drops unknown TOML keys** (`k in host_fields`), so a `tailscale_*` field in `machines.toml` will vanish unless you extend the `Host` dataclass.
4. `_ssh_cfg_py` in `96_ssh_setup.sh` already solves recursive-`Include` resolution, atomic 0600 writes, `~`-tildification, and wildcard-`Host` skipping. Duplicating that logic in a new tool creates a third SSH-config parser (the second being the `awk` in `ssh-config.toml`'s source command).
5. **Tailscale is currently install-only in this repo** — `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`, a `tailscale-app` Homebrew cask row in `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md`, a `tskey-` rule in `.gitleaks.toml:116`, and a `Tailscale IP or domain` comment in `docs/tools/ssh-agent.md:170`. 24	- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
25	  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
26	- This host: profile `{{ dig "profile" "" . }}`, OS `{{ .chezmoi.os }}`/`{{ .chezmoi.arch }}`, primary shell `{{ dig "primaryShell" "zsh" . }}`.
27	
28	## chezmoi essentials
29	
30	```bash
31	chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
32	chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
33	chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
34	chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
35	chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
36	chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
37	chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
38	chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
39	chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
40	```
41	
42	- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
43	  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
44	- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
45	  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
46	  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
47	- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
48	- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
49	  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
50	  `just upgrade-*`.
51

109	
110	## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)
111	
112	Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`, or read `docs/tools/<name>.md`. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.
113	
114	- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
115	- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
116	- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
117	- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
118	- **`view-office`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) in the terminal; also powers the yazi Office previewer. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`.
119	- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
120	- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
121	- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
122	- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
123	- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
124	- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
125	- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
126	- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.
127	
128	## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels
129	
130	There are ~40 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
131	that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:
132	
133	```bash
134	tv                      # default picker
135	tv list-channels        # list everything available
136	tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
137	ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
138	```
139	
140	Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`, `kill-process`, `services`,
141	`sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`, `mac-apps`/`linux-apps`. Full
142	reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.
143	
144	## Keybindings & keymaps
145	
146	- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
147	- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` (or `prefix + e`) opens the action menu;
148	  `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools. Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
149	- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
150	- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

152	## Aliases & functions
153	
154	`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
155	Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
156	`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
157	System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

```text
1	# Tailscale
2	
3	- [Download | Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/download/mac)
4	  - [tailscale-app — Homebrew Formulae](https://formulae.brew.sh/cask/tailscale-app) - Desktop App (Standalone)
5	    - [Tailscale Packages - stable track](https://pkgs.tailscale.com/stable/#macos)
6	  - [tailscale — Homebrew Formulae](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/tailscale) - CLI
7	  - [Tailscale App - App Store](https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/tailscale/id1475387142)
8	
9	> Standalone > App Store
10	
11	## How this repo installs it (macOS)
12	
13	- **GUI app + daemon** → `cask "tailscale-app"` in [`Brewfile.darwin`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl) — the **macsys standalone** build (`io.tailscale.ipn.macsys`), whose **system extension** is the daemon. Previously `mas "Tailscale"`, but Tailscale was **delisted from the Mac App Store**, so `mas` install now fails; the cask is the supported path.
14	- **CLI on PATH** → **also from the cask**, not a separate formula: the pkg installs `/usr/local/bin/tailscale`, a shell wrapper into the app bundle (`exec /Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/tailscale "$@"`). Do **not** also install the standalone `brew "tailscale"` formula — it's redundant and fights the cask over that same path on every upgrade (ollama-style link conflict) while shipping a `tailscaled` the app already runs.
15	- **Never** `brew services start tailscale` on macOS: the app's system extension already *is* the daemon; a second `tailscaled` would conflict.
16	
17	### "Another Tailscale copy was found on this Mac"
18	
19	If the debug panel reports a conflict at `/Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app` (often alongside `DNS Unavailable` / `dns-forward-failing`), that's the **old App Store build left behind** by the `mas → cask` migration (`chezmoi apply` is install-only and won't remove it). Fix:
20	
21	```bash
22	sudo rm -rf /Applications/Tailscale.localized   # deletes only the idle App Store copy
23	```
24	
25	Full detection + root cause: [`pitfalls/tailscale-another-copy-app-store-leftover.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/tailscale-another-copy-app-store-leftover.md).
26
```

 `./docs/tools/agent-skills.md`

```text
1	# Agent skills (`vercel-labs/skills`)
2	
3	This repo manages [`vercel-labs/skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills)
4	agent skills two ways, with sharply different scopes.
5	
6	## TL;DR
7	
8	| Scope | Lock file | Where the skill lives | Restored by |
9	|---|---|---|---|
10	| **Global** (every project, every shell) | `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` (chezmoi-managed) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` on every `chezmoi apply` |
11	| **Project** (only inside this repo's working tree, for editing skills) | `./skills-lock.json` (git-tracked) | `./.agents/skills/<name>/` | `.chezmoiscripts/repo/run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl` on every `chezmoi apply` (when source dir == repo); manual fallback: `just bootstrap-skills` |
12	| **First-party templated** (`chezmoi-dotfiles`) | none — chezmoi-managed | `~/.agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles/` (+ symlink in `~/.claude/skills/`) | `chezmoi apply` (re-renders per host from `.chezmoi.toml`) — see [§ First-party templated skill](#first-party-templated-skill-chezmoi-dotfiles) |
13	
14	The two scopes happen to overlap today (both install
15	`project-knowledge-harness`), but they serve different purposes — see "Why two
16	scopes?" below.
17	
18	## Global scope: must-have skills, on every machine
19	
20	The skills CLI does **not** yet support `npx skills install -g` from a lock
21	file ([upstream issue #283](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283),
22	[#549](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)). So we hand-roll
23	restore in two pieces:
24	
25	### `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` — the merger
26	
27	A `modify_` script that owns `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`. Every `chezmoi
28	apply`:
29	
30	1. Reads the live lock file via stdin.
31	2. Merges the **managed-set** declared in `$managed` (top of the script) into
32	   `.skills`, preserving any `installedAt`/`updatedAt`/`skillFolderHash` from
33	   the live entry.
34	3. Preserves any `.skills.<name>` entries **not** in the managed-set (so
35	   ad-hoc `npx skills add … -g` installs survive).
36	4. Preserves `.dismissed` and `.lastSelectedAgents` per-machine state
37	   verbatim.
38	
39	To declare a new must-have global skill, edit the inline `$managed` JSON in
40	that script:
41	
42	```json
43	{
44	  "skills": {
45	    "your-new-skill": {
46	      "source": "owner/repo",
47	      "sourceType": "github",
48	      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/owner/repo.git",
49	      "skillPath": "skills/your-new-skill/SKILL.md"
50	    }
51	  }
52	}
53	```
54	
55	Then run `chezmoi apply`. The merger writes the new entry into the lock; the
56	restore script (next section) sees the missing on-disk skill and installs it.
57	
58	### `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` — the restorer
59	
60	`onchange` hash trigger is the merger script's own SHA256 — so this script
61	re-runs whenever the **managed-set** is edited (not whenever the live lock
62	mutates from random `npx skills update -g` activity).
63	
64	For each entry in `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`:
65	
66	- If `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` exists → skip (already installed).
67	- Otherwise → `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y`.
68	
69	This is idempotent: a re-run on a fully-installed machine prints
70	"All globally-managed agent skills present; nothing to install" and exits.
71	
72	### After installing a new skill manually
73	
74	If you `npx skills add foo/bar -g` interactively on a machine and want it to
75	become managed across the fleet:
76	
77	1. `cat ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` — find the entry the CLI just wrote.
78	2. Copy `source` / `sourceType` / `sourceUrl` / `skillPath` into the
79	   `$managed.skills` block of `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl`.
80	3. Commit. Other hosts pick it up at next `chezmoi apply`.
81	
82	If you only want it on one machine, do nothing — the merger preserves the
83	live entry on the source machine, and other hosts simply never see it.
84	
85	## Project scope: editing-this-repo convenience
86	
87	`./skills-lock.json` + `./.agents/skills/` exist purely so that **when you're
88	editing the chezmoi repo itself**, agents launched from the repo root can use
89	`project-knowledge-harness` against the repo it documents. They are **not**
90	deployed (chezmoi-ignored: see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `.agents/skills`,
91	`.claude/skills`, `skills-lock.json`) and **not** git-tracked except for
92	`skills-lock.json` (`.gitignore` covers `.agents/`, `.claude/skills/`).
93	
94	Restore is automatic on `chezmoi apply` via
95	`.chezmoiscripts/repo/run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl`. The script:
96	
97	1. Checks whether `.chezmoi.sourceDir` contains a `skills-lock.json` (i.e.
98	   this machine's chezmoi source dir IS the repo). If not, exits silently —
99	   project skills only matter when you're editing the repo with an agent.
100	2. Fast-path: if every skill named in the lock already has a
101	   `./.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, exits without invoking npx.
102	3. Otherwise runs `npx skills@latest experimental_install` from the source
103	   dir to rebuild `./.agents/skills/...` and `./.claude/skills/...` symlinks.
104	
105	Trigger hash: SHA256 of `skills-lock.json` content, so the script only
106	re-runs when the lock actually changes.
107	
108	Manual fallback (if you want to force a re-bootstrap, or you cloned the repo
109	to a path that isn't your chezmoi source dir):
110	
111	```sh
112	just bootstrap-skills
113	# → npx skills@latest experimental_install
114	```
115	
116	## Why two scopes?
117	
118	| Use case | Where to install |
119	|---|---|
120	| Skill you want available in every project, on every machine | Global (edit `$managed` in the merger script) |
121	| Skill that only makes sense inside this specific repo | Project (`npx skills add ... -y` from repo root, commit `skills-lock.json`) |
122	| Skill you're prototyping locally before deciding | Project, then promote to global once stable |
123	
124	`project-knowledge-harness` is in **both** scopes today because (a) the harness
125	itself targets *any* project so it belongs globally, and (b) we want to use it
126	on the chezmoi repo immediately, which the global install covers but
127	project-scope makes the lock-file dependency explicit for anyone reading
128	`skills-lock.json` here.
129	
130	## First-party templated skill (`chezmoi-dotfiles`)
131	
132	Everything above is about **npx-pulled** skills (static clones from external
133	repos, in chezmoi-ignored `.agents/skills/**`). There is exactly one **first-party,
134	chezmoi-managed, *templated*** skill that breaks that mould:
135	
136	| | npx skills | `chezmoi-dotfiles` |
137	|---|---|---|
138	| Source | external git repo, cloned by `npx skills` | `dot_agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles/SKILL.md.tmpl` in this repo |
139	| Owner | `npx skills` CLI (`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`) | chezmoi (a normal managed target) |
140	| Per-host content | identical everywhere | **rendered from `.chezmoi.toml`** — only lists tools this host selected |
141	| Updates | `npx skills` / `just upgrade-skills` | **re-renders on every `chezmoi apply`** |
142	
143	**Why it exists:** so an agent opened in *any* directory can operate these dotfiles
144	and discover the repo's custom tooling (in-house CLIs, `tv` channels, keymaps, `just`
145	recipes) — most of which live under `docs/**`, which is **not** deployed to `$HOME`
146	and is only reachable via `chezmoi source-path`. The skill is deliberately **lean
147	and self-discovering** (it points at `docs/`, `tv list-channels`, `just --list`,
148	`ls $(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/`) so it rarely needs editing.
149	
150	**Deployment:**
151	
152	- Real file → `~/.agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles/SKILL.md` (the universal,
153	  cross-agent dir). Symlink `~/.claude/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles →
154	  ../../.agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles` (source: `dot_claude/skills/symlink_chezmoi-dotfiles`)
155	  so Claude Code discovers it — same per-agent-symlink shape `npx skills` uses.
156	- Re-included past the broad npx ignore in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` using **single-`*`**
157	  globs (`.agents/skills/*` + `.agents/skills/*/**`, not a bare `**`). This is
158	  load-bearing: a recursive `**` (or a bare `.agents/skills` dir line) excludes the
159	  *parent* directory, after which chezmoi — like gitignore — silently ignores the
160	  `!` re-include. Verify with `chezmoi managed | grep chezmoi-dotfiles`.
161	- It is **not** in any npx lock file (chezmoi-owned), so it never collides with an
162	  npx skill — provided the name stays namespaced (hence `chezmoi-dotfiles`, not a
163	  bare `dotfiles`, which could clash in the flat skill namespace).
164	
165	**Keeping it in sync:** see the `CLAUDE.md` cross-file maintenance row. Short
166	version: freshness is automatic; only edit the `.tmpl` when a section must be gated
167	on a **new prompt key** or a stable new CLI is worth naming.
168	
169	## How `npx skills` actually wires agents (mechanism reference)
170	
171	Verified by reading [`vercel-labs/skills/src/agents.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/agents.ts)
172	and [`installer.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/installer.ts).
173	Important because the CLI's "I installed your skill for agent X" message does
174	**not** mean agent X actually reads from `~/.agents/skills/` at runtime — that
175	is a per-agent convention, not a guarantee.
176	
177	### Two install strategies
178	
179	| Strategy | What the CLI writes | Agents that use it |
180	|---|---|---|
181	| **Universal** (`skillsDir: '.agents/skills'`) | Nothing in agent-specific dir; agent reads `~/.agents/skills/` (global) or `./.agents/skills/` (project) directly | `cursor`, `opencode`, `codex`, `gemini-cli`, `copilot`, `antigravity`, `warp`, `replit`, `cline`, `kimi-cli`, `firebender`, `deep-agents` |
182	| **Per-agent symlink** | Symlink `~/.<agent>/skills/<name>` → `~/.agents/skills/<name>` (copy on Windows) | `claude-code`, `augment`, `bob`, `cortex`, `crush`, `goose`, `junie`, `kilo`, `kiro`, `kode`, `roo`, `trae`, `windsurf`, etc. |
183	
184	The skip happens at `installer.ts`:
185	
186	```ts
187	if (isGlobal && isUniversalAgent(agentType)) {
188	  return { /* skipped: no symlink, no copy */ };
189	}
190	```
191	
192	So `npx skills add foo -g -a cursor -a opencode` produces **zero** files in
193	`~/.cursor/skills/` or `~/.opencode/skills/`. Whether Cursor and OpenCode
194	actually pick up `~/.agents/skills/foo/SKILL.md` at runtime is up to those
195	agents (Anthropic's Skills spec is Claude Code's; others adopt by convention,
196	not contract).
197	
198	### Lock filename collision (easy to confuse)
199	
200	| Path | Scope | Owner |
201	|---|---|---|
202	| `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` | Global, **singular** `skill-` | Skills CLI |
203	| `./skills-lock.json` | Project, **plural** `skills-` | Skills CLI |
204	
205	Schema differs (global is v3 with `dismissed`/`lastSelectedAgents`; project is
206	flatter). Don't symlink one to the other.
207	
208	### Restore commands and their quirks
209	
210	| Command | What it does |
211	|---|---|
212	| `npx skills experimental_install` | Restores **project** lock (`./skills-lock.json`) only |
213	| `npx skills experimental_install -g` | `-g` is **silently ignored**, still project-only ([#283](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283), [#549](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)) |
214	| `npx skills update -g` | Updates already-installed global skills; does **not** backfill missing entries from the lock |
215	| `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y` | The only working "restore one missing global skill" idiom — what `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` loops over |
216	
217	### CLI flag gotchas
218	
219	- **Repo shorthand requires `/skills` suffix when skills live under `skills/`**.
220	  `npx skills add owner/repo` looks at `.agents/skills/` in that repo;
221	  `npx skills add owner/repo/skills` looks at `skills/`. Most third-party skill
222	  repos use the latter layout.
223	- **`-a` does NOT take comma-separated values**. Repeat the flag:
224	  `-a claude-code -a opencode -a cursor`.
225	- **Agent names are normalised** (`claude-code` not `claude`,
226	  `gemini-cli` not `gemini`, `copilot` not `github-copilot`). Run
227	  `npx skills add --list` (or trigger the validation error) to see the
228	  canonical list.
229	
230	### Per-agent env var overrides
231	
232	Agents that respect a custom config dir change where the symlink/skill is
233	read from:
234	
235	| Env var | Default | Effect |
236	|---|---|---|
237	| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | `~/.claude` | Skills CLI writes symlinks here instead |
238	| `CODEX_HOME` | `~/.codex` | Codex picks up skills from here (Codex is universal, so the global install relies on `~/.agents/skills/` regardless) |
239	| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | `~/.config` | Affects Cursor/OpenCode/Gemini-CLI lookup paths |
240	
241	If you set any of these and re-run `npx skills add -g`, the CLI writes to the
242	new location; chezmoi's lock-file management still uses
243	`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` (the lock is location-independent).
244	
245	## Anti-patterns
246	
247	- **Don't put skill source files (`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`,
248	  templates, etc.) in chezmoi source.** They're owned by the npx skills CLI;
249	  chezmoi managing them creates a constant fight with the CLI's
250	  `skillFolderHash`. Only the **lock file** is chezmoi-managed.
251	- **Don't run `chezmoi re-add ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`** to capture local
252	  changes. Edit the merger's `$managed` block instead — that's the
253	  source-of-truth list. `re-add` would freeze a snapshot of one machine's
254	  state into the source, defeating the merger's per-machine preservation.
255	- **Don't commit `./.agents/skills/`**. They're skill source clones that the
256	  npx CLI rewrites on every `update`; tracking them creates noisy diffs and
257	  accidental conflicts with upstream skill updates.
258	- **Don't add `-g` to `bootstrap-skills`**. That recipe is project-scope by
259	  design; global is owned by `chezmoi apply`.
260	
261	## References
262	
263	- Live `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` — merger source of truth
264	- Live `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` — restore loop
265	- [`vercel-labs/skills` README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) — CLI docs
266	- [Issue #283 — `skills install -g`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283)
267	- [Issue #549 — global lock restore](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)
268	- [`docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`](agent-overlays.md) — sibling pattern for
269	  Claude/Cursor/OpenCode `settings.json` overlays (also `modify_` based)
270
```

36	import os, re, sys, glob, pathlib, tempfile

38	ROOT = pathlib.Path(os.environ.get("SSH_CFG_ROOT") or os.path.expanduser("~/.ssh/config"))
39	SSH_DIR = ROOT.parent

41

43	BREAK_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)^\s*(host|match)\b")
44	IDF_RE   = re.compile(r"(?i)^(\s*)identityfile\s+(.+?)\s*$")

53	    return pat

56	def resolve_includes(start):
57	    seen, files = set(), []
58	
59	    def walk(path):
60	        rp = os.path.realpath(path)
61	        if rp in seen:
62	            return
63	        seen.add(rp)
64	        p = pathlib.Path(path)
65	        if not p.is_file():
66	            return
67	        files.append(p)
68	        for line in p.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():

73	            if not m:

93	    pats = host_patterns(line)
94	    if not pats:
95	        return False
96	    return any(p == alias and not re.search(r"[*?!]", p) for p in pats)

102	        i = 0

121	def write_atomic(f, lines):
122	    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(f.parent))
123	    try:
124	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as fh:
125	            fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
126	        os.replace(tmp, str(f))
127	        os.chmod(str(f), 0o600)
128	    except BaseException:
129	        try:
130	            os.unlink(tmp)
131	        except OSError:
132	            pass
133	        raise
134	
135	
136	def configd_reachable():
137	    target = os.path.realpath(str(SSH_DIR / "config.d"))
138	    for f in resolve_includes(ROOT):
139	        for line in f.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
140	            s = line.strip()
141	            if not s or s.startswith("#"):
142	                continue
143	            m = INC_RE.match(line)
144	            if not m:
145	                continue
146	            for pat in m.group(1).split():
147	                if os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(expand(pat))) == target:
148	                    return True
149	    return False
150	
151	
152	def cmd_find(alias, keypath):
153	    res = find_block(alias, resolve_includes(ROOT))
154	    if not res:
155	        print("found=0")
156	        return 3
157	    f, lines, i, j = res
158	    block = lines[i:j]
159	    idf = [m for m in (IDF_RE.match(b) for b in block) if m]
160	    keyn = norm(keypath) if keypath else ""
161	    present = bool(keyn) and any(norm(m.group(2)) == keyn for m in idf)
162	    print("found=1")
163	    print("file=%s" % f)
164	    print("has_identityfile=%d" % (1 if idf else 0))
165	    print("has_identitiesonly=%d" % (1 if any(IDO_RE.match(b) for b in block) else 0))
166	    print("key_present=%d" % (1 if present else 0))
167	    print("---BLOCK---")
168	    sys.stdout.write("\n".join(block) + "\n")
169	    return 0
170	
171	
172	def cmd_insert(file, alias, keypath, action, identities_only):
173	    f = pathlib.Path(file)
174	    lines = f.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
175	    res = find_block(alias, [f])
176	    if not res:
177	        sys.stderr.write("block for %s not found in %s\n" % (alias, file))
178	        return 2
179	    _, _, i, j = res
180	    block = lines[i:j]
181	
182	    indent = "    "
183	    for b in block[1:]:
184	        if b.strip() and b[0] in " \t":
185	            indent = b[: len(b) - len(b.lstrip())]
186	            break
187	
188	    idf_line = "%sIdentityFile %s" % (indent, tildify(keypath))
189	    idf_idx = [k for k, b in enumerate(block) if IDF_RE.match(b)]
190	
191	    if action == "replace" and idf_idx:
192	        block[idf_idx[0]] = idf_line
193	    elif action == "add" or not idf_idx:
194	        ins = len(block)
195	        while ins > 1 and not block[ins - 1].strip():
196	            ins -= 1
197	        block.insert(ins, idf_line)
198	    else:  # action == insert but an IdentityFile already exists -> replace first
199	        block[idf_idx[0]] = idf_line
200	
201	    if identities_only and not any(IDO_RE.match(b) for b in block):
202	        pos = next((k for k, b in enumerate(block) if IDF_RE.match(b)), len(block) - 1)
203	        block.insert(pos + 1, "%sIdentitiesOnly yes" % indent)
204	
205	    write_atomic(f, lines[:i] + block + lines[j:])
206	    return 0
207	
208	
209	def cmd_add_include():
210	    if configd_reachable():
211	        return 0
212	    target = tildify(str(SSH_DIR / "config.d"))
213	    inc = ["# Load drop-in host configs from %s/" % target, "Include %s/*" % target, ""]
214	    lines = ROOT.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines() if ROOT.is_file() else []
215	    k = 0
216	    while k < len(lines) and (not lines[k].strip() or lines[k].lstrip().startswith("#")):
217	        k += 1
218	    ROOT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
219	    write_atomic(ROOT, lines[:k] + inc + lines[k:])
220	    return 0
221	
222	
223	def main(argv):
224	    if not argv:
225	        return 2
226	    cmd, rest = argv[0], argv[1:]
227	    if cmd == "find":
228	        return cmd_find(rest[0], rest[1] if len(rest) > 1 else "")
229	    if cmd == "insert":
230	        return cmd_insert(rest[0], rest[1], rest[2], rest[3], "--identities-only" in rest[4:])
231	    if cmd == "ensure-include":
232	        return 0 if configd_reachable() else 1
233	    if cmd == "add-include":
234	        return cmd_add_include()
235	    sys.stderr.write("unknown subcommand: %s\n" % cmd)
236	    return 2
237	
238	
239	sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
240	PY
241	}

243	ssh-setup-remote() {
244	  if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
245	    emulate -L zsh
246	    setopt localoptions pipefail
247	  else
248	    set -o pipefail
249	  fi
250	
251	  local usage="Usage: ssh-setup-remote [user@]host"
252	  if [ $# -ne 1 ]; then
253	    printf '%s\n' "$usage" >&2
254	    return 1
255	  fi
256	
257	  local target="$1"
258	  local remote_user remote_host
259	  if [[ "$target" == *@* ]]; then
260	    remote_user="${target%%@*}"
261	    remote_host="${target#*@}"
262	  else
263	    remote_host="$target"
264	    remote_user=""
265	  fi
266	
267	  # ── Step 0: Key selection ──────────────────────────────────────────────
268	  printf '\n%s\n' "=== SSH Key Setup for $target ==="
269	
270	  local key_path=""
271	  local create_new=""
272	
273	  printf '\nExisting keys in ~/.ssh/:\n'
274	
275	  # Portable nullglob: in zsh, `*.pub(N)` made the glob expand to nothing
276	  # when nothing matched. shopt -s nullglob (bash) / setopt nullglob (zsh)
277	  # is the equivalent.

279	  existing_keys=()
280	  if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
281	    setopt localoptions nullglob

284	    shopt -s nullglob

287	  local f

289	    existing_keys+=("${f%.pub}")
290	    printf '  %s\n' "${f%.pub}"
291	  done

293	  # Restore bash nullglob; zsh is already locally scoped via setopt localoptions.
294	  if [ -n "$BASH_VERSION" ]; then
295	    eval "$_had_nullglob"
296	  fi

298	  if (( ${#existing_keys[@]} > 0 )); then
299	    printf '\nUse an existing key? [Y/n] '
300	    read -r create_new
301	    if [[ "$create_new" =~ ^[Nn] ]]; then

303	    else

306	      # Expand ~ manually

309	        printf '%s\n' "Key not found: $key_path" >&2

311	      fi
312	    fi
313	  else

322	    # Algorithm

327	    [ -n "$algo_input" ] && algo="$algo_input"

329	    # Key name

337	    if [ -f "$key_path" ]; then

341	
342	    # Comment

9	Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*

11	Host *
12	    # Conservative cross-platform keepalive defaults.
13	    ServerAliveInterval 60
14	    ServerAliveCountMax 3
15	
16	    # Connection multiplexing — reuse one TCP + auth handshake for every
17	    # subsequent session to the same (host, port, user). The win scales with
18	    # round-trip time and with how many short-lived SSH sessions a workflow
19	    # opens: `fleet` fan-out, git over ssh, rsync loops, and any mobile /
20	    # tethered / cross-continent link.
21	    #
22	    # ControlPath uses %C (a hash of host+port+user+local host) so no socket
23	    # directory has to exist — sockets land as ~/.ssh/cm-<hash>. That also
24	    # keeps the path short, which matters: a unix socket path over ~104 bytes
25	    # is rejected on macOS.
26	    #
27	    # Gotchas worth knowing before debugging something weird:
28	    # - Forwarding options (-A, -L, -R, -X) are taken from the FIRST connection
29	    #   that opened the master. A later `ssh -L …` to the same host silently
30	    #   rides the existing master without the forward. Use `-o ControlMaster=no`
31	    #   for that one-off, or drop the master first.
32	    # - `ssh -O check <host>` asks whether a master is live; `ssh -O exit <host>`
33	    #   tears it down. Killing the master drops every session sharing it.
34	    # - To opt a host out, set `ControlMaster no` in a ~/.ssh/config.d/ file:
35	    #   `Include` is the first directive in this file and ssh takes the
36	    #   first-obtained value for each keyword, so config.d always wins.
37	    #
38	    # Not set: Compression. It costs CPU and only pays off on genuinely slow
39	    # links; SSH's own default (off) is right for the common case.
40	    ControlMaster auto
41	    ControlPath ~/.ssh/cm-%C
42	    ControlPersist 10m

1	# ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — fleet_apply.py host inventory
2	#
3	# Seeded ONCE by chezmoi (`create_` prefix) so your edits are never overwritten.
4	# To reset to this template: `rm ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml && chezmoi apply`.
5	# File mode is 0600 (chezmoi `private_` prefix) — safe for plaintext passwords,
6	# but Bitwarden / interactive prompt sources are still preferred.
7	#
8	# IMPORTANT: `password_source` is for the REMOTE `sudo` password ONLY (fed to
9	# chezmoi via CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE for `run_*` scripts). It does NOT
10	# authenticate the SSH login itself — fleet always tries key/agent auth
11	# FIRST for SSH login. If `ssh <host>` prompts you for a password, the host
12	# will show as `unreachable` in `just fleet-status`. Fix with `ssh-copy-id`
13	# where possible. If the remote flatly disallows pubkey auth (e.g. corporate/
14	# IDC sshd with `PubkeyAuthentication no`), set the separate, opt-in
15	# `ssh_login_password_source` field (example 6 below) — independent of
16	# `password_source`, since a host's SSH login password may differ from its
17	# sudo password. See `pitfalls/fleet-apply-password-source-not-for-ssh-login.md`
18	# for context.
19	#
20	# Schema reference: docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md
21	# Run: `just fleet-apply` (parallel) | `just fleet-apply-dry-run` (chezmoi diff)
22	
23	[defaults]
24	chezmoi_path    = "auto"           # "auto" → augment remote PATH with common install dirs
25	                                   # (~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin,
26	                                   #  /usr/local/bin, /snap/bin) before invoking `chezmoi`.
27	                                   # Override per-host with an absolute path (e.g.
28	                                   # "/snap/bin/chezmoi") to pin a specific binary.
29	connect_timeout = 15
30	command_timeout = 1800
31	
32	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
33	# Default: apply to THIS machine (local execution, no SSH).
34	# Seeded once on `chezmoi apply`; edit freely — chezmoi won't overwrite.
35	# `no_root_machine` mirrors the chezmoi `.noRoot` prompt from
36	# .chezmoi.toml.tmpl so this entry stays consistent with how the rest of
37	# the dotfiles were initialised on this host.
38	# `password_source` is intentionally omitted: for `local = true` hosts
39	# fleet_apply.py skips its password gate (chezmoi inherits the parent
40	# terminal's TTY and prompts for sudo there if needed).
41	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
42	[[hosts]]
43	name            = "self"
44	local           = true
45	no_root_machine = {{ .noRoot }}
46	
47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
48	# Templates for adding REMOTE hosts — uncomment and edit as needed.
49	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
50	
51	# 1) Preferred: ssh_config alias. Inherits ProxyJump, IdentityAgent (e.g.
52	#    1Password SSH agent), Match blocks — everything you'd get from `ssh lab-box`.
53	# [[hosts]]
54	# name            = "lab-box"
55	# ssh_alias       = "lab-box"
56	# no_root_machine = false                                   # remote was init'd with noRoot=false
57	# password_source = { type = "bitwarden", item = "ssh-lab-box-sudo" }
58	
59	# 2) Explicit connection (no ssh_config entry).
60	# [[hosts]]
61	# name            = "vps-tokyo"
62	# hostname        = "203.0.113.42"
63	# user            = "dwlee"
64	# port            = 22
65	# identity_file   = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
66	# no_root_machine = true                                    # remote was init'd with noRoot=true
67	# # password_source omitted → no sudo phase; chezmoi runs as the SSH user only.
68	
69	# 3) Interactive prompt (asked once at startup, never persisted).
70	# [[hosts]]
71	# name            = "office-mac"
72	# ssh_alias       = "office-mac"
73	# no_root_machine = false
74	# password_source = { type = "prompt" }
75	
76	# 4) Plaintext password (last resort — relies on file mode 0600).
77	# [[hosts]]
78	# name            = "throwaway-vm"
79	# ssh_alias       = "throwaway-vm"
80	# no_root_machine = false
81	# password_source = { type = "plain", value = "hunter2" }
82	
83	# 5) Local execution (this machine, no SSH). Useful when you want
84	#    `just fleet-apply` to keep the orchestrator itself in sync along
85	#    with the SSH hosts. ssh_alias / hostname / user / port /
86	#    identity_file are ignored. Sudo is inherited from the parent
87	#    terminal (chezmoi may prompt for password if it needs root).
88	# [[hosts]]
89	# name            = "self"
90	# local           = true
91	# no_root_machine = true                                    # set false if your local apply needs sudo
92	
93	# 6) SSH LOGIN itself is password-only (e.g. IDC/corporate sshd with
94	#    `PubkeyAuthentication no` — real trigger: `zyc_friend`, an IDC server
95	#    whose sshd only offers `keyboard-interactive`/PAM, so even

98	#    `ssh_login_password_source` is INDEPENDENT of `password_source` (that

101	#    tries key/agent auth first; only falls back to password/
102	#    keyboard-interactive (PAM) auth if that's flatly rejected.

16	"""fleet hosts — pick a fleet-configured host, SSH into it.
17	
18	Three entry points:
19	
20	  fleet hosts                 Interactive picker via `tv fleet-hosts`. Falls
21	                              back to a numbered-stdin menu if `tv` is not on
22	                              PATH (e.g. headless CI).
23	  fleet hosts NAME            SSH directly into NAME (skip the picker). Uses
24	                              ssh_alias if set; otherwise constructs
25	                              `ssh -p PORT -i KEY user@hostname`. Lands in an
26	                              attach-or-create tmux session (`--no-tmux` opts
27	                              out, `--tmux-session NAME` renames it).
28	  fleet hosts --list*         Script-friendly inventory dumps — also used by
29	                              the TV cable + your own shell glue:
30	                                --list        plain names, one per line
31	                                --list-tsv    name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
32	                                --list-json   full inventory JSON
33	                                --describe N  preview block for N
34	                                --probe N     BatchMode SSH probe of N
35	
36	Mirrors `dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml` (which is sourced from
37	~/.ssh/config), but reads ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml instead so explicit
38	hostname/user/port/identity_file hosts (no ssh_config alias) are reachable.
39	
40	The TV cable at `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` shells out to
41	`fleet hosts --list-tsv` (source), `fleet hosts --describe '{...}'` (preview),
42	and `fleet hosts '{...}'` (Enter action). This module is the SSOT for fleet
43	inventory introspection — the only TOML parser is `load_hosts()` in apply.py.
44	
45	`local = true` hosts are hidden from `--list-tsv` (picker) by default — SSH'ing
46	into yourself is silly. Use `--include-local` to override, or run
47	`fleet hosts NAME` on a local host (prints a no-op message and exits 0).
48	"""
49	from __future__ import annotations
50	
51	import argparse
52	import dataclasses
53	import json
54	import os
55	import shlex
56	import shutil
57	import subprocess
58	import sys
59	from pathlib import Path

61	# Bootstrap: when invoked directly (not via the `fleet hosts` dispatcher in
62	# dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet), put the chezmoi source dir on sys.path
63	# so `from scripts.fleet import ...` works regardless of cwd.
64	_SRC = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent  # hosts.py -> fleet -> scripts -> src
65	if str(_SRC) not in sys.path:

70	
71	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
72	# Host introspection helpers
73	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
74	
75	
76	def _kind(host: Host) -> str:
77	    """Compact connection-style summary for the picker's 3rd column."""
78	    if host.local:
79	        return "LOCAL"
80	    if host.ssh_alias:
81	        return f"alias:{host.ssh_alias}"
82	    parts: list[str] = []
83	    if host.user:
84	        parts.append(f"{host.user}@")
85	    parts.append(host.hostname or "?")
86	    if host.port and host.port != 22:
87	        parts.append(f":{host.port}")
88	    return "explicit:" + "".join(parts)
89	
90	
91	def _target(host: Host) -> str:
92	    """Resolved SSH target for the picker's 2nd column."""
93	    if host.local:
94	        return "(local)"
95	    if host.ssh_alias:
96	        return host.ssh_alias
97	    return host.hostname or "?"

100	def _ssh_argv(host: Host, remote_cmd: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
101	    """argv for `ssh ...`. Mirrors apply.py:_connect_kwargs precedence —
102	    ssh_alias wins (let ssh_config resolve everything); otherwise build from
103	    hostname/user/port/identity_file.
104	
105	    When `remote_cmd` is given it is appended as the remote command and `-t` is
106	    added to force a TTY (ssh does not allocate one when a command is present,
107	    and tmux needs one)."""
108	    argv: list[str] = ["ssh"]
109	    if remote_cmd is not None:
110	        argv.append("-t")
111	    if host.ssh_alias:
112	        argv.append(host.ssh_alias)
113	    else:
114	        if host.port:
