116	        if host.identity_file:
117	            argv += ["-i", str(Path(host.identity_file).expanduser())]
118	        argv.append(f"{host.user}@{host.hostname}" if host.user else (host.hostname or ""))
119	    if remote_cmd is not None:
120	        argv.append(remote_cmd)
121	    return argv
122	
123	
124	_DEFAULT_TMUX_SESSION = "fleet"
125	
126	
127	def _tmux_remote_cmd(session: str) -> str:
128	    """Remote command that attaches to `session` or creates it, degrading to a
129	    login shell on hosts without tmux.
130	
131	    `tmux new -A -s NAME` is attach-if-exists / create-otherwise (tmux >= 1.8),
132	    which is the whole point: a dropped mobile connection reconnects into the
133	    same session instead of losing the work. `exec` replaces the wrapper shell
134	    so the SSH session ends when tmux does.
135	    """
136	    quoted = shlex.quote(session)
137	    return (
138	        f"command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec tmux new -A -s {quoted} "
139	        '|| exec "${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -l'
140	    )
141	
142	
143	def _load(config: Path) -> list[Host]:
144	    try:
145	        hosts, _defaults = load_hosts(config)
146	    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError) as e:
147	        print(f"fleet hosts: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
148	        sys.exit(2)
149	    return hosts
150	
151	
152	def _find_host(name: str, hosts: list[Host]) -> Host:
153	    for h in hosts:
154	        if h.name == name:
155	            return h
156	    available = ", ".join(h.name for h in hosts) or "(none)"
157	    print(
158	        f"fleet hosts: unknown host {name!r}. Available: {available}",
159	        file=sys.stderr,
160	    )
161	    sys.exit(2)
162	
163	
164	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
165	# Listing modes
166	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
167	
168	
169	def _cmd_list_plain(hosts: list[Host]) -> int:
170	    for h in hosts:
171	        print(h.name)
172	    return 0
173	
174	
175	def _cmd_list_tsv(hosts: list[Host], include_local: bool) -> int:
176	    for h in hosts:
177	        if h.local and not include_local:
178	            continue
179	        print(f"{h.name}\t{_target(h)}\t{_kind(h)}")
180	    return 0
181	
182	
183	def _cmd_list_json(hosts: list[Host], config: Path) -> int:
184	    payload = []
185	    for h in hosts:
186	        d = dataclasses.asdict(h)
187	        # Never leak a resolved sudo_password / ssh_login_password (they'd
188	        # be None at this point — resolve_passwords()/
189	        # resolve_ssh_login_passwords() never ran — but be defensive in
190	        # case that changes).
191	        d.pop("sudo_password", None)
192	        d.pop("ssh_login_password", None)
193	        # For plain-type password sources, the TOML file itself is 0600 but
194	        # JSON dump goes to stdout (could be piped into logs/screenshots).
195	        if d.get("password_source_type") == "plain":
196	            d["password_source_arg"] = "(redacted — type=plain)"
197	        if d.get("ssh_login_password_source_type") == "plain":
198	            d["ssh_login_password_source_arg"] = "(redacted — type=plain)"
199	        payload.append(d)
200	    json.dump(
201	        {"config": str(config), "hosts": payload},
202	        sys.stdout,
203	        indent=2,
204	        default=str,
205	    )
206	    sys.stdout.write("\n")
207	    return 0
208	
209	
210	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
211	# Describe (TV preview pane)
212	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
213	
214	
215	def _ssh_g_lines(alias: str, wanted: tuple[str, ...]) -> list[str]:
216	    """Run `ssh -G ALIAS` and return matching `key value` lines."""
217	    if not shutil.which("ssh"):
218	        return []
219	    try:
220	        out = subprocess.run(
221	            ["ssh", "-G", alias],
222	            capture_output=True,
223	            text=True,
224	            timeout=3,
225	            check=False,
226	        )
227	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
228	        return []
229	    if out.returncode != 0:
230	        return []
231	    matched: list[str] = []
232	    for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
233	        parts = line.split(None, 1)
234	        if len(parts) == 2 and parts[0] in wanted:
235	            matched.append(line)
236	    return matched
237	
238	
239	def _identity_paths_from_ssh_g(alias: str) -> list[str]:
240	    out: list[str] = []
241	    for line in _ssh_g_lines(alias, ("identityfile",)):
242	        parts = line.split(None, 1)
243	        if len(parts) == 2:
244	            out.append(parts[1])
245	    return out
246	
247	
248	def _expand_key_path(p: str) -> Path:
249	    return Path(p.replace("~", str(Path.home()))).expanduser()
250	
251	
252	def _cmd_describe(name: str, hosts: list[Host], config: Path) -> int:
253	    h = _find_host(name, hosts)
254	
255	    print(f"# host: {h.name}        (defined in: {config})")
256	    print()
257	
258	    print("connection:")
259	    if h.local:
260	        print("  local           true   (runs on orchestrator — no SSH)")
261	    elif h.ssh_alias:
262	        print(f"  ssh_alias       {h.ssh_alias}")
263	        print(f"  user            {h.user or '(from ssh_config)'}")
264	        print(f"  hostname        {h.hostname or '(from ssh_config)'}")
265	        print(f"  port            {h.port if h.port is not None else '(from ssh_config)'}")
266	        print(f"  identity_file   {h.identity_file or '(from ssh_config)'}")
267	    else:
268	        print("  ssh_alias       (none — explicit fields below)")
269	        print(f"  user            {h.user or '(default)'}")
270	        print(f"  hostname        {h.hostname}")
271	        print(f"  port            {h.port if h.port is not None else 22}")
272	        print(f"  identity_file   {h.identity_file or '(default agent / key)'}")
273	    print()
274	
275	    print("fleet metadata:")
276	    print(f"  local                {str(h.local).lower()}")
277	    print(f"  no_root_machine      {str(h.no_root_machine).lower()}")
278	    print(f"  chezmoi_path         {h.chezmoi_path}")
279	    ps_label = h.password_source_type
280	    if h.password_source_arg and h.password_source_type != "plain":
281	        ps_label += f" (item={h.password_source_arg})"
282	    elif h.password_source_type == "plain":
283	        ps_label += " (value redacted)"
284	    print(f"  password_source      {ps_label}")
285	    ssh_ps_label = h.ssh_login_password_source_type
286	    if h.ssh_login_password_source_arg and h.ssh_login_password_source_type != "plain":
287	        ssh_ps_label += f" (item={h.ssh_login_password_source_arg})"
288	    elif h.ssh_login_password_source_type == "plain":
289	        ssh_ps_label += " (value redacted)"
290	    print(f"  ssh_login_password_source  {ssh_ps_label}")
291	    if h.extra_env:
292	        print(f"  extra_env            {', '.join(h.extra_env.keys())}")
293	    else:
294	        print("  extra_env            (none)")
295	    print()
296	
297	    if h.ssh_alias:
298	        print(f"ssh -G {h.ssh_alias!r} (resolved by ssh_config):")
299	        wanted = (
300	            "hostname", "user", "port", "identityfile",
301	            "proxycommand", "proxyjump", "forwardagent", "identityagent",
302	        )
303	        lines = _ssh_g_lines(h.ssh_alias, wanted)
304	        if not lines:
305	            print("  (ssh -G unavailable or returned nothing)")
306	        else:
307	            for line in lines:
308	                print(f"  {line}")
309	        print()
310	
311	    if not h.local:
312	        print("local key check (offline):")
313	        paths: list[str] = []
314	        if h.identity_file:
315	            paths.append(h.identity_file)
316	        elif h.ssh_alias:
317	            paths = _identity_paths_from_ssh_g(h.ssh_alias)
318	        if not paths:
319	            print("  (no identityfile to check)")
320	        else:
321	            found = False
322	            for p in paths:
323	                f = _expand_key_path(p)
324	                if f.is_file():
325	                    print(f"  [OK]   {f}")
326	                    found = True
327	                else:
328	                    print(f"  [miss] {f}")
329	            if not found:
330	                print()
331	                print(
332	                    "  => no IdentityFile present locally —"
333	                    " password / agent login required"
334	                )
335	        print()
336	
337	    return 0
338	
339	
340	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
341	# Probe (TV Alt+T action)
342	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
343	
344	
345	def _cmd_probe(name: str, hosts: list[Host]) -> int:
346	    h = _find_host(name, hosts)
347	    if h.local:
348	        print(f"# {h.name} is local=true — no SSH probe needed.")
349	        return 0
350	    target = h.ssh_alias or h.hostname or "?"
351	    print(f"# Probing {target!r} with BatchMode=yes (ConnectTimeout=3)")
352	    print(
353	        "# Exit 0 = passwordless login works; non-zero = needs password /"
354	        " key not authorized / unreachable"
355	    )
356	    print()
357	
358	    argv = _ssh_argv(h)
359	    argv = [
360	        argv[0],
361	        "-o", "BatchMode=yes",
362	        "-o", "ConnectTimeout=3",
363	        "-o", "StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new",
364	        "-o", "PreferredAuthentications=publickey,hostbased,gssapi-with-mic",
365	        *argv[1:],
366	        "true",
367	    ]
368	    rc = subprocess.call(argv)
369	    print()
370	    if rc == 0:
371	        print(f"[OK] passwordless login works for {target!r}")
372	    elif rc == 255:
373	        print("[FAIL] connection / auth error (exit 255) — needs password,"
374	              " key not authorized, or host unreachable")
375	    else:
376	        print(f"[FAIL] remote command failed (exit {rc}) — auth probably OK"
377	              " but 'true' failed")
378	    return rc
379	
380	
381	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
382	# Direct SSH (positional NAME)
383	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
384	
385	
386	def _cmd_connect(name: str, hosts: list[Host], tmux_session: str | None) -> int:
387	    h = _find_host(name, hosts)
388	    if h.local:
389	        print(
390	            f"fleet hosts: '{h.name}' is local = true — nothing to SSH into "
391	            "(you're already on the orchestrator).",
392	            file=sys.stderr,
393	        )
394	        return 0
395	    remote_cmd = _tmux_remote_cmd(tmux_session) if tmux_session else None
396	    argv = _ssh_argv(h, remote_cmd)
397	    # os.execvp replaces this process with ssh, so the user's terminal
398	    # becomes the SSH session directly — matches Enter in `tv ssh-config`.
399	    try:
400	        os.execvp(argv[0], argv)
401	    except OSError as e:
402	        print(f"fleet hosts: failed to exec {argv[0]}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
403	        return 127
404	    return 0  # unreachable
405	
406	
407	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
408	# Picker (no args)
409	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
410	
411	
412	def _cmd_picker(hosts: list[Host], tmux_session: str | None) -> int:
413	    tv = shutil.which("tv")
414	    if tv:
415	        try:
416	            os.execvp(tv, [tv, "fleet-hosts"])
417	        except OSError as e:
418	            print(f"fleet hosts: failed to exec tv: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
419	            # fall through to text menu
420	
421	    pickable = [h for h in hosts if not h.local]
422	    if not pickable:
423	        print(
424	            "fleet hosts: no SSH-able hosts in inventory (all `local = true`).",
425	            file=sys.stderr,
426	        )
427	        return 2
428	    print("Fleet hosts (pick one to SSH into):")
429	    for i, h in enumerate(pickable, 1):
430	        print(f"  {i:>2}. {h.name:<24}  {_kind(h)}")
431	    print()
432	    try:
433	        choice = input("Number (or empty to abort): ").strip()
434	    except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
435	        print()
436	        return 130
437	    if not choice:
438	        return 0
439	    try:
440	        idx = int(choice) - 1
441	        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(pickable):
442	            raise ValueError
443	    except ValueError:
444	        print(f"fleet hosts: invalid choice {choice!r}", file=sys.stderr)
445	        return 2
446	    return _cmd_connect(pickable[idx].name, hosts, tmux_session)
447	
448	
449	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
450	# CLI
451	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
452	
453	
454	def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
455	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
456	        prog="fleet hosts",
457	        description=(
458	            "Pick a fleet-configured host and SSH in. Mirrors `tv ssh-config`,"
459	            " but sourced from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml."
460	        ),
461	    )
462	    p.add_argument(
463	        "name",
464	        nargs="?",
465	        help="Host name to SSH into (skip the picker). Use `--list` to enumerate.",
466	    )
467	    modes = p.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
468	    modes.add_argument(
469	        "--list",
470	        action="store_true",
471	        help="Plain host names, one per line.",
472	    )
473	    modes.add_argument(
474	        "--list-tsv",
475	        action="store_true",
476	        dest="list_tsv",
477	        help="TSV `name<TAB>target<TAB>kind` (used by the TV cable source).",
478	    )
479	    modes.add_argument(
480	        "--list-json",
481	        action="store_true",
482	        dest="list_json",
483	        help="Full inventory as JSON (plain password values are redacted).",
484	    )
485	    modes.add_argument(
486	        "--describe",
487	        metavar="NAME",
488	        help="Print the preview block for NAME (used by the TV cable preview).",
489	    )
490	    modes.add_argument(
491	        "--probe",
492	        metavar="NAME",
493	        help="BatchMode SSH probe of NAME (used by the TV cable Alt+T action).",
494	    )
495	    p.add_argument(
496	        "--include-local",
497	        action="store_true",
498	        help="Include `local = true` hosts in --list-tsv (default: hidden).",
499	    )
500	    p.add_argument(
501	        "--no-tmux",
502	        action="store_true",
503	        dest="no_tmux",
504	        help="Land in a plain login shell instead of attaching to tmux.",
505	    )
506	    p.add_argument(
507	        "--tmux-session",
508	        metavar="NAME",
509	        dest="tmux_session",
510	        default=_DEFAULT_TMUX_SESSION,
511	        help=(
512	            "Remote tmux session to attach-or-create "
513	            f"(default: {_DEFAULT_TMUX_SESSION!r}). Ignored with --no-tmux."
514	        ),
515	    )
516	    p.add_argument(
517	        "--config",
518	        type=Path,
519	        default=DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH,
520	        help=f"Fleet inventory path (default: {DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH}).",
521	    )
522	    return p
523	
524	
525	def main() -> int:
526	    args = _build_parser().parse_args()
527	    hosts = _load(args.config)
528	
529	    if args.list:
530	        return _cmd_list_plain(hosts)
531	    if args.list_tsv:
532	        return _cmd_list_tsv(hosts, include_local=args.include_local)
533	    if args.list_json:
534	        return _cmd_list_json(hosts, args.config)
535	    if args.describe:
536	        return _cmd_describe(args.describe, hosts, args.config)
537	    if args.probe:
538	        return _cmd_probe(args.probe, hosts)
539	    tmux_session = None if args.no_tmux else args.tmux_session
540	    if args.name:
541	        return _cmd_connect(args.name, hosts, tmux_session)
542	    return _cmd_picker(hosts, tmux_session)
543	
544	
545	if __name__ == "__main__":
546	    sys.exit(main())
547

1	# Custom fleet-hosts channel for television (tv).
2	# Sourced from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — the same inventory used by
3	# `fleet chezmoi apply` / `fleet tmux` / `fleet info` / `fleet pueue` /
4	# `fleet exec`. Mirrors the `ssh-config` cable's UX but reads fleet's TOML
5	# inventory instead of ~/.ssh/config, so hosts with explicit
6	# hostname/user/port/identity_file (no ssh_alias) are reachable too.
7	#
8	# The actual TOML parsing lives in Python — this cable shells out to:
9	#   fleet hosts --list-tsv      (source — `name<TAB>target<TAB>kind` lines)
10	#   fleet hosts --describe N    (preview pane content)
11	#   fleet hosts N               (Enter action — os.execvp("ssh", ...))
12	# So this file stays small and the picker tracks any inventory changes
13	# automatically (no parallel TOML parser to keep in sync).
14	#
15	# Enter lands you in an attach-or-create tmux session (`fleet`) on the remote,
16	# so a dropped connection resumes instead of losing the shell. That lives in
17	# `fleet hosts` itself, NOT here — do not inline an `ssh` invocation into this
18	# cable or the two will drift. See docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md.
19	#
20	# Usage:
21	#   tv fleet-hosts
22	#   fleet hosts          # same picker via the fleet umbrella
23	#   fleet hosts lab-box  # skip the picker, SSH directly
24	#
25	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
26	#   Enter      SSH into the selected host
27	#   Alt+T      BatchMode SSH probe (does passwordless login actually work?)
28	#   Alt+S      fleet chezmoi status scoped to this host
29	#   Alt+I      fleet info scoped to this host
30	#   Alt+P      fleet pueue scoped to this host
31	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
32	#
33	# `local = true` hosts are intentionally hidden — they live on the
34	# orchestrator and have no SSH endpoint. Run `fleet hosts --list-tsv
35	# --include-local` to confirm one is in the inventory.
36	
37	[metadata]
38	name = "fleet-hosts"
39	description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
40	requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]
41	
42	[source]
43	command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"
44	# Lines look like:   name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
45	# e.g.   lab-box <TAB> lab-box <TAB> alias:lab-box
46	#        vps-tokyo <TAB> 203.0.113.42 <TAB> explicit:dwlee@203.0.113.42
47	display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
48	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
49	
50	[preview]
51	command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"
52	
53	[keybindings]
54	enter = "actions:connect"
55	alt-t = "actions:probe"
56	alt-s = "actions:status"
57	alt-i = "actions:info"
58	alt-p = "actions:pueue"
59	
60	[actions.connect]
61	description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
62	command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
63	mode = "execute"
64	
65	[actions.probe]
66	description = "BatchMode SSH probe (passwordless login check)"
67	command = "fleet hosts --probe '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
68	mode = "execute"

1	# Custom SSH config channel for television (tv)
2	# Parses Host entries from ~/.ssh/config AND ~/.ssh/config.d/* (Include support).
3	# The community ssh-hosts channel only reads ~/.ssh/config directly.
4	#
5	# Each entry shows which file the host is defined in, so duplicates across
6	# config.d/* are easy to spot. The output (what gets passed to ssh / actions)
7	# is just the bare hostname.
8	#
9	# Usage:
10	#   tv ssh-config
11	#
12	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
13	#   Enter      SSH into selected host
14	#   Alt+T      Online probe: BatchMode=yes test (does pubkey login actually work?)
15	#   Alt+A      Offline batch scan: list every host + whether a local key file exists
16	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
17	#
18	# Preview shows resolved config via `ssh -G` plus a local-key existence check
19	# (no network — just stat the IdentityFile paths).
20	
21	[metadata]
22	name = "ssh-config"
23	description = "SSH hosts (with Include config.d/* support)"
24	requirements = ["ssh", "awk", "sort"]
25	
26	[source]
27	# Emit "<source-file>\t<hostname>" so the picker shows the origin file but
28	# actions still receive a clean hostname via {split:\t:1}.
29	command = """
30	for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
31	  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
32	  rel=${f#$HOME/}
33	  awk -v src="$rel" '
34	    /^[[:space:]]*Host[[:space:]]/ {
35	      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
36	        if ($i !~ /[*?]/) printf "%s\\t%s\\n", src, $i
37	      }
38	    }' "$f"
39	done | sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2
40	"""
41	display = "{split:\\t:1}  ({split:\\t:0})"
42	output = "{split:\\t:1}"
43	
44	[preview]
45	command = """
46	host='{split:\\t:1}'
47	src='{split:\\t:0}'
48	echo "# defined in: $src"
49	echo
50	ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^(host|hostname|user|port|identityfile|proxycommand|proxyjump|forwardagent|identityagent|localforward|remoteforward)[[:space:]]'
51	echo
52	echo '--- local key check (offline) ---'
53	found=0
54	while IFS= read -r f; do
55	  [ -z "$f" ] && continue
56	  case "$f" in '~/'*) f="$HOME/${f#'~/'}";; '~') f="$HOME";; esac
57	  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
58	    echo "  [OK]   $f"
59	    found=1
60	  else
61	    echo "  [miss] $f"
62	  fi
63	done <<EOF
64	$(ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^identityfile / {print $2}')
65	EOF
66	if [ "$found" -eq 0 ]; then
67	  echo
68	  echo '  => no IdentityFile present locally — password login likely required'
69	  echo '     (or relies on ssh-agent / IdentityAgent — try Alt+T to probe)'
70	fi
71	"""
72	
73	[keybindings]
74	enter = "actions:connect"

78	[actions.connect]
79	description = "SSH into the selected host"
80	command = "ssh '{split:\\t:1}'"
81	mode = "execute"
82	
83	[actions.probe]
84	description = "Probe selected host with BatchMode (no password prompt allowed)"
85	command = """
86	host='{split:\\t:1}'
87	echo "# Probing $host with BatchMode=yes (ConnectTimeout=3)"
88	echo "# Exit 0 = passwordless login works; non-zero = needs password / unreachable / key not authorized"
89	echo
90	ssh -o BatchMode=yes \\
91	    -o ConnectTimeout=3 \\
92	    -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \\
93	    -o PreferredAuthentications=publickey,hostbased,gssapi-with-mic \\
94	    "$host" true
95	rc=$?
96	echo
97	case $rc in
98	  0)   echo "[OK] passwordless login works for '$host'" ;;
99	  255) echo "[FAIL] connection / auth error (exit 255) — needs password, key not authorized, or host unreachable" ;;
100	  *)   echo "[FAIL] remote command failed (exit $rc) — auth probably OK but 'true' failed" ;;
101	esac
102	echo
103	echo '[Press Enter to exit]'
104	read -r _
105	"""
106	mode = "execute"
107	
108	[actions.scan_all]
109	description = "Offline scan: for every host, check if any IdentityFile exists locally"
110	command = """
111	echo "# Scanning all hosts (offline — no network) ..."
112	echo "# Legend: [OK] = at least one IdentityFile present locally"
113	echo "#         [--] = no key file on disk (password / agent / unconfigured)"
114	echo
115	for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
116	  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
117	  rel=${f#$HOME/}
118	  awk -v src="$rel" '
119	    /^[[:space:]]*Host[[:space:]]/ {
120	      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
121	        if ($i !~ /[*?]/) printf "%s\\t%s\\n", src, $i
122	      }
123	    }' "$f"
124	done | sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2 | while IFS=$'\\t' read -r src host; do
125	  keyline=""
126	  found=0
127	  while IFS= read -r kf; do
128	    [ -z "$kf" ] && continue
129	    case "$kf" in '~/'*) kf="$HOME/${kf#'~/'}";; '~') kf="$HOME";; esac
130	    if [ -f "$kf" ]; then
131	      keyline="$kf"
132	      found=1
133	      break
134	    fi
135	  done <<EOF
136	$(ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^identityfile / {print $2}')
137	EOF
138	  if [ "$found" -eq 1 ]; then
139	    printf '  [OK] %-28s %-22s -> %s\\n' "$host" "($src)" "$keyline"
140	  else
141	    printf '  [--] %-28s %-22s    (no local key)\\n' "$host" "($src)"
142	  fi
143	done
144	echo
145	echo '[Press Enter to exit]'
146	read -r _
147	"""

Did you start the daemon yet?`, then after `brew services start pueue` (reports `Successfully started`) fails one step later `I/O error at path ".../Library/Application Support/pueue/pueue_<you>.socket" while connecting to daemon`; `ps` shows no `pueued`; `launchctl list homebrew.mxcl.pueue` = `"OnDemand" = true` + `"LastExitStatus" = 0` with NO `"PID"`; `~/.config/pueue/` doesn't exist (red herring — macOS uses `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/`); daemon runs fine by hand (`pueued -d`) | not a bug — Homebrew formula ships `keep_alive false` + RunAtLoad-only, launchd doesn't execute pueued after a `brew services` toggle that coincides with an upgrade/relink; workaround = `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/homebrew.mxcl.pueue` |
pitfalls/README.md-182-| [`raycast-clipboard-sqlcipher-key-not-recoverable`](raycast-clipboard-sqlcipher-key-not-recoverable.md) | Want to read Raycast clipboard history programmatically; `~/Library/Application Support/com.raycast.macos/raycast-enc.sqlite` is SQLCipher (binary contains `cipher_*` PRAGMAs); `security find-generic-password -s Raycast -a database_key -w` returns 64-hex; that key fails `Parse error: file is not a database (26)` for every `cipher_compatibility` / page_size / raw-vs-KDF combo on every `*-enc.sqlite` file; older plaintext `Clipboard.sqlite` schema (`ZCLIPBOARDHISTORYITEM`) no longer exists | UNSOLVED without RE'ing AppDelegate; workaround = switch to Maccy (open SQLite at `~/Library/Containers/org.p0deje.Maccy/`) |
pitfalls/README.md:183:| [`tailscale-another-copy-app-store-leftover`](tailscale-another-copy-app-store-leftover.md) | Tailscale debug → `Another Tailscale copy was found on this Mac.` / `/Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app` / `onlyOneCopyExplainer` + `DNS Unavailable` `Code: dns-forward-failing`; `mdfind Tailscale.app` returns two paths (`io.tailscale.ipn.macsys` cask vs `io.tailscale.ipn.macos` App Store leftover); plus `brew upgrade` fights over `/usr/local/bin/tailscale` between the `tailscale` formula and the `tailscale-app` cask wrapper | fixed (`sudo rm -rf /Applications/Tailscale.localized` + `brew uninstall tailscale`; **cask-only** on macOS — the cask ships the CLI wrapper; never `brew services start tailscale`) |
pitfalls/README.md-184-| [`recovery-mode-resume-keeps-nomodeset-in-cmdline`](recovery-mode-resume-keeps-nomodeset-in-cmdline.md) | an iGPU / DRM device silently disappears after a troubled boot; `amdgpu … probe with driver amdgpu failed with error -22`; `card2` missing from `/sys/class/drm/`; module loaded with refcount 0 and nothing bound; the NVIDIA proprietary driver still works so nothing looks wrong; `amdgpu: ATPX version 1, functions 0x00000000` (red herring — appears on healthy boots too); `/proc/cmdline` has `recovery nomodeset dis_ucode_ldr` | not a bug — recovery-menu "resume" keeps the recovery cmdline; only `nomodeset` actually bites (`recovery`/`dis_ucode_ldr` aren't even recognised on kernel 7.0). Check `/proc/cmdline` BEFORE reading driver logs |
pitfalls/README.md-185-| [`specstory-custom-command-drops-configured-flags`](specstory-custom-command-drops-configured-flags.md) | `claude-copilot-once` (no args) runs in bypass-permissions mode but `claude-copilot-once --resume <id>` runs in `auto` mode; `/status` shows the permission mode coming from `~/.claude/settings.json` instead of the `--dangerously-skip-permissions` set in `claude_cmd`; no warning either way, `specstory check claude` reports `✅ All systems go!` in both | fixed (`_copilot_specstory_claude_cmd` rebuilds specstory's `-c` string from the configured `claude_cmd` — `-c` **replaces** that command, never appends to it) |
pitfalls/README.md-186-| [`tmux-display-menu-silent-fail`](tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md) | `prefix + Space` / `prefix + e` doesn't open the popup menu, no error | workaround documented (script + height tiers) |
pitfalls/README.md-187-| [`tmux-extended-keys-always-paste`](tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md) | pasting a multi-line snippet into bash + ble.sh under tmux mashes every line into one command with a literal `^[[106;5u` between them: `> uname -r^[[106;5uldd --version^[[106;5ugcc --version…`, then `uname: invalid option -- '['`, `bash: 5uldd: command not found...`, `[ble: exit 127]`; bracketed-paste markers are present but the inner newlines arrive CSI-u-encoded; zsh 5.9+ does not reproduce (its paste handler normalizes CSI-u back), so it only shows up with `primaryShell=bash` / ad-hoc bash + ble.sh | fixed (`set -s extended-keys on`, never `always`, in `dot_config/tmux/common.conf`) — `always` re-encodes EVERY modifier combo that already has a legacy encoding, including the Ctrl+J (LF) embedded in pasted text, as `ESC [ 106 ; 5 u`; `on` emits CSI-u only for keys with no legacy encoding so Shift+Enter / Ctrl+Enter / Ctrl+/ / Ctrl+digit still reach Claude Code, Neovim and tmux window-switching. Graduated to a CLAUDE.md Hard invariant |
pitfalls/README.md-188-| [`tmux-join-pane-numeric-target-pane-not-window`](tmux-join-pane-numeric-target-pane-not-window.md) | `Source and target panes must be different` in the status bar after answering a `command-prompt -p "Send pane to (target):"` with a bare window number (`1`), even though source and target are visibly in **different** windows; `join-pane` / `swap-pane` / `move-pane` all affected while `move-window -t` / `link-window -t` / `break-pane -t` accept the same bare `N` happily (the asymmetry is the confusion); a hand-typed `tmux join-pane -h -s @20 -t 1` may appear to work — an accident of which window was current; `#{window_id}` in the menu-row body is the red herring, `display-menu -t =` propagates the mouse target correctly | fixed (`command-prompt` → `choose-tree -Zw`, which returns an unambiguous `session:window`, plus pinning the source with `-s '#{pane_id}'`; `prefix + M/B/A` migrated to `choose-tree -Zs` in the same change) — a bare `N` on any `-t target-pane` resolves against the *current window's pane index*, so it often names the source pane itself |
pitfalls/README.md-189-| [`tmux-pane-bottom-blank-alacritty-macos-tabs`](tmux-pane-bottom-blank-alacritty-macos-tabs.md) | inside Alacritty + macOS native tabs **when window is maximised (green-button zoom)**, tmux status bar + a few rows of output paint at the top, then the entire bottom of the window stays empty; `tmux display -p '#{pane_height}'` reports the full height (e.g. 45); **un-maximise / drag corner** un-sticks instantly, **re-maximise reliably repros**; `tmux refresh-client` does NOT help (redraws using stale cached size); `$TERM = tmux-256color` (correct, not the cause) | confirmed 2026-05-10 (PTY size desync, maximise-state-specific); workaround = drop Alacritty native tabs / switch to Ghostty |
pitfalls/README.md-190-| [`tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right`](tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md) | nested `display-menu` via `run-shell` from right-click parent: flash, bottom-right placement, or selection silently does nothing on 2nd open | workaround documented (inline submenu items into parent) |
pitfalls/README.md-191-| [`tmux-pane-vanishes-on-ctrl-c-despite-shell-wrapper`](tmux-pane-vanishes-on-ctrl-c-despite-shell-wrapper.md) | tmux pane built with `cmd; exec $SHELL` wrapper closes on Ctrl+C inside btop/htop/less even though clean quit (`q`/`:q`) lands in shell as designed | fixed in `dot_config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh` (`trap '' INT;` prefix in `_sesh_on_exit_wrap`) |
pitfalls/README.md-192-| [`tmux-resurrect-agents`](tmux-resurrect-agents.md) | tmux-resurrect doesn't restore coding-agent / TUI sessions after `kill-server` | known limitation |

261	def _dispatch_chezmoi(forwarded: list[str]) -> int:
262	    """Route `fleet chezmoi <action> [args...]` to the chezmoi-backend helpers.
263	
264	    The top-level `apply`/`status`/`diff`/`tail`/`kill`/`compact` subcommands
265	    were removed on 2026-05-13 to free the top level for generic primitives
266	    (`tmux` / `info` / `pueue` / `exec`). All chezmoi-specific deploy ops
267	    live under this namespace now.
268	    """
269	    if not forwarded or forwarded[0] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
270	        print(_CHEZMOI_ACTIONS)
271	        return 0
272	    action = forwarded[0]
273	    rest = forwarded[1:]
274	    nested = {
275	        "apply": _dispatch_apply,
276	        "status": _dispatch_status,
277	        "diff": _dispatch_diff,
278	        "tail": _dispatch_tail,
279	        "kill": _dispatch_kill,
280	        "compact": _dispatch_compact,
281	    }
282	    fn = nested.get(action)
283	    if fn is None:

285	        return 2

303	        # The bare top-level names (apply/status/diff/tail/kill/compact) were
304	        # removed on 2026-05-13 — `fleet apply` now errors with "unknown
305	        # subcommand" by design so the namespace stays clean.
306	        "chezmoi": _dispatch_chezmoi,

310	        "tmux": _dispatch_tmux,

317	    if fn is None:

319	        return 2

118	    Shared by `password_source` (sudo) and `ssh_login_password_source`
119	    (SSH transport auth fallback) — identical 4-way schema, different
120	    Host attribute names / error-message prefixes.
121	    """
122	    t = raw_table or {}
123	    ps_type = (t.get("type") or "none").lower()
124	    if ps_type not in ("plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"):
125	        raise ValueError(
126	            f"{path}: host {host_name!r} has invalid {field_name}.type={ps_type!r}"
127	        )
128	    ps_arg = t.get("value") if ps_type == "plain" else t.get("item")
129	    return ps_type, ps_arg  # type: ignore[return-value]
130	
131	
132	def load_hosts(path: Path) -> tuple[list[Host], dict]:
133	    """Parse machines.toml -> ([Host, ...], defaults dict).
134	
135	    Merges [defaults] into each host (host overrides defaults). The
136	    `password_source` / `ssh_login_password_source` tables are normalized
137	    into (type, arg) pairs on Host.
138	    """
139	    if not path.exists():
140	        raise FileNotFoundError(
141	            f"Fleet config not found: {path}\n"
142	            f"Hint: chezmoi apply seeds ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — edit it "
143	            f"to list your machines, or pass --config PATH."
144	        )
145	    with path.open("rb") as f:
146	        data = tomllib.load(f)
147	
148	    defaults = data.get("defaults", {}) or {}
149	    raw_hosts = data.get("hosts", []) or []
150	    if not raw_hosts:
151	        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no [[hosts]] entries defined.")
152	
153	    hosts: list[Host] = []
154	    seen_names: set[str] = set()
155	    for idx, raw in enumerate(raw_hosts):
156	        name = raw.get("name")
157	        if not name:
158	            raise ValueError(f"{path}: [[hosts]][{idx}] missing required `name`.")
159	        if name in seen_names:
160	            raise ValueError(f"{path}: duplicate host name {name!r}.")
161	        seen_names.add(name)
162	
163	        merged = {**defaults, **raw}
164	        ps_type, ps_arg = _parse_password_source_table(
165	            merged.pop("password_source", None),
166	            field_name="password_source", path=path, host_name=name,
167	        )
168	        ssh_ps_type, ssh_ps_arg = _parse_password_source_table(
169	            merged.pop("ssh_login_password_source", None),
170	            field_name="ssh_login_password_source", path=path, host_name=name,
171	        )
172	
173	        # Drop keys that aren't Host fields (e.g. defaults-only knobs we read elsewhere).
174	        host_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(Host)}
175	        host_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in merged.items() if k in host_fields}
176	        host = Host(
177	            **host_kwargs,
178	            password_source_type=ps_type,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
179	            password_source_arg=ps_arg,
180	            ssh_login_password_source_type=ssh_ps_type,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
181	            ssh_login_password_source_arg=ssh_ps_arg,
182	        )
183	
184	        # Validation: at least one of ssh_alias / hostname (skipped for local hosts).
185	        if not host.local and not host.ssh_alias and not host.hostname:
186	            raise ValueError(
187	                f"{path}: host {name!r} must define either `ssh_alias` "
188	                f"(preferred) or `hostname` (or set `local = true` to run "
189	                f"on the orchestrator machine without SSH)."
190	            )
191	        hosts.append(host)
192	    return hosts, defaults

=== plan file head ===
# Plan: smarter "Local SSH config" step in `ssh-setup-remote`

## Context

`ssh-setup-remote` (`dot_config/shell/96_ssh_setup.sh`, "Step 3: Local SSH config",
lines 187–248) currently **always appends** a fresh `Host` block to the chosen config file.
That is wrong for the case the user just hit: running `ssh-setup-remote ts_mac` where `ts_mac`
is **already** a configured Host (that is exactly why `ssh-copy-id ts_mac` reached
`100.100.100.100`). Appending a second `Host ts_mac` block produces a confusing duplicate, and
the new `IdentityFile` may not even take effect (first-match-wins per key).

We want the wizard to recognize two situations and do the right thing automatically:

1. **Adhoc new host** (`user@ip`): one-step — create a Host alias + write the block. (≈ current
   behavior, refined.)
2. **Existing host**: alias already exists but had no key configured; *add* `IdentityFile`
   (+ optional `IdentitiesOnly yes`) **into the existing block, in whichever file it lives** —
   not a duplicate stanza.

The config can be split: managed `~/.ssh/config` is an entry point that `Include
~/.ssh/config.d/*`. Locating an existing Host must **recursively follow `Include` directives**
(glob, `~`/relative/absolute). On *this* machine the live `~/.ssh/config` is the user's
pre-existing hand-curated file with **no `Include` line**, yet `~/.ssh/config.d/` exists — so
drop-ins here currently do not load (handled below).

### Decisions (confirmed)
- **Mechanism**: inline `python3` heredoc helper for parse/find/edit; shell keeps all
  interactive prompts. Fall back to current append-only flow if `python3` is absent.
- **Existing IdentityFile present**: show the block, prompt `[r]eplace / [a]dd another / [s]kip`.
- **config.d drop-in but no `Include` in `~/.ssh/config`**: detect and offer to add
  `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*`.

## Implementation

### 1. New shell helper `_ssh_cfg_py()` in `dot_config/shell/96_ssh_setup.sh`

One POSIX-source-safe function wrapping a single `python3 - "$@" <<'PY' … PY` heredoc with a
subcommand dispatch (keeps all Include-resolution logic in one place). Returns 127 if `python3`
is missing so callers can fall back.

Python CLI (root = `$HOME/.ssh/config`, ssh_dir = its parent):
- `resolve_includes(start)` — recursive walk from `~/.ssh/config`; for each non-comment
  `Include` line, split patterns, `os.path.expanduser`, make relative patterns relative to
  `ssh_dir`, `glob.glob`, recurse; `seen` set guards loops; returns ordered file list. Reuses the
  pattern already proven in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py:_detect_ssh` but made recursive.
- `find <alias>` — scan resolved files for a `Host` line whose tokens contain `alias` as an
  exact token (skip `*?!` wildcard/negation patterns, matching the awk in
  `dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml`). On hit, print machine-readable
  `key=value` lines for the shell: `found=1`, `file=…`, `has_identityfile=0|1`,
  `identityfile=…`, `key_present=0|1` (idempotency: exact `$key_path` already in block), plus
  the block text (for display). Exit non-zero / `found=0` when not found.
- `insert <file> <alias> <key> <action>` — rewrite the matched block: `action` ∈
  `insert` (no existing IdentityFile), `replace`, `add`. Indentation copied from the block's
  existing indented lines (fallback 4 spaces). Optional trailing `--identities-only` appends
  `IdentitiesOnly yes` if absent. Atomic write: temp file in same dir → `os.replace` →
  reapply `0o600`.
- `ensure-include` / `add-include` — report whether `resolve_includes` reaches
  `~/.ssh/config.d/`; if not, `add-include` prepends `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` (with a
  comment) near the top of `~/.ssh/config`, matching `dot_ssh/create_private_config` layout
  (Include-at-top so drop-ins are visible; note first-match-wins ordering).
```

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "mlflow>=3.4",
#   "tyro>=0.9",
#   "rich>=13.9",
#   "plotext>=5.2",
#   "textual>=5.0",
# ]
# ///
"""mlf — umbrella CLI for MLflow operations.

Bare `mlf` (no args) launches the interactive Textual TUI dashboard.
Subcommands below bypass it for scripted automation.

Subcommands:
  tui                            Launch the interactive dashboard (default)
  tv [...]                       Launch `tv mlflow` (the fuzzy picker channel)
  open <id>                      Open the experiment / run / model page in browser
  copy <id>                      Copy an id to the clipboard
  plot <run_id> [metric...]      Terminal line plot of metric history (scripts/mlf/plot.py)
  list <kind> [...]              Tabular dump of experiments / runs / models (scripts/mlf/list.py)
  download <name>[@version|alias] Download a registered model's artifacts (scripts/mlf/download.py)

Backend is read from $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI (file:./mlruns | sqlite:///path | http(s)://host:port).
`open` requires an http(s):// URI; other subcommands work against all three.

Mirrors the structure of `fleet` (see dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet).
"""
===== dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x =====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
    printf '%s\n' \
        "Usage:" \
        "  x copy [--force] [FILE]" \
        "  x copy-file [--force] PATH..." \
        "  x paste" \
        "  x open TARGET" \
        "  x help" \
        "" \
        "Examples:" \
        "  printf \"hello\" | x copy" \
        "  x copy ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub" \
        "  x copy-file ~/Downloads/report.pdf" \
        "  x paste" \
        "  x open https://example.com"
}

err() {
    printf 'x: %s\n' "$*" >&2
}

is_wsl() {
    local version
    [[ -r /proc/version ]] || return 1
    version="$(< /proc/version)"
    [[ "$version" == *[Mm]icrosoft* || "$version" == *[Ww][Ss][Ll]* ]]
}

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "rich>=13.9",

# ///
"""pqsum — pueue queue summary (text + AI + cleanup verdicts).

Subcommands (positional, default `text`):
  text                Tabular summary (overall + status breakdown + per-group).
  ai                  AI summary with per-group cleanability + per-task recovery hints.
  json                Raw parsed JSON to stdout (machine-readable).

AI flags:
  --report            Emit a markdown report (Summary / Cleanup Candidates /
                      Failures Needing Action / Raw status) instead of Rich blocks.
  --out PATH          Write the report to PATH (default: stdout).
  --clean             Render report, then for each `safe-to-clean` group prompt y/N
                      and run its cleanup_command. `review`/`keep` are NEVER touched.
  --yes               Skip y/N prompts (still only acts on `safe-to-clean`).
  --multi-host        Tell the LLM the input describes multiple hosts (used by `fleet pueue --ai`).
  --stdin-json        Read pre-merged pueue JSON from stdin (fleet feeds this).
                      Schema: list of host snapshots, each with the parsed shape this script emits.
  --deep              Include the last ~20 lines of each Failed task's log in the prompt
                      (more recovery context, more tokens).
  -r, --refresh       Bypass the prompt-hash cache.
  --no-cache          Don't read or write the cache.
  --dry-run           Print the constructed prompt; no AI call.

# wake — Wake-on-LAN sender. Powers on a box by broadcasting a magic packet.
#
# The passive side (arming the target NIC + persisting it across reboots) is the
# `wake_on_lan` ansible role (chezmoi prompt `installWakeOnLan`). Wake-from-full-
# shutdown (S5) also needs a one-time BIOS change (Power On By PCI-E on, ErP off).

#
# Usage:
#   wake <host|MAC> [<host|MAC> ...]   # send magic packet(s)
#   wake --list                        # show configured hosts
#   wake <host> -b 192.168.1.255       # override the broadcast address
#
# Hosts live in ~/.config/wake/hosts.toml (seeded once by chezmoi):
#   [hosts.david-ubuntu]
#   mac       = "cc:28:aa:89:1b:9a"
#   broadcast = "192.168.31.255"   # optional; subnet-directed broadcast
#   # port    = 9                  # optional (default 9)
#
# Pure stdlib (socket + tomllib) — no external dependency, so it works on a
# fresh box before the `wakeonlan` apt/brew twin is installed.

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import re
import socket

===== dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_dotcfg =====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# dotcfg — reconfigure your dotfiles prompts on an already-initialized machine.
#
# Thin, deployed launcher (lives on PATH at ~/.dotfiles/bin/dotcfg) for the
# `reconfigure` subcommand of scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py — the single source
# of truth for chezmoi prompts. That script is NOT deployed (scripts/** is in
# .chezmoiignore.tmpl); it is fetched as one URL by bootstrap.sh on fresh
# machines and otherwise run from the chezmoi source dir. We locate it via
# `chezmoi source-path`, so this wrapper works from any cwd.
#
# Why a wrapper and not move the script here: the script must stay a single
# self-contained PEP 723 file in scripts/init/ (bootstrap fetches it by URL,
# and `gen` renders .chezmoi.toml.tmpl + Dockerfile from its PROMPTS table).
# Mirrors the `czcfg` shell function in dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh;
# this binary form additionally works from non-interactive / non-shell contexts
# and gets tab-completion parity with fleet / mlf / pqsum / x.
#
#   dotcfg                                  # interactive TUI, seeded from current values
#   dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes # non-interactive single-key change
#   dotcfg --dry-run                        # preview the chezmoi command
#
# All arguments are forwarded verbatim to `dotfiles_init.py reconfigure`.
set -euo pipefail

if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'dotcfg: uv not found — install it first (https://astral.sh/uv).\n' >&2
    exit 1
fi
if ! command -v chezmoi >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'dotcfg: chezmoi not found on PATH.\n' >&2
```

#!/usr/bin/env bats

load "../test_helper.bash"

X_BIN="$REPO_ROOT/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x"

setup() {
  setup_path_stub
  X_TMP="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/x-cli.XXXXXX")"
  export X_TMP
}

teardown() {
  [ -n "${X_TMP:-}" ] && [ -d "$X_TMP" ] && rm -rf "$X_TMP"
  cleanup_path_stubs
}

_stub_uname() {
  local value="$1"
  cat > "$BATS_STUB_DIR/uname" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf '%s\n' "$value"
EOF
  chmod +x "$BATS_STUB_DIR/uname"
}

cat > "$X_TMP/pbcopy.input"

  printf 'file contents\n' > "$X_TMP/source.txt"

  [ "$(cat "$X_TMP/pbcopy.input")" = "file contents" ]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
script="$1"
shift
printf '%s\n' "$script" > "$X_TMP/osascript.script_arg"
printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$X_TMP/osascript.args"
cat > "$X_TMP/osascript.stdin"

  mkdir -p "$X_TMP/folder"
  printf 'payload' > "$X_TMP/file.txt"

  run "$X_BIN" copy-file "$X_TMP/file.txt" "$X_TMP/folder"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$(cat "$X_TMP/osascript.script_arg")" = "-" ]
  grep -F 'set the clipboard to fileList' "$X_TMP/osascript.stdin" >/dev/null

=== test_helper ===
# Shared helpers for bats tests. Source from each .bats file:
#   load "../test_helper.bash"   # or the equivalent relative path
#
# Keep this file tiny. No bats-assert / bats-file / bats-support — plain
# bats built-ins ([ ], run, $status, $output) are enough.

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/.." && pwd)"
if [ "$(basename "$REPO_ROOT")" = "tests" ]; then
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$REPO_ROOT/.." && pwd)"
fi
export REPO_ROOT

_BATS_STUB_DIRS=()

# Create a temp directory and prepend it to PATH. Exposes the path via
# $BATS_STUB_DIR (not via stdout) so the PATH export actually sticks — using
# command substitution would run this in a subshell and discard the export.
setup_path_stub() {
  BATS_STUB_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bats-stub.XXXXXX")"
  _BATS_STUB_DIRS+=("$BATS_STUB_DIR")
  PATH="$BATS_STUB_DIR:$PATH"
  export PATH BATS_STUB_DIR
}

# Cleanup function. Call from your own teardown() if you override it:
#   teardown() { your_cleanup; cleanup_path_stubs; }
cleanup_path_stubs() {
  local dir
  for dir in "${_BATS_STUB_DIRS[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$dir" ] && [ -d "$dir" ] && rm -rf "$dir"
  done
  _BATS_STUB_DIRS=()
}

# Default teardown — fires only if the .bats file does not define its own.
teardown() { cleanup_path_stubs; }

`echo "########## lan-devices.toml"; cat dot_config/television/cable/lan-devices.toml; echo "########## ssh-config.toml"; cat dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml`

```text
########## lan-devices.toml
# LAN devices channel for television (tv)
# Fuzzy-search local network devices with open ports, MAC/vendor,
# hostname, latency, and last-seen timestamp.
#
# Usage:
#   tv lan-devices
#   lanscan                 # shell alias, runs a full scan up front
#
# The channel reads ~/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv, which is populated by
# ~/.config/television/lan-scan.sh. `watch = 2.0` makes rows appear as
# the background scan progresses (state column: discovered / scanning /
# scanned / stale).
#
# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
#   1. All discovered devices (sorted by IP)
#   2. Only devices with open ports
#   3. Fresh only (last-seen within 5 min)
#
# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
#   1. Cached nmap service detail (fast)
#   2. Live `nmap -sV -Pn` rescan (blocking)
#   3. ARP + rDNS + mDNS metadata
#
# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid tmux/TV conflicts):
#   Enter      Full `nmap -sV -A` in execute mode
#   Alt+R      Rescan ports on selected host + reload
#   Alt+F      Rescan full subnet (discover + ports) + reload
#   Alt+D      Re-discover only (no port scan) + reload
#   Alt+S      Open ssh to host
#   Alt+H      Open http://host in browser
#   Alt+C      Clear cache + reload
#   Ctrl+Y     Copy IP to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH)

[metadata]
name = "lan-devices"
description = "LAN devices: IP, MAC, vendor, hostname, open ports, latency"
requirements = ["nmap"]

[source]
# Columns (tab-separated, matches lan-scan.sh TSV_HEADER):
# 0:ip  1:mac  2:vendor  3:hostname  4:ports  5:top  6:rtt  7:seen  8:state
command = [
  """
  tsv="$HOME/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv"
  if [ ! -s "$tsv" ]; then
    "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh" all >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    printf '...\\t-\\t(scanning — results will stream in)\\t-\\t-\\t-\\t-\\t-\\tscanning\\n'
    exit 0
  fi
  awk -F'\\t' 'NR>1' "$tsv"
  """,
  """
  tsv="$HOME/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv"
  awk -F'\\t' 'NR>1 && $5 ~ /^[1-9]/' "$tsv"
  """,
  """
  tsv="$HOME/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv"
  now=$(date +%s)
  awk -F'\\t' -v now="$now" 'NR>1 {
    "date -j -f %H:%M:%S \"" $8 "\" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -d \"" $8 "\" +%s 2>/dev/null" | getline ts
    if (now - ts < 300) print
  }' "$tsv"
  """,
]
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:2}  {split:\\t:3}  [{split:\\t:4}p] {split:\\t:5}  {split:\\t:6}ms  {split:\\t:7}  {split:\\t:8}"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"
watch = 2.0
no_sort = true

[preview]
command = [
  """
  ip='{split:\\t:0}'
  f="$HOME/.cache/tv/lan-ports/$ip.txt"
  if [ -s "$f" ]; then
    cat "$f"
  else
    echo "No cached port scan for $ip."
    echo "Press Alt+R to scan this host, or Ctrl+F to cycle preview."
  fi
  """,
  """
  ip='{split:\\t:0}'
  echo "# Live nmap -sV -Pn -F $ip (blocking, ~10-30s)"
  echo
  nmap -sV -Pn -F "$ip" 2>/dev/null
  """,
  """
  ip='{split:\\t:0}'
  echo "# ARP"
  if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then arp -an | grep -F "($ip)" || echo "no ARP entry"; \
  else ip neigh show "$ip" 2>/dev/null || echo "no ARP entry"; fi
  echo
  echo "# Reverse DNS"
  getent hosts "$ip" 2>/dev/null || dig +short +time=1 +tries=1 -x "$ip" 2>/dev/null || echo "(none)"
  echo
  echo "# mDNS"
  if command -v avahi-resolve >/dev/null 2>&1; then avahi-resolve -a "$ip" 2>/dev/null || echo "(none)"; \
  elif [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then dscacheutil -q host -a ip_address "$ip" 2>/dev/null || echo "(none)"; \
  else echo "(no mDNS tool)"; fi
  echo
  echo "# Ping"
  ping -c 2 "$ip" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 5
  """,
]
header = "Device {split:\\t:0} ({split:\\t:2} / {split:\\t:3})"

[ui]
input_header = "LAN Devices"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 55

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:details"
alt-r = ["actions:rescan_host", "reload_source"]
alt-f = ["actions:rescan_all", "reload_source"]
alt-d = ["actions:rediscover", "reload_source"]
alt-s = "actions:ssh"
alt-h = "actions:http"
alt-c = ["actions:clean", "reload_source"]
ctrl-y = ["actions:copy_ip", "reload_source"]

[actions.details]
description = "Full nmap -sV -A scan"
command = "ip='{split:\\t:0}'; echo \"# nmap -sV -A $ip\"; nmap -sV -A -Pn \"$ip\" 2>/dev/null; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.rescan_host]
description = "Rescan selected host's open ports"
command = "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh ports --host '{split:\\t:0}' >/dev/null 2>&1 &"
mode = "fork"

[actions.rescan_all]
description = "Rescan full subnet (discover + ports)"
command = "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh all >/dev/null 2>&1 &"
mode = "fork"

[actions.rediscover]
description = "Re-discover hosts (no port scan)"
command = "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh discover >/dev/null 2>&1 &"
mode = "fork"

[actions.ssh]
description = "SSH to selected host"
command = "ssh '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "execute"

[actions.http]
description = "Open http://host in browser"
command = """
ip='{split:\\t:0}'
url="http://$ip"
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then open "$url"
elif command -v xdg-open >/dev/null 2>&1; then xdg-open "$url"
else echo "No browser opener; URL: $url"; read -r _
fi
"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.clean]
description = "Clear LAN scan cache"
command = "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh clean >/dev/null 2>&1"
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy_ip]
description = "Copy IP to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH)"
command = """
d='{split:\\t:0}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\\033]52;c;%s\\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
"""
mode = "fork"
########## ssh-config.toml
# Custom SSH config channel for television (tv)
# Parses Host entries from ~/.ssh/config AND ~/.ssh/config.d/* (Include support).
# The community ssh-hosts channel only reads ~/.ssh/config directly.
#
# Each entry shows which file the host is defined in, so duplicates across
# config.d/* are easy to spot. The output (what gets passed to ssh / actions)
# is just the bare hostname.
#
# Usage:
#   tv ssh-config
#
# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
#   Enter      SSH into selected host
#   Alt+T      Online probe: BatchMode=yes test (does pubkey login actually work?)
#   Alt+A      Offline batch scan: list every host + whether a local key file exists
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Preview shows resolved config via `ssh -G` plus a local-key existence check
# (no network — just stat the IdentityFile paths).

[metadata]
name = "ssh-config"
description = "SSH hosts (with Include config.d/* support)"
requirements = ["ssh", "awk", "sort"]

[source]
# Emit "<source-file>\t<hostname>" so the picker shows the origin file but
# actions still receive a clean hostname via {split:\t:1}.
command = """
for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  rel=${f#$HOME/}
  awk -v src="$rel" '
    /^[[:space:]]*Host[[:space:]]/ {
      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
        if ($i !~ /[*?]/) printf "%s\\t%s\\n", src, $i
      }
    }' "$f"
done | sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2
"""
display = "{split:\\t:1}  ({split:\\t:0})"
output = "{split:\\t:1}"

[preview]
command = """
host='{split:\\t:1}'
src='{split:\\t:0}'
echo "# defined in: $src"
echo
ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^(host|hostname|user|port|identityfile|proxycommand|proxyjump|forwardagent|identityagent|localforward|remoteforward)[[:space:]]'
echo
echo '--- local key check (offline) ---'
found=0
while IFS= read -r f; do
  [ -z "$f" ] && continue
  case "$f" in '~/'*) f="$HOME/${f#'~/'}";; '~') f="$HOME";; esac
  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
    echo "  [OK]   $f"
    found=1
  else
    echo "  [miss] $f"
  fi
done <<EOF
$(ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^identityfile / {print $2}')
EOF
if [ "$found" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo
  echo '  => no IdentityFile present locally — password login likely required'
  echo '     (or relies on ssh-agent / IdentityAgent — try Alt+T to probe)'
fi
"""

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:connect"
alt-t = "actions:probe"
alt-a = "actions:scan_all"

[actions.connect]
description = "SSH into the selected host"
command = "ssh '{split:\\t:1}'"
mode = "execute"

[actions.probe]
description = "Probe selected host with BatchMode (no password prompt allowed)"
command = """
host='{split:\\t:1}'
echo "# Probing $host with BatchMode=yes (ConnectTimeout=3)"
echo "# Exit 0 = passwordless login works; non-zero = needs password / unreachable / key not authorized"
echo
ssh -o BatchMode=yes \\
    -o ConnectTimeout=3 \\
    -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \\
    -o PreferredAuthentications=publickey,hostbased,gssapi-with-mic \\
    "$host" true
rc=$?
echo
case $rc in
  0)   echo "[OK] passwordless login works for '$host'" ;;
  255) echo "[FAIL] connection / auth error (exit 255) — needs password, key not authorized, or host unreachable" ;;
  *)   echo "[FAIL] remote command failed (exit $rc) — auth probably OK but 'true' failed" ;;
esac
echo
echo '[Press Enter to exit]'
read -r _
"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.scan_all]
description = "Offline scan: for every host, check if any IdentityFile exists locally"
command = """
echo "# Scanning all hosts (offline — no network) ..."
echo "# Legend: [OK] = at least one IdentityFile present locally"
echo "#         [--] = no key file on disk (password / agent / unconfigured)"
echo
for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  rel=${f#$HOME/}
  awk -v src="$rel" '
    /^[[:space:]]*Host[[:space:]]/ {
      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
        if ($i !~ /[*?]/) printf "%s\\t%s\\n", src, $i
      }
    }' "$f"
done | sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2 | while IFS=$'\\t' read -r src host; do
  keyline=""
  found=0
  while IFS= read -r kf; do
    [ -z "$kf" ] && continue
    case "$kf" in '~/'*) kf="$HOME/${kf#'~/'}";; '~') kf="$HOME";; esac
    if [ -f "$kf" ]; then
      keyline="$kf"
      found=1
      break
    fi
  done <<EOF
$(ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^identityfile / {print $2}')
EOF
  if [ "$found" -eq 1 ]; then
    printf '  [OK] %-28s %-22s -> %s\\n' "$host" "($src)" "$keyline"
  else
    printf '  [--] %-28s %-22s    (no local key)\\n' "$host" "($src)"
  fi
done
echo
echo '[Press Enter to exit]'
read -r _
"""
mode = "execute"
```

**Dynamic candidates wired up:**

- `fleet` host names — `_fleet_hosts_one` / `_fleet_hosts_csv` shell out to `fleet hosts --list`. Used for the positional `fleet hosts NAME`, `fleet chezmoi diff HOST`, `fleet chezmoi tail HOST`, and the `--hosts=foo,bar,baz` CSV flag everywhere.
- `pqsum -g <GROUP>` — `_pqsum` shells out to `pueue status --json | jq '.groups | keys[]'`.
- `mlf` ids (run-id, experiment-id, model-name) — **not** auto-completed (would round-trip MLflow tracking server, possibly auth-required). Use `tv mlflow` for fuzzy id picking instead.
- `yth` video ids — **not** auto-completed (opaque 11-char ids; enumerating the whole history on every TAB is wasteful). Use `tv yth` or `yth search <query>` instead.
- `wake` host names — `_wake` shells out to `wake --list-names` (reads `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`), same pattern as `_fleet_hosts_one`.
- `appsrc which <name>` / `appsrc size <name>` — `_appsrc_names` shells out to `appsrc scan --list-names` (installed GUI app names) and adds `_command_names -e` / `compgen -c` (PATH commands), so both a GUI app name and a shell command complete. Same shell-out pattern as `_wake` / `_fleet_hosts_one`.

**Adding a new in-house CLI** (decision flow):

1. **Does it use tyro?** → Use Strategy A. Mirror `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh`. Add a `<tool>-update-completion` helper to `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. Don't forget to rewrite `#compdef` in zsh post-gen.
2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).
3. **Hand-rolled / shell script** → Strategy B hand-written. One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers.
4. **Update this table + `docs/shells/aliases.md`** in the same commit (per the cross-file maintenance rule in `CLAUDE.md`).

## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi

**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:

1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.

### What we DO track

- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`

## Generating Completions After Fresh Install

**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).

The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
```

```text
# shellcheck shell=bash
# log_shared.sh — one console-logging vocabulary for every shell script in
# this repo.
#
# WHY this file exists: 13 scripts each hand-rolled the same colour block plus
# an info/warn/success/error trio, in four mutually incompatible dialects —
# `echo -e` vs `printf '%b'` vs `printf '%s'`, `'\033'` (needs %b) vs
# `$'\033'` (real ESC), `[OK]` vs `[SUCCESS]`. Colour was gated on `[[ -t 1 ]]`
# in three of them and unconditional in the rest; NO_COLOR was honoured
# nowhere. This file is the single source of truth for all of it.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# How to consume it
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two mechanisms, picked by whether the script has a stable path back to the
# source tree at runtime:
#
#   1. INLINED — `{{ include "scripts/lib/log_shared.sh" }}`
#      chezmoi renders every run_*.sh.tmpl to a temp path and executes it
#      there, so `source` has nothing to resolve against. `include` (not
#      `includeTemplate`) because this file is plain bash with no `{{ … }}`
#      tokens to re-render. Same reasoning as scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh —
#      read that file's header for the long version.
#
#      COST: an inlined copy is part of the consuming script's bytes, so
#      editing THIS file changes the hash of every `run_onchange_after_*`
#      that includes it and re-triggers all of them on the next apply
#      (a full ansible re-run, a full brew bundle, …). Batch edits here.
#
#   2. SOURCED — `. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/lib/log_shared.sh"`
#      For scripts/*.sh, which only ever run from the repo checkout.
#
# `scripts/**` is listed in .chezmoiignore.tmpl, so this file is never
# deployed to $HOME. Its only runtime existence is the inlined copy or a
# source from the checkout.
#
# Consumers are enumerated in the `scripts/lib/log_shared.sh` row of
# CLAUDE.md § Cross-file maintenance rules — update it when you add one.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# API
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Message lines (all accept multiple args, joined with a single space):
#   info    "msg"    [INFO]     blue
#   success "msg"    [SUCCESS]  green
#   warn    "msg"    [WARN]     yellow
#   error   "msg"    [ERROR]    red      → stderr (see LOG_STREAM)
#   skip    "msg"    [SKIP]     dim
#   die     "msg"    [ERROR]    red      → stderr, then `exit 1`
#
# Structure:
#   step "Heading"   blank line + bold heading (section separator)
#   hr               dim horizontal rule
#   dim  "msg"       unlabelled dim text (hints, command echoes)
#
# Verification mode — for one-shot "did this actually work" check scripts.
# This is NOT a test framework: committed, re-runnable tests belong in
# tests/unit/*.bats (`just bats`). Use these when you want a throwaway
# post-apply sanity script that still exits non-zero on failure:
#   ok  "condition holds"     ✔ green,  bumps the pass counter
=== consumers ===

# 50_networking.sh - Networking tool aliases and helpers (shared bash + zsh).
# Moved from dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh; the only zsh-isms were
# `print -r --` / `print -u2` / `print "..."` which all became `printf`.

# --- Listening ports (works everywhere, no extra install needed) ---
alias ports='lsof -i -P -n | grep LISTEN'

# --- IP address helpers ---
alias myip='curl -s https://ifconfig.me'
if [[ "$OSTYPE" == darwin* ]]; then
  alias localip='ipconfig getifaddr en0'
else
  # shellcheck disable=SC2142  # `\$1` is awk's field-1, not a shell positional.
  alias localip='hostname -I | awk "{print \$1}"'
fi

# ipinfo.io returns JSON (ip/city/region/country/org) in one call; use for VPN
# exit-node verification where you need country + ISP at a glance.
ipgeo() {
  if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
    curl -s https://ipinfo.io | jq -r '"IP:      \(.ip)\nCity:    \(.city)\nRegion:  \(.region)\nCountry: \(.country)\nOrg:     \(.org)"'
  else
    curl -s https://ipinfo.io
  fi
}
alias vpncheck='ipgeo'

# --- nmap shortcuts ---
if command -v nmap &>/dev/null; then
  # Quick ping sweep of local /24 subnet
  pingsweep() {
    local ip
    if [[ "$OSTYPE" == darwin* ]]; then
      ip=$(ipconfig getifaddr en0 2>/dev/null)
    else
      ip=$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')
    fi
    local base="${ip%.*}.0/24"
    echo "Scanning $base ..."
    nmap -sn "$base"

#   - lm-sensors  -> on-board Super-I/O / PCI temp+fan chips (hw-sensors)

# that's normal, not a fault; chassis fans live on the BMC plane instead.

<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./pitfalls/tailscale-another-copy-app-store-leftover.md`

```text
1	# "Another Tailscale copy was found on this Mac" + DNS unavailable
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- Tailscale debug → System Configuration Inspector: `System Configuration Issue Found` / `A software conflict and/or installation error on your Mac has been detected` / `Another Tailscale copy was found on this Mac.` / `Another copy of Tailscale was found at this path: /Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app` / `onlyOneCopyExplainer`
5	- `Current Issues` → `DNS Unavailable` / `Tailscale can't reach the configured DNS servers` / `Code: dns-forward-failing`
6	- `mdfind -name "Tailscale.app"` returns **two** paths: `/Applications/Tailscale.app` **and** `/Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app`
7	- macsys menu-bar app keeps flagging the conflict even after quitting/reopening
8	- (related, second trap) `brew upgrade --cask tailscale-app` prints `Removing files: /usr/local/bin/tailscale` and re-creates it; a later `brew upgrade tailscale` / `brew link tailscale` warns `Target /usr/local/bin/tailscale already exists` — the **formula and cask fight over `/usr/local/bin/tailscale`**
9	
10	**First seen**: 2026-07
11	**Affects**: macOS. (1) The `.localized` leftover bites any host that installed Tailscale from the Mac App Store **before** this repo migrated `mas "Tailscale"` → `cask "tailscale-app"` (May 2026). (2) The formula/cask CLI-path conflict bites any host that had **both** `cask "tailscale-app"` and the standalone `brew "tailscale"` formula installed.
12	**Status**: fixed — delete the leftover; use the **cask only** (no `tailscale` formula on macOS)
13	
14	## Symptom
15	
16	Two independent Tailscale `.app` bundles coexist. The **running** one is the
17	macsys standalone build (installed by `cask "tailscale-app"`); the **idle** one
18	is the old sandboxed App Store build, sitting in a `.localized` wrapper folder:
19	
20	```
21	$ mdfind -name "Tailscale.app"
22	/Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app
23	/Applications/Tailscale.app
24	
25	$ for p in /Applications/Tailscale.app /Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app; do
26	    echo "$p → $(defaults read "$p/Contents/Info.plist" CFBundleIdentifier)  $(defaults read "$p/Contents/Info.plist" CFBundleShortVersionString)"
27	  done
28	/Applications/Tailscale.app                       → io.tailscale.ipn.macsys  1.98.8   # cask, RUNNING, system extension
29	/Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app   → io.tailscale.ipn.macos   1.98.8   # App Store leftover, idle
30	```
31	
32	The `dns-forward-failing` / DNS Unavailable banner tends to ride along with the
33	conflict (two IPN clients confusing the network-extension / DNS proxy state).
34	
35	## Root cause
36	
37	Two collisions, both stemming from **install-only** package management:
38	
39	### 1. App Store `.app` leftover (the "Another copy" warning)
40	
41	Two Tailscale variants exist for macOS, with *different bundle IDs and signing
42	chains* — macOS treats them as separate apps:
43	
44	- `io.tailscale.ipn.**macsys**` — standalone build, Developer ID-signed
45	  (`Developer ID Application: Tailscale Inc. (W5364U7YZB)`), runs a **system
46	  extension** as the daemon. This is what `cask "tailscale-app"` installs.
47	- `io.tailscale.ipn.**macos**` — sandboxed **Mac App Store** build, re-signed by
48	  Apple (`Apple Mac OS Application Signing`). Installed into a
49	  `/Applications/Tailscale.localized/` wrapper folder.
50	
51	This repo migrated `mas` → `cask` in May 2026 (Tailscale was delisted from the
52	Mac App Store — `mas` install now fails with `No apps found in the App Store for
53	ADAM ID 1475387142`; see `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`). `chezmoi
54	apply` is **install-only** and does not uninstall the previously `mas`-installed
55	copy, so it lingers. The macsys installer takes `/Applications/Tailscale.app`
56	and shoves the old copy aside into `.localized/`, producing the warning.
57	
58	(`_MASReceipt` exists in **both** bundles, so it is *not* a reliable
59	discriminator — use `CFBundleIdentifier` `macsys` vs `macos`, or the `codesign
60	-dv --verbose=4` Authority line, to tell them apart.)
61	
62	### 2. `tailscale` formula vs `tailscale-app` cask fight over the CLI path
63	
64	The `tailscale-app` **cask/pkg already installs the CLI** at
65	`/usr/local/bin/tailscale` — a tiny root-owned shell wrapper into the app:
66	
67	```
68	$ cat /usr/local/bin/tailscale
69	#!/bin/sh
70	/Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/tailscale "$@"
71	```
72	
73	So the separate standalone **`brew "tailscale"` formula is redundant** on a
74	GUI-app host. Worse, both the formula (via its `/usr/local/bin/tailscale`
75	symlink into the Cellar) and the cask (via the pkg wrapper) target the **same
76	path** — whoever installs/upgrades last wins, so `brew upgrade tailscale` and
77	`brew upgrade --cask tailscale-app` clobber each other. The formula also ships a
78	`/usr/local/bin/tailscaled` the app's system extension already provides — a
79	daemon that must **never** run on macOS. Same shape as
80	[`ollama-brew-link-fails-cask-shadows-formula`](ollama-brew-link-fails-cask-shadows-formula.md).
81	
82	## Workaround
83	
84	**Delete the idle App Store leftover** (root-owned → needs `sudo`). The running
85	macsys cask app and your tailnet login are untouched:
86	
87	```bash
88	sudo rm -rf /Applications/Tailscale.localized
89	```
90	
91	The "Another Tailscale copy" warning clears once the second `.app` is gone.
92	Optionally purge the stale sandbox container:
93	
94	```bash
95	rm -rf ~/Library/Containers/io.tailscale.ipn.macos ~/Library/Group\ Containers/*.io.tailscale.ipn.macos 2>/dev/null || true
96	```
97	
98	**Drop the redundant formula** so nothing fights the cask over the CLI path. The
99	cask's `/usr/local/bin/tailscale` wrapper is a pkg file, not brew-managed, so
100	`brew uninstall` leaves it in place — the CLI keeps working:
101	
102	```bash
103	brew uninstall tailscale                 # removes the formula + its stray tailscaled symlink
104	tailscale version                        # still 1.98.8 via the cask wrapper
105	```
106	
107	Keep the cask current (`auto_updates`, but a running server may need a nudge):
108	
109	```bash
110	HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew upgrade --cask tailscale-app   # sudo + may re-approve the system extension
111	```
112	
113	## Prevention
114	
115	- **Cask only on macOS. No `tailscale` formula.** The repo's shared
116	  `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl` carries an explicit "deliberately no
117	  `brew \"tailscale\"`" note in the darwin block — do not re-add it. The GUI app
118	  (`cask "tailscale-app"`, Brewfile.darwin) *is* the daemon **and** the CLI.
119	- **NEVER `brew services start tailscale` on macOS.** Homebrew's own post-install
120	  caveat suggests it, but the app's system extension is the daemon; a second
121	  `tailscaled` conflicts.
122	- **Prefer Standalone (cask) over App Store** — see `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`
123	  ("Standalone > App Store"). Do **not** re-add a `mas "Tailscale"` entry (it's
124	  delisted anyway).
125	- Fresh installs don't hit either trap (no App Store copy, no formula). These
126	  only bite hosts that predate the `mas → cask` migration or that once had the
127	  formula installed alongside the cask.
128	
129	## Related
130	
131	- `docs/tools/Tailscale.md` — install preference (Standalone > App Store) + this cleanup
132	- `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl` — `cask "tailscale-app"` + delisted-`mas` note
133	- `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl` — darwin block's "deliberately no formula" note
134	- `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` — A–Z row for `tailscale-app`
135	- [`ollama-brew-link-fails-cask-shadows-formula`](ollama-brew-link-fails-cask-shadows-formula.md) — same formula-vs-cask path fight
136	- [`macfuse-too-old-unsupported-macos-version-rclone-mount`](macfuse-too-old-unsupported-macos-version-rclone-mount.md) — another `auto_updates` cask that `brew upgrade` won't move
137
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
elif [[ -f /usr/local/bin/brew ]]; then
    eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"
fi
{{ end -}}

# =============================================================================
# Modular Configuration Loader
# =============================================================================

# Load all files matching $extension from $dir (sorted by filename).
# Used for the shared POSIX layer (.sh) and the zsh-only layer (.zsh).
# The sister bash equivalent (load_modular_dir in dot_bashrc.tmpl) shares
# the same name + signature so dot_config/shell/*.sh are sourced uniformly.
load_modular_dir() {
    local dir="$1"
    local ext="${2:-zsh}"
    [[ -d "$dir" ]] || return 0
    setopt local_options null_glob
    local f
    for f in "$dir"/*."$ext"; do
        [[ -r "$f" ]] && source "$f"
    done
}

# Load modular configs.
# Shared POSIX layer first — env/PATH/Homebrew shellenv, tool init wrappers
# (starship/mise/zoxide/direnv/thefuck), POSIX aliases. Both ~/.zshrc and
# ~/.bashrc source this dir so env stays consistent across shells.
load_modular_dir "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell" sh
load_modular_dir "$ZSH_CONFIG_DIR" zsh
load_modular_dir "$ZSH_CONFIG_DIR/tools" zsh
