<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Read lan-devices tv channel

`cat dot_config/television/cable/lan-devices.toml`

```text
# LAN devices channel for television (tv)
# Fuzzy-search local network devices with open ports, MAC/vendor,
# hostname, latency, and last-seen timestamp.
#
# Usage:
#   tv lan-devices
#   lanscan                 # shell alias, runs a full scan up front
#
# The channel reads ~/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv, which is populated by
# ~/.config/television/lan-scan.sh. `watch = 2.0` makes rows appear as
# the background scan progresses (state column: discovered / scanning /
# scanned / stale).
#
# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
#   1. All discovered devices (sorted by IP)
#   2. Only devices with open ports
#   3. Fresh only (last-seen within 5 min)
#
# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
#   1. Cached nmap service detail (fast)
#   2. Live `nmap -sV -Pn` rescan (blocking)
#   3. ARP + rDNS + mDNS metadata
#
# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid tmux/TV conflicts):
#   Enter      Full `nmap -sV -A` in execute mode
#   Alt+R      Rescan ports on selected host + reload
#   Alt+F      Rescan full subnet (discover + ports) + reload
#   Alt+D      Re-discover only (no port scan) + reload
#   Alt+S      Open ssh to host
#   Alt+H      Open http://host in browser
#   Alt+C      Clear cache + reload
#   Ctrl+Y     Copy IP to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH)

[metadata]
name = "lan-devices"
description = "LAN devices: IP, MAC, vendor, hostname, open ports, latency"
requirements = ["nmap"]

[source]
# Columns (tab-separated, matches lan-scan.sh TSV_HEADER):
# 0:ip  1:mac  2:vendor  3:hostname  4:ports  5:top  6:rtt  7:seen  8:state
command = [
  """
  tsv="$HOME/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv"
  if [ ! -s "$tsv" ]; then
    "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh" all >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    printf '...\\t-\\t(scanning — results will stream in)\\t-\\t-\\t-\\t-\\t-\\tscanning\\n'
    exit 0
  fi
  awk -F'\\t' 'NR>1' "$tsv"
  """,
  """
  tsv="$HOME/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv"
  awk -F'\\t' 'NR>1 && $5 ~ /^[1-9]/' "$tsv"
  """,
  """
  tsv="$HOME/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv"
  now=$(date +%s)
  awk -F'\\t' -v now="$now" 'NR>1 {
    "date -j -f %H:%M:%S \"" $8 "\" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -d \"" $8 "\" +%s 2>/dev/null" | getline ts
    if (now - ts < 300) print
  }' "$tsv"
  """,
]
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:2}  {split:\\t:3}  [{split:\\t:4}p] {split:\\t:5}  {split:\\t:6}ms  {split:\\t:7}  {split:\\t:8}"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"
watch = 2.0
no_sort = true

[preview]
command = [
  """
  ip='{split:\\t:0}'
  f="$HOME/.cache/tv/lan-ports/$ip.txt"
  if [ -s "$f" ]; then
    cat "$f"
  else
    echo "No cached port scan for $ip."
    echo "Press Alt+R to scan this host, or Ctrl+F to cycle preview."
  fi
  """,
  """
  ip='{split:\\t:0}'
  echo "# Live nmap -sV -Pn -F $ip (blocking, ~10-30s)"
  echo
  nmap -sV -Pn -F "$ip" 2>/dev/null
  """,
  """
  ip='{split:\\t:0}'
  echo "# ARP"
  if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then arp -an | grep -F "($ip)" || echo "no ARP entry"; \
  else ip neigh show "$ip" 2>/dev/null || echo "no ARP entry"; fi
  echo
  echo "# Reverse DNS"
  getent hosts "$ip" 2>/dev/null || dig +short +time=1 +tries=1 -x "$ip" 2>/dev/null || echo "(none)"
  echo
  echo "# mDNS"
  if command -v avahi-resolve >/dev/null 2>&1; then avahi-resolve -a "$ip" 2>/dev/null || echo "(none)"; \
  elif [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then dscacheutil -q host -a ip_address "$ip" 2>/dev/null || echo "(none)"; \
  else echo "(no mDNS tool)"; fi
  echo
  echo "# Ping"
  ping -c 2 "$ip" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 5
  """,
]
header = "Device {split:\\t:0} ({split:\\t:2} / {split:\\t:3})"

[ui]
input_header = "LAN Devices"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 55

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:details"
alt-r = ["actions:rescan_host", "reload_source"]
alt-f = ["actions:rescan_all", "reload_source"]
alt-d = ["actions:rediscover", "reload_source"]
alt-s = "actions:ssh"
alt-h = "actions:http"
alt-c = ["actions:clean", "reload_source"]
ctrl-y = ["actions:copy_ip", "reload_source"]

[actions.details]
description = "Full nmap -sV -A scan"
command = "ip='{split:\\t:0}'; echo \"# nmap -sV -A $ip\"; nmap -sV -A -Pn \"$ip\" 2>/dev/null; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.rescan_host]
description = "Rescan selected host's open ports"
command = "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh ports --host '{split:\\t:0}' >/dev/null 2>&1 &"
mode = "fork"

[actions.rescan_all]
description = "Rescan full subnet (discover + ports)"
command = "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh all >/dev/null 2>&1 &"
mode = "fork"

[actions.rediscover]
description = "Re-discover hosts (no port scan)"
command = "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh discover >/dev/null 2>&1 &"
mode = "fork"

[actions.ssh]
description = "SSH to selected host"
command = "ssh '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "execute"

[actions.http]
description = "Open http://host in browser"
command = """
ip='{split:\\t:0}'
url="http://$ip"
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then open "$url"
elif command -v xdg-open >/dev/null 2>&1; then xdg-open "$url"
else echo "No browser opener; URL: $url"; read -r _
fi
"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.clean]
description = "Clear LAN scan cache"
command = "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh clean >/dev/null 2>&1"
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy_ip]
description = "Copy IP to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH)"
command = """
d='{split:\\t:0}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\\033]52;c;%s\\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
"""
mode = "fork"
```
</details></tool-use>

=== fleet hosts.py head ===
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   # hosts.py itself only needs stdlib (tomllib, argparse, subprocess), but
#   # `from scripts.fleet import ...` transitively imports apply.py whose
#   # top-level `import asyncssh` / tyro / rich would otherwise fail under
#   # `uv run --script scripts/fleet/hosts.py` (the dispatcher in
#   # dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet already pulls these in via its own
#   # PEP 723 header). Keep this list in sync with apply.py.
#   "asyncssh>=2.18",
#   "tyro>=0.9",
#   "rich>=13.9",
# ]
# ///
"""fleet hosts — pick a fleet-configured host, SSH into it.

Three entry points:

  fleet hosts                 Interactive picker via `tv fleet-hosts`. Falls
                              back to a numbered-stdin menu if `tv` is not on
                              PATH (e.g. headless CI).
  fleet hosts NAME            SSH directly into NAME (skip the picker). Uses
                              ssh_alias if set; otherwise constructs
                              `ssh -p PORT -i KEY user@hostname`. Lands in an
                              attach-or-create tmux session (`--no-tmux` opts
                              out, `--tmux-session NAME` renames it).
  fleet hosts --list*         Script-friendly inventory dumps — also used by
                              the TV cable + your own shell glue:
                                --list        plain names, one per line
                                --list-tsv    name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
                                --list-json   full inventory JSON
                                --describe N  preview block for N
                                --probe N     BatchMode SSH probe of N

Mirrors `dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml` (which is sourced from
~/.ssh/config), but reads ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml instead so explicit
hostname/user/port/identity_file hosts (no ssh_config alias) are reachable.

The TV cable at `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` shells out to
`fleet hosts --list-tsv` (source), `fleet hosts --describe '{...}'` (preview),
and `fleet hosts '{...}'` (Enter action). This module is the SSOT for fleet
inventory introspection — the only TOML parser is `load_hosts()` in apply.py.

`local = true` hosts are hidden from `--list-tsv` (picker) by default — SSH'ing
into yourself is silly. Use `--include-local` to override, or run
`fleet hosts NAME` on a local host (prints a no-op message and exits 0).

```text
# fleet hosts — picker for SSH'ing into fleet-configured machines

`fleet hosts` is the TV-style picker for the fleet inventory at
`~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`. It mirrors the
[`ssh-config` cable](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml)
(`tv ssh-config`) but reads fleet's TOML instead of `~/.ssh/config`, so hosts
with explicit `hostname` / `user` / `port` / `identity_file` (no ssh_alias)
are reachable too.

Sister tools: [`fleet exec`](fleet-exec.md) for cross-host ad-hoc commands,
[`fleet pueue`](pueue.md) for queue probing,
[`fleet chezmoi apply`](../this_repo/fleet-apply.md) for the deploy workflow.
All four read the same inventory via `scripts/fleet/apply.py:load_hosts()`.

## Install

Deployed automatically by chezmoi:

- `~/.dotfiles/bin/fleet` — the umbrella binary (dispatches `fleet hosts`)
- `~/.config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` — the TV channel
- `~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/fleet/hosts.py` — the implementation
  (resolved at runtime via `chezmoi source-path`, so the cable / binary find
  the latest version even on hosts where you haven't run `chezmoi apply` yet)

No separate install step. `tv` (television) is pulled in by the devtools role
and is what powers the picker UX.

## Three entry points

| Form | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `tv fleet-hosts` | Open the picker directly via television. Enter → SSH. |
| `fleet hosts` | Same picker via the fleet umbrella (execs `tv fleet-hosts`). |
| `fleet hosts NAME` | Skip the picker — SSH straight into `NAME` (lands in tmux; see below). |
| `fleet hosts --list` | Plain host names, one per line. Scriptable. |
| `fleet hosts --list-tsv` | `name<TAB>target<TAB>kind` (the cable's source). |
| `fleet hosts --list-json` | Full inventory as JSON (plain passwords redacted). |
| `fleet hosts --describe N` | Multi-section preview block for `N` (the cable's preview). |
| `fleet hosts --probe N` | BatchMode SSH probe of `N` (the cable's Alt+T action). |

Direct invocation (`fleet hosts NAME`) uses `os.execvp("ssh", ...)`, so your
terminal becomes the SSH session — no wrapper subprocess, no lost TTY
attributes. Behaviour matches Enter inside the picker.

## You land in tmux by default

`fleet hosts NAME` (and Enter in the picker) runs `ssh -t` with a remote command
that attaches to a tmux session named `fleet`, creating it if absent:

```sh
command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec tmux new -A -s fleet || exec "${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -l
```

`tmux new -A -s` is attach-if-exists / create-otherwise. The point is
resumability: drop the connection — laptop sleeps, Wi-Fi flips, an iPad
backgrounds the terminal app — and the next `fleet hosts NAME` lands back in the
same session with the work still running. Without it every disconnect is a lost
shell.

| Flag | Effect |
|------|--------|
| *(default)* | Attach-or-create session `fleet` |
| `--tmux-session NAME` | Use a different session name |
| `--no-tmux` | Plain login shell — argv is identical to the pre-tmux behaviour |

Hosts without tmux installed fall through to a login shell, so this is safe to
leave on for a mixed fleet. `exec` in both branches means the SSH session ends
when tmux (or the shell) does, rather than leaving a wrapper behind.

The tv cable inherits all of this for free — its Enter action shells out to
`fleet hosts '{name}'`, so there is no second copy of the ssh invocation to keep
in sync.

`local = true` hosts are hidden from `--list-tsv` (you can't SSH into
yourself). They still appear in `--list` / `--list-json` for scripts that
want the full inventory. `--include-local` overrides for `--list-tsv` too.

## Keybindings (inside the picker)

| Key | Action |
```

```text
=== fleet machines.toml.tmpl ===
# ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — fleet_apply.py host inventory
#
# Seeded ONCE by chezmoi (`create_` prefix) so your edits are never overwritten.
# To reset to this template: `rm ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml && chezmoi apply`.
# File mode is 0600 (chezmoi `private_` prefix) — safe for plaintext passwords,
# but Bitwarden / interactive prompt sources are still preferred.
#
# IMPORTANT: `password_source` is for the REMOTE `sudo` password ONLY (fed to
# chezmoi via CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE for `run_*` scripts). It does NOT
# authenticate the SSH login itself — fleet always tries key/agent auth
# FIRST for SSH login. If `ssh <host>` prompts you for a password, the host
# will show as `unreachable` in `just fleet-status`. Fix with `ssh-copy-id`
# where possible. If the remote flatly disallows pubkey auth (e.g. corporate/
# IDC sshd with `PubkeyAuthentication no`), set the separate, opt-in
# `ssh_login_password_source` field (example 6 below) — independent of
# `password_source`, since a host's SSH login password may differ from its
# sudo password. See `pitfalls/fleet-apply-password-source-not-for-ssh-login.md`
# for context.
#
# Schema reference: docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md
# Run: `just fleet-apply` (parallel) | `just fleet-apply-dry-run` (chezmoi diff)

[defaults]
chezmoi_path    = "auto"           # "auto" → augment remote PATH with common install dirs
                                   # (~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin,
                                   #  /usr/local/bin, /snap/bin) before invoking `chezmoi`.
                                   # Override per-host with an absolute path (e.g.
                                   # "/snap/bin/chezmoi") to pin a specific binary.
connect_timeout = 15
command_timeout = 1800

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Default: apply to THIS machine (local execution, no SSH).
# Seeded once on `chezmoi apply`; edit freely — chezmoi won't overwrite.
# `no_root_machine` mirrors the chezmoi `.noRoot` prompt from
# .chezmoi.toml.tmpl so this entry stays consistent with how the rest of
# the dotfiles were initialised on this host.
# `password_source` is intentionally omitted: for `local = true` hosts
# fleet_apply.py skips its password gate (chezmoi inherits the parent
# terminal's TTY and prompts for sudo there if needed).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[[hosts]]
name            = "self"
local           = true
no_root_machine = {{ .noRoot }}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Templates for adding REMOTE hosts — uncomment and edit as needed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1) Preferred: ssh_config alias. Inherits ProxyJump, IdentityAgent (e.g.
#    1Password SSH agent), Match blocks — everything you'd get from `ssh lab-box`.
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "lab-box"
# ssh_alias       = "lab-box"
# no_root_machine = false                                   # remote was init'd with noRoot=false
# password_source = { type = "bitwarden", item = "ssh-lab-box-sudo" }

# 2) Explicit connection (no ssh_config entry).
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "vps-tokyo"
# hostname        = "203.0.113.42"
# user            = "dwlee"
# port            = 22
# identity_file   = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
# no_root_machine = true                                    # remote was init'd with noRoot=true
# # password_source omitted → no sudo phase; chezmoi runs as the SSH user only.

# 3) Interactive prompt (asked once at startup, never persisted).
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "office-mac"
# ssh_alias       = "office-mac"
# no_root_machine = false
# password_source = { type = "prompt" }

# 4) Plaintext password (last resort — relies on file mode 0600).
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "throwaway-vm"
# ssh_alias       = "throwaway-vm"
# no_root_machine = false
# password_source = { type = "plain", value = "hunter2" }

# 5) Local execution (this machine, no SSH). Useful when you want
#    `just fleet-apply` to keep the orchestrator itself in sync along
#    with the SSH hosts. ssh_alias / hostname / user / port /
#    identity_file are ignored. Sudo is inherited from the parent
#    terminal (chezmoi may prompt for password if it needs root).
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "self"
# local           = true
# no_root_machine = true                                    # set false if your local apply needs sudo

# 6) SSH LOGIN itself is password-only (e.g. IDC/corporate sshd with
#    `PubkeyAuthentication no` — real trigger: `zyc_friend`, an IDC server
#    whose sshd only offers `keyboard-interactive`/PAM, so even
#    `ssh-copy-id` doesn't help). Opt-in only; every example above keeps
#    today's key/agent-only login behaviour unchanged.
#    `ssh_login_password_source` is INDEPENDENT of `password_source` (that
#    one is sudo-only) — a host's SSH login password may differ from its
#    sudo password. Same 4-way schema as password_source. fleet always
#    tries key/agent auth first; only falls back to password/
#    keyboard-interactive (PAM) auth if that's flatly rejected.
# [[hosts]]
# name                       = "zyc-friend"
# hostname                   = "203.0.113.99"
# user                       = "dwlee"
# no_root_machine            = true
# ssh_login_password_source  = { type = "bitwarden", item = "zyc-friend-ssh-login" }
```

=== bin-migration backlog ===
# Relocate `~/bin/` to a chezmoi-distinct path

**Status**: Done 2026-05-13 — relocated to `~/.dotfiles/bin/` (namespace anchor variant, NOT the `~/.dotfiles-bin/` flat layout originally recommended below).
**Effort**: M (actual: source rename + 12 doc/config references + transitional PATH)
**Related**: `dot_dotfiles/bin/`, `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl:21-26`, `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md`

## Resolution (2026-05-13)

Chosen target: **`~/.dotfiles/bin/`** — `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*` in source.

**Why the namespace variant won over the flat `~/.dotfiles-bin/`**: user signalled
extensibility intent — "這種設計 可能也可以把一些通用的 scripts/ 放過去" — so
future `~/.dotfiles/scripts/`, `~/.dotfiles/lib/`, etc. can grow as siblings inside
the one namespace anchor instead of proliferating top-level hidden dirs
(`~/.dotfiles-bin/`, `~/.dotfiles-lib/`, ...). The name is also tool-agnostic
(no chezmoi-coupling) so renaming the toolchain later doesn't make the path lie.

**Transitional PATH**: `$HOME/.dotfiles/bin:$HOME/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH`.
`$HOME/bin` stays in PATH for one personal sync cycle so any hand-placed
`~/bin/<x>` files keep resolving. After every host has applied the new layout
AND the user has cleaned up old `~/bin/{sms,mi-router,x,sesh-preview,fleet}`,
a follow-up commit drops `$HOME/bin` from PATH entirely.

**Cleanup is manual** (intentionally not automated via run-script): chezmoi
doesn't own non-chezmoi `~/bin/<x>` entries, and an auto-rm could surprise a
user with a same-named binary they placed there. Per host:

```
rm ~/bin/{sms,mi-router,x,sesh-preview,fleet}
rmdir ~/bin 2>/dev/null  # only succeeds if dir is empty
```

## Original context (preserved for reference)

Surfaced 2026-05-13 while adding `bin/executable_fleet` (the umbrella `fleet`
CLI). Currently `bin/executable_*` files in chezmoi deploy to `~/bin/`:

```
bin/executable_sms           → ~/bin/sms
bin/executable_mi-router     → ~/bin/mi-router
bin/executable_x             → ~/bin/x   (also documented at ~/.local/bin/x)
bin/executable_sesh-preview  → ~/bin/sesh-preview
bin/executable_fleet         → ~/bin/fleet  (post 2026-05)
```

`~/bin` is a collision-prone target — third-party installers (Anaconda, asdf,
mise, custom build scripts) sometimes drop binaries there or expect it as
user-writable scratch space. With 5 chezmoi-managed entries and growing, "where
did this binary come from" is harder to answer than it should be.

User question (paraphrased): "can we rename `~/bin` to a more hidden path that
doesn't mix with `~/.local/bin` (which is for auto-installed `uv tool` / `cargo
install` / `mise` output), so it's obvious these are chezmoi-managed?"

## Options

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| **Stay at `~/bin/`** (current) | Zero migration cost; widely understood convention | Collision risk persists; mixes with non-chezmoi binaries |
| **`~/.dotfiles-bin/`** | Prefix telegraphs origin; clean isolation from `.local/bin` | Non-standard XDG; needs PATH update + every doc update |
| **`~/.local/share/chezmoi-bin/`** | XDG-aligned ("data" under chezmoi); explicit ownership | `share/` is conventionally for non-executable data; long path |

Recommended (if/when migrated): `~/.dotfiles-bin/` — the prefix is the whole
point, and `.local/share/` for executables is unusual enough to surprise
future contributors.

## Files affected by any migration

- `bin/executable_sms` / `mi-router` / `x` / `sesh-preview` / `fleet` — rename
  the source dir (`bin/` → e.g. `dot_dotfiles-bin/`)

=== CLAUDE.md conventions greps ===
CLAUDE.md
21:| `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet` / `scripts/fleet/*.py` / `justfile` `fleet-*` recipes / `dot_config/fleet/` / `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` | Three schema pairs break **silently** when only one side changes: `tmux-session-summary.py --json` ↔ `scripts/fleet/tmux.py:_parse_raw`; `executable_pqsum`'s `HostSnapshot`/`GroupRec`/`TaskRec` ↔ `scripts/fleet/pueue.py:_run_pqsum_ai` payload (fleet pipes `pueue status --json` → `pqsum json --raw-stdin` → `pqsum ai --stdin-json`); `scripts/fleet/pueue.py:_REMOTE_CMD` ↔ `scripts/fleet/exec.py:_PATH_PRELUDE`. | [fleet-apply](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md), [pueue](docs/tools/pueue.md), [fleet-exec](docs/tools/fleet-exec.md), [fleet-hosts](docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md) |

Add a row to that § F table, and to [aliases.md](docs/shells/aliases.md) if it ships an `<tool>-update-completion` helper. | § F also records the two existing strategies + the dynamic-candidate pattern |

Keep it lean (pointers over enumerations). | [agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md) § First-party templated skill — incl. the `.chezmoiignore` single-`*` re-include trap |

/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md:330:> **Historical note**: an earlier debugging round assumed `prefix + Space` and `prefix + Enter` were broken because of `extended-keys` / `csi-u` keysym encoding (tmux/tmux#4571, #4147, #4959, #4984), and the menu was moved to `prefix + e` as a workaround. That diagnosis was wrong. The actual failure was that the inline 50-row flat menu was **taller than the terminal**, and tmux silently suppresses oversized menus per `man tmux` ("If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."). Both `Space` and `Enter` were always bindable; the keysym story was a red herring. Full debugging trail in [`pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`](../../../pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md). The menu was bound to both `Space` (canonical) and `e` (alias) for a while; the `e` alias has since been **removed** to free `e` as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal" in the window right-click menu). The canonical binding stays on `prefix + Space`.

571-> Portable loopback-proxy helpers. Honors `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` (+ optional `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` for split Clash `socks-port:` configs). Detection order: env → **macOS System Proxy** (when HTTPEnable and a loopback port is listening — what Clash Verge / CFW "System Proxy" writes) → Clash Verge / mihomo / CFW config files whose declared port is actually open → probe ports `7897/7890/7891/17890/1087/8118/8080`. Preferring System Proxy avoids a stale `~/.config/clash` winning over a live Verge instance on `7897`. Detection is cached per shell; `proxy-off` and `proxy-refresh` clear that cache. Set `$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1` to auto-export env vars on shell startup. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md). See also: [docs/tools/containers.md](../tools/containers.md) for how `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` feeds the chezmoi-managed `~/.docker/config.json` `proxies.default` block. Copilot Node clients need `HTTPS_PROXY` / `--proxy-env` separately — see [docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md](../tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md).

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bats
# Unit tests for pure helpers in
# dot_config/television/executable_lan-scan.sh.
#
# We cover only the functions that are pure string / IP logic — the network
# probes (arp-scan, nmap, ping, dig) are out of scope. Bugs in these pure
# helpers are silent-regression-risk: a mis-filter in `is_usable_ip` silently
# drops real hosts from LAN scans; a mis-normalised MAC prefix silently
# mis-attributes a vendor.
#
# The script dispatches at the bottom (line 325+), so bare `source` runs the
# "all" command and tries to probe the network. Work around by sourcing with
# the `clean` subcommand, pointing XDG_CACHE_HOME at an isolated tempdir so
# clean just wipes our scratch space. After `clean` returns, the function
# definitions are left in scope.

load "../test_helper.bash"

LAN_SCAN="$REPO_ROOT/dot_config/television/executable_lan-scan.sh"

# Build the prologue that sources the script in `clean` mode against an
# isolated cache dir. Call this inside `bash -c "..."` bodies.
_source_prologue() {
  cat <<EOF
export XDG_CACHE_HOME="$BATS_STUB_DIR/tv-cache"
export HOME="$BATS_STUB_DIR/home"
mkdir -p "\$HOME" "\$XDG_CACHE_HOME"
source '$LAN_SCAN' clean >/dev/null 2>&1
set +u
EOF
}

@test "is_usable_ip: accepts normal /24 host addresses" {
  setup_path_stub
  run bash -c "
    $(_source_prologue)
    for ip in 192.168.1.1 192.168.1.50 10.0.0.42 172.16.3.99; do
      if is_usable_ip \"\$ip\"; then echo \"ok:\$ip\"; else echo \"rejected:\$ip\"; fi
    done
  "
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [[ "$output" == *"ok:192.168.1.1"* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *"ok:192.168.1.50"* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *"ok:10.0.0.42"* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *"ok:172.16.3.99"* ]]
  [[ "$output" != *"rejected:"* ]]
}

@test "is_usable_ip: rejects link-local, multicast, broadcast, network" {
  setup_path_stub

# chezmoi managed | grep -n 'README' || true
README.md
NOTES.md
TODO.md

CLAUDE.md
AGENTS.md
GEMINI.md

# Docker and development files
Dockerfile
Dockerfile.*
docker-compose.yml
justfile
.dockerignore

# Repo tooling that must not deploy to $HOME
mkdocs.yml
pyproject.toml
uv.lock
tests
tests/**

# mkdocs build output — regenerated by `uv run mkdocs build` (CLAUDE.md tells
# contributors to run it on doc changes). Repo root IS the chezmoi source root,
# so without this chezmoi would try to deploy every generated file to ~/site/**.
# Already git-ignored via /site/ in .gitignore; this stops chezmoi apply from
# choking on build artifacts when someone builds docs locally.
site
site/**

# curl|sh bootstrap for `dotfiles-init` — lives at repo root so
# `curl … | bash` is a simple one-liner, but it's tooling-for-init,
# not something that should land in $HOME/bootstrap.sh.
# See scripts/init/README.md.
bootstrap.sh

*.txt   # ignore *.txt in the target directory
*/*.txt # ignore *.txt in subdirectories of the target directory
        # but not in subdirectories of subdirectories;
        # so a/b/c.txt would *not* be ignored

*/*.org# # Ignore org-mode backup files that end with `#`

backups/   # ignore the backups folder, but not its contents
backups/** # ignore the contents of backups folder but not the folder itself

docs/** # ignore everything in docs/ and its subdirectories
```

| `Enter` | SSH into the selected host (`fleet hosts NAME`) |
| `Alt+T` | BatchMode SSH probe — does passwordless login actually work? |
| `Alt+S` | `fleet chezmoi status --hosts NAME` (readiness probe for one host) |
| `Alt+I` | `fleet info --hosts NAME` (OS / CPU / memory / disk snapshot) |
| `Alt+P` | `fleet pueue --hosts NAME` (queue summary for one host) |
| `Ctrl+/` | Toggle preview panel (TV builtin) |

The `Alt+` namespace is used (rather than `Ctrl+letter`) to avoid collisions
with tmux's root-table bindings — see
[CLAUDE.md keybinding rule](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/CLAUDE.md).

## Preview pane contents

`fleet hosts --describe NAME` (which the cable shells out to for every
cursor move) prints four sections:

```
# host: lab-box        (defined in: /Users/dwlee/.config/fleet/machines.toml)

connection:
  ssh_alias       lab-box
  user            (from ssh_config)
  hostname        (from ssh_config)
  port            (from ssh_config)
  identity_file   (from ssh_config)

fleet metadata:
  local                false
  no_root_machine      false
  chezmoi_path         auto
  password_source      bitwarden (item=ssh-lab-box-sudo)
  ssh_login_password_source  none
  extra_env            (none)

ssh -G 'lab-box' (resolved by ssh_config):
  hostname 192.0.2.42
  user dwlee
  port 22
  identityfile /Users/dwlee/.ssh/id_ed25519
  proxyjump bastion.example.com

local key check (offline):
  [OK]   /Users/dwlee/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

- The `ssh -G` block is omitted for hosts that don't use an `ssh_alias` —
  for those, the explicit fields in the `connection:` section already are
  the resolved values.
- **Both `password_source` and `ssh_login_password_source` deliberately
  redact `type = "plain"` values**. The TOML file itself is 0600, but the
  preview output scrolls into logs / screenshots; the type label suffices
  for triage.

## Repo conventions for where a new tailscale helper belongs

**The decision boundary observed across the repo:**

**Shell function in `dot_config/shell/NN_*.sh`** — for thin wrappers around an existing binary, ~1–30 lines, no state, no argument parsing beyond `$1`. Numbered-prefix modular files auto-sourced by both bash and zsh via `load_modular_dir`. `50_networking.sh` is the natural home for tailscale wrappers (it already holds `ipgeo`/`vpncheck`/`lanscan`/`tv-lan`/`wifiscan`/`tv-wifi`). Use `.tmpl` only when OS/prompt gating is needed (see `49_homelab.sh.tmpl`, `54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl`). Conventions from the `49_homelab.sh.tmpl` header: `# shellcheck shell=sh`, POSIX-portable, all public functions accept `--help`, internal helpers get a `_prefix_` name, root-needing paths elevate via a single `sudo -v`. **Every new alias/function must get a row in `docs/shells/aliases.md`** (and the `aliases` tv channel picks it up from there).

**In-house CLI in `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_<name>`** — for real programs: subcommand dispatch, JSON output, caching, TUI. Almost all are Python with a **PEP 723 `# /// script` header + `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script`** shebang (see `executable_appsrc`, `executable_fleet`). Deploys to `~/.dotfiles/bin/` (rationale recorded in `backlog/bin-migration.md`). `CLAUDE.md` L28 states the hard requirement: **a new CLI here must ship tab completion for both shells** — `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`, kept in sync, plus a row in `docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md` § F. Also expects a `docs/tools/<name>.md` page and an `mkdocs.yml` nav entry.

**Python module in `scripts/<tool>/*.py`** — only for **multi-module** implementations behind a thin `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_<tool>` dispatcher. Exactly the `fleet` pattern: `executable_fleet` dispatches into `scripts/fleet/{apply,exec,hosts,info,pueue,tmux}.py`, each with its own PEP 723 header. `scripts/adhoc/` is for one-off audits, `scripts/lib/` for shared code.

**Television channel** — a `.toml` in `dot_config/television/cable/` with `[metadata] name/description/requirements`, `[source]`, `[preview]`, `[keybindings]` (Alt+ namespace to dodge tmux/TV conflicts), `[actions.*]` with `mode = "execute"|"fork"`, plus a top-of-file comment block documenting usage/source-cycling/keys. Heavy logic goes into a sibling `dot_config/television/executable_<name>-source.sh` / `-preview.sh` / `.py`, often with a TSV cache under `~/.cache/tv/` and `watch = N.N` for streaming (the `lan-devices` + `lan-scan.sh` pattern). Add `tv-<name>` + scan aliases to `50_networking.sh`, a row in `docs/shells/aliases.md`, and a section in `docs/tools/tv.md`. Use `.toml.tmpl` only if the channel needs OS gating.

**Given the existing footprint, a tailscale utility fits most naturally as:** a `50_networking.sh` function set (`ts-*` / `tsip` / `tsssh`) + a `tailnet` tv channel with a `dot_config/television/executable_tailnet-source.sh` backed by `tailscale status --json`, mirroring `lan-devices` almost exactly. An `executable_tailnet` Python CLI would only be warranted if you need caching, cross-host aggregation, or `--json`/AI-summary output like `fleet`/`pqsum`. Note that a Linux install path would have to be added to ansible first (probably `networking_tools`), since none exists today.

# SSH config & remote-host inventory in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi`

## 1. `ssh-setup-remote` — it is NOT a `bin/` executable

**It's a shell function**, defined at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/96_ssh_setup.sh` (566 lines). Deployed to `~/.config/shell/96_ssh_setup.sh` (confirmed via `chezmoi managed`). It was moved there from `dot_config/zsh/tools/96_ssh_setup.zsh` and de-zsh-ified so both shells can source it.

**Loading**: `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl` both define `load_modular_dir()` with the same signature; zsh calls `load_modular_dir "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell" sh`, so every `dot_config/shell/*.sh` is sourced by both shells at startup.

### CLI interface
```
Usage: ssh-setup-remote [user@]host
```
Exactly one positional arg; no flags. `[ $# -ne 1 ]` → prints usage to stderr, `return 1`.

### Steps (fully interactive — ~10 `read -r` prompts, no `--yes`/non-interactive mode)
- **Step 0** — lists `~/.ssh/*.pub` (portable nullglob: `setopt localoptions nullglob` on zsh / `shopt -s nullglob` + restore on bash), asks "Use an existing key? [Y/n]".
- **Step 0b** — if creating: prompts algorithm (`ed25519` default, also `ed25519-sk`/`rsa`), key name (default `id_${algo}_${remote_host}`), comment (default `${USER}@$(hostname -s) -> ${remote_host}`), passphrase y/N. Runs `ssh-keygen`; adds `-b 4096` for rsa.
- **Step 1** — `ssh-copy-id -i "${key_path}.pub" "$target"`.
- **Step 2** — optional `scp` of the key **pair** to `$target:~/.ssh/`, then `chmod 600/644` remotely; optionally appends a `Host github.com / IdentityFile` block to the *remote's* `~/.ssh/config`.
- **Step 3** — local `~/.ssh/config` wiring. Two modes:
  - **Mode B (alias already configured)** — edits the existing `Host` block *in place*, in whichever file it actually lives in (follows `Include` recursively). Offers `[r]eplace / [a]dd another / [s]kip` for an existing `IdentityFile`, and optional `IdentitiesOnly yes`. Validates with `ssh -G "$alias"` afterwards.
  - **Mode A (new host, or no python3)** — prompts alias / HostName / User / IdentitiesOnly, then **prefers `~/.ssh/config.d/host_${host_alias}`** if that dir exists, else appends to `~/.ssh/config`. `chmod 600`. If it wrote a drop-in that isn't reachable via `Include`, it offers to add one.

### Exit codes
Only `return 1` (usage error, key-not-found, key-already-exists, `ssh-keygen`/`ssh-copy-id`/`scp` failure) and implicit `0`. **No distinct exit codes.**

### The embedded Python helper — this is the most reusable piece for you
`_ssh_cfg_py()` in the same file (lines 33-241) is a heredoc'd `python3 -` script. It is the repo's only real SSH-config parser/editor:

```
find <alias> [keypath]                 kv lines, "---BLOCK---", then the block. rc 0=found, 3=not found
insert <file> <alias> <key> <action> [--identities-only]   action: insert|replace|add, atomic, mode 0600
ensure-include                         rc 0 if ~/.ssh/config.d is reachable via Include, else 1
add-include                            prepend `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` (idempotent)
```
Key properties worth reusing: honours `$SSH_CFG_ROOT` (defaults `~/.ssh/config`), `resolve_includes()` walks `Include` recursively with glob + `~`/relative/absolute expansion and realpath cycle-detection, `write_atomic()` uses `mkstemp` in the same dir + `os.replace` + `chmod 0600`, `tildify()` rewrites `$HOME/...` back to `~/...`, and `block_matches()` deliberately **skips wildcard patterns** (`re.search(r"[*?!]", p)`). Returns **127 when `python3` is absent** so callers fall back to plain append.

**None.** It's absent from the § F table in `docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md` and there is no `*_ssh_setup_completion.*` file. It is documented as a row in `docs/shells/aliases.md:567` (type: `function`) and has a tutorial section at `docs/tutorials/setup_ssh_key_on_remote.md:223` ("Automation: `ssh-setup-remote`").

## 2. SSH config management — yes, `~/.ssh/config` IS chezmoi-managed (create-only)

`git ls-files dot_ssh` → exactly three files:

| Source | Target | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ssh/create_private_config` | `~/.ssh/config` | `create_` = seed once, never overwrite; `private_` = 0600 |
| `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ssh/private_config.d/create_private_00-defaults` | `~/.ssh/config.d/00-defaults` | dir is `private_` (0700) |
| `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ssh/private_config.d/create_private_01_git` | `~/.ssh/config.d/01_git` | |

`chezmoi managed` confirms: `.ssh`, `.ssh/config`, `.ssh/config.d`, `.ssh/config.d/00-defaults`, `.ssh/config.d/01_git`. The live `~/.ssh/config.d/` currently contains exactly `00-defaults` and `01_git`.

- **There is no `private_dot_ssh/`, no `dot_config/ssh/`, and no `modify_`-prefixed SSH file anywhere.** All three are `create_` — meaning **chezmoi will never touch these files again after first apply**. A generator that rewrites SSH config must therefore be a *runtime tool*, not a chezmoi template.
- **The drop-in `~/.ssh/config.d/` pattern is real and load-bearing.** `create_private_config` line 9 is `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` and it is deliberately the **first directive**, documented in its own comments:
  > "To opt a host out, set `ControlMaster no` in a `~/.ssh/config.d/` file: `Include` is the first directive in this file and ssh takes the first-obtained value for each keyword, so config.d always wins."
- Naming convention in `config.d/` is lexical-ordered `NN-name` / `NN_name` (both dash and underscore in use: `00-defaults`, `01_git`). `ssh-setup-remote`'s Mode A writes `host_${host_alias}` (no NN prefix).
- `Host *` in the root config sets `ServerAliveInterval 60`, `ServerAliveCountMax 3`, and **connection multiplexing** — `ControlMaster auto`, `ControlPath ~/.ssh/cm-%C`, `ControlPersist 10m`. (`%C` is used specifically because macOS rejects unix socket paths over ~104 bytes.)

### `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` re SSH
**No SSH-related entries at all** — `grep -n "ssh" .chezmoiignore.tmpl` returns nothing. The critical line for you is **line 93: `scripts/**`** — anything under `scripts/` is never deployed to `$HOME`.

## 3. Fleet host inventory

### Inventory file
`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` → `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`, `create_` + `private_` (0600, seeded once). It's a template only because of `no_root_machine = {{ .noRoot }}`. It ships one real host (`self`, `local = true`) plus six commented example blocks.

### Schema (the parser is `load_hosts()` in `scripts/fleet/apply.py:132`)
`@dataclasses.dataclass class Host` at `scripts/fleet/apply.py:64`:

```python
name: str
ssh_alias: str | None = None
hostname: str | None = None
user: str | None = None
port: int | None = None
identity_file: str | None = None
no_root_machine: bool = False
chezmoi_path: str = "auto"
local: bool = False
extra_env: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
password_source_type / password_source_arg / sudo_password
ssh_login_password_source_type / ssh_login_password_source_arg / ssh_login_password
```

TOML shape: a `[defaults]` table (`chezmoi_path`, `connect_timeout`, `command_timeout`) merged into each `[[hosts]]` (host wins), plus `password_source = { type = "plain"|"prompt"|"bitwarden"|"none", value=|item= }`.

Validation rules in `load_hosts()`:
- `name` required; duplicates raise.
- **Unknown TOML keys are silently dropped**: `host_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(Host)}` then `{k: v for k, v in merged.items() if k in host_fields}` — so adding e.g. a `tailscale_id` field to machines.toml would be discarded unless you add it to `Host`.
- Non-local hosts must have `ssh_alias` **or** `hostname`.

`DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH` (apply.py:107) honours `$FLEET_CONFIG`, else `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`.

### `scripts/fleet/` modules
| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `scripts/fleet/__init__.py` | Re-exports `DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH`, `Host`, `load_hosts`, `connect_host`, `resolve_passwords`, `resolve_ssh_login_passwords`, `_connect_kwargs` from `apply.py` so submodules do `from scripts.fleet import ...` |
| `scripts/fleet/apply.py` | The SSOT: `Host` dataclass, `load_hosts()`, asyncssh connection, `chezmoi update --init` fan-out, readiness/status/tail/compact |
| `scripts/fleet/hosts.py` | **Most relevant to you** — inventory introspection + picker + SSH exec |
| `scripts/fleet/exec.py` | Cross-host argv-list command runner |
| `scripts/fleet/info.py` | Cross-host system snapshot |
| `scripts/fleet/pueue.py` | Cross-host pueue summary |
| `scripts/fleet/tmux.py` | Cross-host tmux session summary |

`hosts.py` is the model for a "generate a list, feed a tv channel" tool. Its output modes: `--list` (plain), `--list-tsv` (`name\ttarget\tkind`), `--list-json`, `--describe NAME`, `--probe NAME`, and bare `NAME` → `os.execvp("ssh", ...)`. Note `_cmd_list_json` defensively pops `sudo_password`/`ssh_login_password` and redacts `type="plain"` args.

Also note `hosts.py`'s docstring explicitly names your problem space:
> "Mirrors `dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml` (which is sourced from `~/.ssh/config`), but reads `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml` instead…"

### `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet`
Deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/fleet`. PEP 723 header (`asyncssh`, `tyro`, `rich`), a `USAGE` string, and `_source_path()` which resolves the chezmoi source dir at runtime via `chezmoi source-path` with a `~/.local/share/chezmoi` fallback — **this is the standard workaround for `scripts/**` being chezmoi-ignored**. It then `sys.path.insert(0, str(src))` and dispatches via a plain dict:
```python
dispatch = {"chezmoi": ..., "edit": ..., "tmux": ..., "info": ..., "pueue": ..., "exec": ..., "hosts": _dispatch_hosts}
```
Each `_dispatch_*` sets `sys.argv = ["fleet hosts", *forwarded]` then imports and calls `main()`.

### `justfile` `fleet-*` recipes (line ~514-631)
`fleet *ARGS` (calls `uv run --script ./dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet`), then direct `./scripts/fleet/apply.py`-backed recipes: `fleet-apply`, `fleet-edit`, `fleet-status`, `fleet-status-quick`, `fleet-apply-dry-run`, `fleet-diff HOST`, `fleet-apply-file PATH`, `fleet-apply-branch`, `fleet-apply-branch-force`, `fleet-apply-one HOST`, `fleet-apply-kill`, `fleet-apply-status`, `fleet-apply-watch`, `fleet-apply-tail HOST`, `fleet-apply-compact`. Note `just fleet-edit` duplicates the seed template that also lives in `executable_fleet:_SEED_TEMPLATE` — a known two-copy drift risk.

## 4. `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` — the model

Full file quoted below (it's 84 lines, no `.tmpl`):

```toml
[metadata]
name = "fleet-hosts"
description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]

[source]
command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"
display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[preview]
command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:connect"
alt-t = "actions:probe"
alt-s = "actions:status"
alt-i = "actions:info"
alt-p = "actions:pueue"

[actions.connect]
description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "execute"
```
The other four actions follow the same shape, each suffixed with `; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _` because `mode = "execute"` returns to the picker.

**Design rule stated in its header comments** (worth honouring in your new channel):
> "The actual TOML parsing lives in Python — this cable shells out to `fleet hosts --list-tsv` / `--describe N` / `N`. So this file stays small and the picker tracks any inventory changes automatically (no parallel TOML parser to keep in sync)."
>
> "Enter lands you in an attach-or-create tmux session (`fleet`) on the remote… That lives in `fleet hosts` itself, NOT here — do not inline an `ssh` invocation into this cable or the two will drift."

**`<mod>+<letter>` convention**: `Alt+` is mandatory for new actions. Stated in the cable header ("Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts"), in `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`, and as a hard rule in `CLAUDE.md:31` ("tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner apps; prefer `Alt+` for new actions"). `CLAUDE.md:22` adds: the paired-TUI rule that a launcher's single-letter `BINDINGS` and the channel's `<mod>+<letter>` actions must use **the same letters**.

Current Alt-key usage across all 48 cables (for picking free letters): `alt-r` ×14, `alt-t` ×13, `alt-c` ×13, `alt-s` ×11, `alt-p` ×10, `alt-e` ×9, `alt-y` ×8, `alt-d` ×6, `alt-o` ×5, `alt-j` ×4, `alt-x/k/i/a` ×3, `alt-m/h/b` ×2, `alt-v/u/n/l/g/f` ×1. `ctrl-y` ×32 is the universal "copy to clipboard (OSC 52)" binding.

**Sibling cable** `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml` is the `~/.ssh/config`-sourced twin: its `[source]` is a shell `for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*` loop piped through `awk` that emits `<source-file>\t<hostname>` and skips wildcard `Host` patterns (`if ($i !~ /[*?]/)`), then `sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2`. Its preview greps `ssh -G` output. Bindings: `enter`=connect, `alt-t`=probe, `alt-a`=offline scan_all.

**Cable channels are auto-discovered** — `channels.toml` awks `~/.config/television/cable/*.toml` for `[metadata] name/description`. No registration file to update.

A good precedent for a *cached, background-refreshed* host list is `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/lan-devices.toml` + `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/executable_lan-scan.sh`: TSV in `~/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv`, `watch = 2.0`, `no_sort = true`, multi-element `command = [...]` arrays for `Ctrl+S` source cycling and `Ctrl+F` preview cycling, and `mode = "fork"` actions that pair with `reload_source`. Its shell aliases are at `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh:87-94` (`lanscan`, `tv-lan`).

## 5. In-house CLI conventions (`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*`)

21 tools. Mix of bash and Python; **every Python one uses PEP 723 inline script metadata** with a `uv run --script` shebang.

**`fleet`** — Python, PEP 723:
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "asyncssh>=2.18",
#   "tyro>=0.9",
#   "rich>=13.9",
# ]
# ///
```
Arg parsing: **hand-rolled dict dispatch** at the umbrella level (`dispatch.get(sub)`), delegating to submodules that use `argparse` (`hosts.py`) or `tyro` (`apply.py`). Big triple-quoted `USAGE` constant printed on `-h`/`--help`/no args; unknown subcommand → prints usage to stderr and returns `2`.

**`mi-router`** — Python, PEP 723 (`tyro`, `httpx`, `rich`, `platformdirs`). Uses **tyro** (Strategy A completion). Credential precedence documented in its docstring: CLI flags → `~/.config/mi-router/config.toml` → env vars → **interactive `getpass` prompt (TTY only; offers to save to config)**. That last one is the repo's canonical interactive-prompt pattern for a Python CLI.

**`pqsum`** — Python, PEP 723 (`rich` only). `argparse` with positional subcommands defaulting to `text`. Interactive prompts via `--clean` (y/N per group) with a `--yes` escape hatch — note the safety design: `--yes` "still only acts on `safe-to-clean`".

**`x`** — plain `#!/usr/bin/env bash` + `set -euo pipefail`, a `usage()` function built from `printf '%s\n' \` with one arg per line, and an `err()` helper (`printf 'x: %s\n' "$*" >&2`).

**`wake`** — `#!/usr/bin/env python3` (deliberately **not** uv/PEP723): *"Pure stdlib (socket + tomllib) — no external dependency, so it works on a fresh box."* `argparse`. Its host list is `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`, seeded by `dot_config/wake/create_private_hosts.toml` — **this is the closest existing template for a new host-inventory-backed CLI**, and it exposes `wake --list-names` purely so its completion function can shell out to it.

**`dotcfg`** — bash wrapper whose header explains the whole `scripts/**`-is-ignored problem and why a thin deployed launcher is the answer.

### Logging
Your intuition is correct. `scripts/lib/log_shared.sh` header states it explicitly:
> "`scripts/**` is listed in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so this file is never deployed to `$HOME`. Its only runtime existence is the inlined copy or a source from the checkout."

Its two consumption mechanisms are (1) `{{ include "scripts/lib/log_shared.sh" }}` inside `run_*.sh.tmpl` chezmoi scripts, (2) `. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/lib/log_shared.sh"` from `scripts/*.sh`. **Neither is available to `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*`.** So the bin CLIs each hand-roll their own tiny output helpers (`err()` in `x`, `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` in the Python ones). `CLAUDE.md:14` codifies this: *"`$HOME`-deployed files can't use it."*

API for reference: `info` / `success` / `warn` / `error` / `skip` / `die`, plus `step` / `hr` / `dim`, plus verification-mode `ok`. Editing it rehashes every `run_onchange_after_*` that inlines it → batch edits.

## 6. Tab completion convention

**Doc**: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md` § F "In-house CLIs (this repo)" (line 140). It's a table of CLI / source / framework / strategy / files, followed by a **decision flow**:

1. tyro → Strategy A (lazy autoload, gen + mtime check, one file in `dot_config/shell/<NN>_<name>.sh`, plus a `<tool>-update-completion` helper in `10_aliases.sh`).
2. argparse → either `argcomplete` + Strategy C, or hand-write Strategy B.
3. Hand-rolled/shell → **Strategy B**: "One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers."
4. Update the § F table + `docs/shells/aliases.md` in the same commit.

### Example pair — `fleet` (NN=45)
`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh` — guard is `(( $+commands[fleet] )) || return 0`, ends with `compdef _fleet fleet`. Structure: dynamic helpers → per-subcommand `_arguments` funcs → top-level `_fleet` with `_arguments -C '1: :->subcommand' '*::arg:->args'` and a `_describe -t subcommands` list.

The dynamic-host pattern you'll want to copy verbatim:
```zsh
_fleet_hosts_one() {
    local -a hosts
    hosts=( ${(f)"$(fleet hosts --list 2>/dev/null)"} )
    (( ${#hosts} )) && _describe -t hosts 'fleet host' hosts
}
_fleet_hosts_csv() {
    local -a hosts
    hosts=( ${(f)"$(fleet hosts --list 2>/dev/null)"} )
    (( ${#hosts} )) && _values -s , 'fleet host' $hosts
}
```

`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/bash/45_fleet_completion.bash` — guard `command -v fleet >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0`, ends `complete -F _fleet_completion fleet`, uses `_init_completion -n =`, `compgen -W`, `COMPREPLY`, `_filedir`. Its CSV helper hand-rolls the `${cur%,*},` / `${cur##*,}` split since bash has no `_values -s ,`. Header says: *"Mirrors dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh — keep both in sync."*

## 7. Tests

**bats only. There is no pytest anywhere** — `pyproject.toml` is docs-build-only (`name = "chezmoi-docs"`, mkdocs deps), and grepping `pytest` across `pyproject.toml`, `justfile`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, and `.github/workflows/*.yml` returns zero hits. No `tests/**/*.py`.

**Layout**:
- `tests/test_helper.bash` — deliberately minimal ("No bats-assert / bats-file / bats-support — plain bats built-ins are enough"). Provides `setup_path_stub` (mktemp dir prepended to `PATH`, exported as `$BATS_STUB_DIR` — *not* via stdout, because command substitution would discard the export), `cleanup_path_stubs`, `REPO_ROOT`, and a default `teardown`.
- `tests/unit/`: `agent_overlays.bats`, `claude_plans_here.bats`, `copilot_proxy.bats`, `ghget.bats`, `lan_scan.bats`, `log_shared.bats`, `x_cli.bats`, `zsh_proxy.bats`.
- `tests/smoke/docker_install.bats`.
- `just bats` → `bats tests/unit`. `just check-all` → `lint bats docker-test`.

**The convention for testing an in-house CLI** — `tests/unit/x_cli.bats` is the template:
```bash
load "../test_helper.bash"
X_BIN="$REPO_ROOT/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x"
setup() { setup_path_stub; X_TMP="$(mktemp -d ...)"; export X_TMP; }
```
It tests the **source-tree file directly** (not the deployed `~/.dotfiles/bin/` copy), and stubs external binaries (`pbcopy`, `osascript`, `uname`) by writing executable shims into `$BATS_STUB_DIR`. `tests/unit/lan_scan.bats` shows how to unit-test a script that dispatches at the bottom: source it with a harmless subcommand (`source '$LAN_SCAN' clean`) against an isolated `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, then the function definitions remain in scope.

**Note the gap**: there is **no test for `ssh-setup-remote`**, none for `fleet hosts`, and none for any `dot_config/shell/*.sh` function. Lint coverage: `just lint-shell` runs shellcheck over `dot_config/shell/*.sh dot_config/bash/*.bash scripts/*.sh scripts/lib/*.sh` at `--severity=warning`; the pre-commit hook `shellcheck-shared` (`files: '^dot_config/(shell/[^/]+\.sh|bash/[^/]+\.bash)$'`) runs errors-only. **`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*` is not shellcheck'd at all.**

## Things that will bite your Tailscale utility

1. **`~/.ssh/config` and `config.d/*` are `create_`-only.** chezmoi seeds them once and then never touches them. Your generator must write at runtime, into `~/.ssh/config.d/<something>` — that directory already exists, is 0700, is `Include`d as the *first* directive of the root config (so it wins every keyword), and is loaded in lexical order. Taken names: `00-defaults`, `01_git`.
2. **`scripts/**` is chezmoi-ignored (`.chezmoiignore.tmpl:93`)**, so any Python module you put there is only reachable through the `_source_path()` → `chezmoi source-path` trick used by `executable_fleet`, or by inlining. That also means `scripts/lib/log_shared.sh` is unavailable to a deployed `~/.dotfiles/bin/` binary.
3. **`load_hosts()` silently drops unknown TOML keys** (`k in host_fields`), so a `tailscale_*` field in `machines.toml` will vanish unless you extend the `Host` dataclass.
4. `_ssh_cfg_py` in `96_ssh_setup.sh` already solves recursive-`Include` resolution, atomic 0600 writes, `~`-tildification, and wildcard-`Host` skipping. Duplicating that logic in a new tool creates a third SSH-config parser (the second being the `awk` in `ssh-config.toml`'s source command).
5. **Tailscale is currently install-only in this repo** — `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`, a `tailscale-app` Homebrew cask row in `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md`, a `tskey-` rule in `.gitleaks.toml:116`, and a `Tailscale IP or domain` comment in `docs/tools/ssh-agent.md:170`. There is **no existing Tailscale CLI, tv channel, or inventory integration**. (Though a live `~/.ssh/cm-yczhang@100.109.48.79:22` ControlMaster socket shows the `100.64.0.0/10` range is already in daily use.)
6. **`CLAUDE.md:21` will require you to update mirrors** if you touch `executable_fleet` / `scripts/fleet/*.py` / `justfile fleet-*` / `dot_config/fleet/` / `cable/fleet-hosts.toml`. `CLAUDE.md:28` requires both completion files + the § F table row + an `aliases.md` row for any new `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*`. `CLAUDE.md:15` requires an `mkdocs.yml` nav entry for any new `docs/**/*.md` plus `uv run mkdocs build --strict`. `CLAUDE.md:29` requires touching `dot_agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles/SKILL.md.tmpl` if you name a stable new CLI.

36	import os, re, sys, glob, pathlib, tempfile

56	def resolve_includes(start):

59	    def walk(path):

102	        i = 0

104	            if block_matches(lines[i], alias):

124	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as fh:

126	        os.replace(tmp, str(f))
127	        os.chmod(str(f), 0o600)
128	    except BaseException:

130	            os.unlink(tmp)
131	        except OSError:
132	            pass

154	    if not res:

254	    return 1

257	  local target="$1"
258	  local remote_user remote_host

261	    remote_host="${target#*@}"
262	  else
263	    remote_host="$target"
264	    remote_user=""
265	  fi

270	  local key_path=""

272

274	
275	  # Portable nullglob: in zsh, `*.pub(N)` made the glob expand to nothing
276	  # when nothing matched. shopt -s nullglob (bash) / setopt nullglob (zsh)
277	  # is the equivalent.
278	  local -a existing_keys
279	  existing_keys=()
280	  if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
281	    setopt localoptions nullglob
282	  else

293	  # Restore bash nullglob; zsh is already locally scoped via setopt localoptions.
294	  if [ -n "$BASH_VERSION" ]; then
295	    eval "$_had_nullglob"
296	  fi
297	
298	  if (( ${#existing_keys[@]} > 0 )); then

325	    local algo_input
326	    read -r algo_input
327	    [ -n "$algo_input" ] && algo="$algo_input"
328	
329	    # Key name
330	    local key_name="id_${algo}_${remote_host}"
331	    printf 'Key name [%s]: ' "$key_name"
332	    local name_input
333	    read -r name_input
334	    [ -n "$name_input" ] && key_name="$name_input"
335	    key_path="$HOME/.ssh/$key_name"
336	
337	    if [ -f "$key_path" ]; then
338	      printf '%s\n' "Key already exists: $key_path" >&2
339	      return 1
340	    fi
341	
342	    # Comment
343	    local comment="${USER}@$(hostname -s) -> ${remote_host}"
344	    printf 'Comment [%s]: ' "$comment"
345	    local comment_input
346	    read -r comment_input
347	    [ -n "$comment_input" ] && comment="$comment_input"
348	
349	    # Passphrase
350	    local -a passphrase_flag
351	    passphrase_flag=()
352	    printf 'Set a passphrase? [y/N] '
353	    local use_pass
354	    read -r use_pass
355	    if [[ "$use_pass" =~ ^[Yy] ]]; then
356	      # Let ssh-keygen prompt for it

358	    else
359	      passphrase_flag=(-N "")
360	    fi
361	
362	    # Generate

365	    [ "$algo" = "rsa" ] && keygen_args+=(-b 4096)

367	    printf '\n> ssh-keygen %s\n' "${keygen_args[*]}"
368	    ssh-keygen "${keygen_args[@]}" || return 1

370	  fi

372	  # ── Step 1: ssh-copy-id ────────────────────────────────────────────────
373	  printf '\n--- Copy public key to %s ---\n' "$target"
374	  printf 'Run ssh-copy-id to enable passwordless login? [Y/n] '
375	  local do_copy

383	  fi

385	  # ── Step 2: Copy key pair to remote ────────────────────────────────────
386	  printf '\n--- Copy key pair to remote ---\n'

388	  printf 'Copy private+public key to %s:~/.ssh/? [y/N] ' "$target"

414	  printf '\n--- Local SSH config ---\n'

440	          key_present)        key_present="$_v" ;;
441	        esac
442	      done <<EOF
443	$kv
444	EOF

447	      printf '%s\n' "$block"

449	      if [ "$key_present" = "1" ]; then

482	        fi
483	      fi

489	      read -r alias_input
490	      [ -n "$alias_input" ] && host_alias="$alias_input"
491

504	      printf 'Add IdentitiesOnly yes? [y/N] '

1	# Custom SSH config channel for television (tv)
2	# Parses Host entries from ~/.ssh/config AND ~/.ssh/config.d/* (Include support).
3	# The community ssh-hosts channel only reads ~/.ssh/config directly.
4	#
5	# Each entry shows which file the host is defined in, so duplicates across
6	# config.d/* are easy to spot. The output (what gets passed to ssh / actions)
7	# is just the bare hostname.
8	#
9	# Usage:
10	#   tv ssh-config
11	#
12	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
13	#   Enter      SSH into selected host
14	#   Alt+T      Online probe: BatchMode=yes test (does pubkey login actually work?)
15	#   Alt+A      Offline batch scan: list every host + whether a local key file exists
16	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
17	#
18	# Preview shows resolved config via `ssh -G` plus a local-key existence check
19	# (no network — just stat the IdentityFile paths).
20	
21	[metadata]
22	name = "ssh-config"
23	description = "SSH hosts (with Include config.d/* support)"
24	requirements = ["ssh", "awk", "sort"]
25	
26	[source]
27	# Emit "<source-file>\t<hostname>" so the picker shows the origin file but
28	# actions still receive a clean hostname via {split:\t:1}.
29	command = """
30	for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
31	  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
32	  rel=${f#$HOME/}
33	  awk -v src="$rel" '
34	    /^[[:space:]]*Host[[:space:]]/ {
35	      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
36	        if ($i !~ /[*?]/) printf "%s\\t%s\\n", src, $i
37	      }
38	    }' "$f"
39	done | sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2
40	"""
41	display = "{split:\\t:1}  ({split:\\t:0})"
42	output = "{split:\\t:1}"
43	
44	[preview]
45	command = """
46	host='{split:\\t:1}'
47	src='{split:\\t:0}'
48	echo "# defined in: $src"
49	echo
50	ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^(host|hostname|user|port|identityfile|proxycommand|proxyjump|forwardagent|identityagent|localforward|remoteforward)[[:space:]]'
51	echo
52	echo '--- local key check (offline) ---'
53	found=0
54	while IFS= read -r f; do
55	  [ -z "$f" ] && continue
56	  case "$f" in '~/'*) f="$HOME/${f#'~/'}";; '~') f="$HOME";; esac
57	  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
58	    echo "  [OK]   $f"
59	    found=1
60	  else
61	    echo "  [miss] $f"
62	  fi
63	done <<EOF
64	$(ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^identityfile / {print $2}')
65	EOF
66	if [ "$found" -eq 0 ]; then
67	  echo
68	  echo '  => no IdentityFile present locally — password login likely required'
69	  echo '     (or relies on ssh-agent / IdentityAgent — try Alt+T to probe)'
70	fi
71	"""
72	
73	[keybindings]
74	enter = "actions:connect"
75	alt-t = "actions:probe"
76	alt-a = "actions:scan_all"
77	
78	[actions.connect]
79	description = "SSH into the selected host"
80	command = "ssh '{split:\\t:1}'"
81	mode = "execute"
82	
83	[actions.probe]
84	description = "Probe selected host with BatchMode (no password prompt allowed)"
85	command = """
86	host='{split:\\t:1}'
87	echo "# Probing $host with BatchMode=yes (ConnectTimeout=3)"
88	echo "# Exit 0 = passwordless login works; non-zero = needs password / unreachable / key not authorized"
89	echo
90	ssh -o BatchMode=yes \\
91	    -o ConnectTimeout=3 \\
92	    -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \\
93	    -o PreferredAuthentications=publickey,hostbased,gssapi-with-mic \\
94	    "$host" true
95	rc=$?
96	echo
97	case $rc in
98	  0)   echo "[OK] passwordless login works for '$host'" ;;
99	  255) echo "[FAIL] connection / auth error (exit 255) — needs password, key not authorized, or host unreachable" ;;
100	  *)   echo "[FAIL] remote command failed (exit $rc) — auth probably OK but 'true' failed" ;;
101	esac
102	echo
103	echo '[Press Enter to exit]'
104	read -r _
105	"""
106	mode = "execute"
107	
108	[actions.scan_all]
109	description = "Offline scan: for every host, check if any IdentityFile exists locally"
110	command = """
111	echo "# Scanning all hosts (offline — no network) ..."
112	echo "# Legend: [OK] = at least one IdentityFile present locally"
113	echo "#         [--] = no key file on disk (password / agent / unconfigured)"
114	echo
115	for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
116	  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
117	  rel=${f#$HOME/}
118	  awk -v src="$rel" '
119	    /^[[:space:]]*Host[[:space:]]/ {
120	      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
121	        if ($i !~ /[*?]/) printf "%s\\t%s\\n", src, $i
122	      }
123	    }' "$f"
124	done | sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2 | while IFS=$'\\t' read -r src host; do
125	  keyline=""
126	  found=0
127	  while IFS= read -r kf; do
128	    [ -z "$kf" ] && continue
129	    case "$kf" in '~/'*) kf="$HOME/${kf#'~/'}";; '~') kf="$HOME";; esac
130	    if [ -f "$kf" ]; then
131	      keyline="$kf"
132	      found=1
133	      break
134	    fi
135	  done <<EOF
136	$(ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^identityfile / {print $2}')
137	EOF
138	  if [ "$found" -eq 1 ]; then
139	    printf '  [OK] %-28s %-22s -> %s\\n' "$host" "($src)" "$keyline"
140	  else
141	    printf '  [--] %-28s %-22s    (no local key)\\n' "$host" "($src)"
142	  fi
143	done
144	echo
145	echo '[Press Enter to exit]'
146	read -r _
147	"""
148	mode = "execute"
149

107	# starting/stopping the proxy.

109	# Environment variables honored:
110	#   LOCAL_PROXY_URL         HTTP/HTTPS proxy URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7890).

129	  "$HOME/Library/Application Support/io.github.clash-verge-rev.clash-verge-rev/config.yaml"
130	  "$HOME/Library/Application Support/io.github.clash-verge-rev.clash-verge-rev/clash-verge.yaml"
131	  "$HOME/.config/mihomo/config.yaml"
132	  "$HOME/.config/clash/config.yaml"
133	  "$HOME/.config/clash/config.yml"
134	  "$HOME/Library/Application Support/clash/config.yaml"
135	  "$HOME/Library/Application Support/clash/config.yml"
136	)

138	__net_clear_proxy_cache() {
139	  _NET_PROXY_CACHE=""
140	  _NET_PROXY_SOCKS_CACHE=""
141	  _NET_PROXY_SOURCE_CACHE=""
142	}
143	
144	__net_set_proxy_cache() {
145	  _NET_PROXY_CACHE="$1"
146	  _NET_PROXY_SOCKS_CACHE="$2"
147	  _NET_PROXY_SOURCE_CACHE="$3"
148	}
149	
150	__net_port_open() {
151	  nc -z -w1 127.0.0.1 "$1" 2>/dev/null
152	}
153	
154	__net_find_clash_config() {
155	  local candidate
156	  for candidate in "${__NET_PROXY_CLASH_CONFIG_CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
157	    if [[ -f "$candidate" ]]; then
158	      printf '%s\n' "$candidate"

160	    fi
161	  done
162	  return 1
163	}
164	
165	__net_yaml_scalar() {
166	  local key="$1"
167	  local config_path="$2"
168	  awk -v key="$key" '
169	    {
170	      line = $0
171	      sub(/\r$/, "", line)
172	      if (line ~ /^[[:space:]]*#/) {
173	        next
174	      }
175	      sub(/[[:space:]]+#.*/, "", line)
176	      if (line ~ "^[[:space:]]*" key ":[[:space:]]*") {
177	        sub("^[[:space:]]*" key ":[[:space:]]*", "", line)
178	        gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", line)
179	        gsub(/^["'"'"']|["'"'"']$/, "", line)
180	        print line
181	        exit
182	      }
183	    }
184	  ' "$config_path"
185	}

187	# macOS: honor the *active* System Settings proxy when it points at a live
188	# loopback port. Clash Verge / CFW "System Proxy" writes here; Node/bun do NOT
189	# read it — only curl/scutil consumers do — but it is still the best signal of
190	# which local port the user intends right now (beats a stale ~/.config/clash).
191	__net_detect_system_proxy() {
192	  command -v scutil >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
193	  local host port enable
194	  enable="$(command scutil --proxy 2>/dev/null | command awk '/HTTPEnable/ {print $3; exit}')"
195	  [[ "$enable" == "1" ]] || return 1
196	  host="$(command scutil --proxy 2>/dev/null | command awk '/HTTPProxy/ {print $3; exit}')"
197	  port="$(command scutil --proxy 2>/dev/null | command awk '/HTTPPort/ {print $3; exit}')"
198	  [[ -n "$host" && -n "$port" ]] || return 1
199	  # Only auto-trust loopback / explicit local proxies — never silently route
200	  # shell helpers through a remote corporate proxy discovered via scutil.
201	  case "$host" in
202	    127.0.0.1|localhost|::1) ;;
203	    *) return 1 ;;
204	  esac
205	  __net_port_open "$port" || return 1
206	  __net_set_proxy_cache \
207	    "http://127.0.0.1:$port" \
208	    "socks5://127.0.0.1:$port" \
209	    "macOS system proxy"
210	  return 0
211	}
212	
213	__net_detect_clash_proxy() {
214	  local config_path mixed_port http_port socks_port socks_url="" source_label
215	  # Prefer a config whose declared port is *actually listening* — an old CFW
216	  # yaml sitting next to a live Verge instance used to win and report a dead
217	  # 7891 while traffic was on 7897.
218	  local candidate
219	  for candidate in "${__NET_PROXY_CLASH_CONFIG_CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
220	    [[ -f "$candidate" ]] || continue
221	    config_path="$candidate"
222	    source_label="clash/mihomo config"
223	    case "$candidate" in
224	      *clash-verge*) source_label="clash-verge config" ;;
225	      */mihomo/*)    source_label="mihomo config" ;;
226	    esac
227	
228	    mixed_port="$(__net_yaml_scalar "mixed-port" "$config_path")"
229	    if [[ -n "$mixed_port" ]] && __net_port_open "$mixed_port"; then
230	      __net_set_proxy_cache \
231	        "http://127.0.0.1:$mixed_port" \
232	        "socks5://127.0.0.1:$mixed_port" \
233	        "$source_label"
234	      return 0
235	    fi
236	
237	    http_port="$(__net_yaml_scalar "port" "$config_path")"
238	    socks_port="$(__net_yaml_scalar "socks-port" "$config_path")"
239	    if [[ -n "$http_port" ]] && __net_port_open "$http_port"; then
240	      socks_url=""
241	      if [[ -n "$socks_port" ]] && __net_port_open "$socks_port"; then
242	        socks_url="socks5://127.0.0.1:$socks_port"
243	      fi
244	      __net_set_proxy_cache \
245	        "http://127.0.0.1:$http_port" \
246	        "$socks_url" \
247	        "$source_label"
248	      return 0
249	    fi
250	  done
251	
252	  return 1
253	}
254	
255	__net_detect_proxy() {
256	  if [[ -n "$LOCAL_PROXY_URL" ]]; then
257	    __net_set_proxy_cache \
258	      "$LOCAL_PROXY_URL" \
259	      "$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL" \
260	      "LOCAL_PROXY_URL env"
261	    return 0
262	  fi
263	  # Cache hit (including cached "none") — skip re-probe until proxy-refresh.
264	  if [[ -n "$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" ]]; then
265	    [[ "$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]] && return 1
266	    return 0
267	  fi
268	  if __net_detect_system_proxy; then
269	    return 0
270	  fi
271	  if __net_detect_clash_proxy; then
272	    return 0
273	  fi
274	  local port
275	  for port in "${__NET_PROXY_PROBE_PORTS[@]}"; do
276	    if __net_port_open "$port"; then
277	      __net_set_proxy_cache "http://127.0.0.1:$port" "socks5://127.0.0.1:$port" "probe"
278	      return 0
279	    fi
280	  done
281	  __net_set_proxy_cache "none" "" "probe"
282	  return 1
283	}
284	
285	# Resolve the URL that should be used for ALL_PROXY / all_proxy.
286	# Falls back to the HTTP proxy when no SOCKS-specific URL is set (works for
287	# mixed-port Clash configs where one port serves both HTTP and SOCKS).
288	__net_all_proxy_url() {
289	  if [[ -n "$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL" ]]; then
290	    printf '%s\n' "$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL"

292	    printf '%s\n' "$_NET_PROXY_SOCKS_CACHE"
293	  else
294	    printf '%s\n' "$_NET_PROXY_CACHE"
295	  fi
296	}
297	
298	# Run one command with proxy env applied to the child process only.
299	withproxy() {
300	  __net_detect_proxy
301	  if [[ "$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]]; then
302	    "$@"
303	    return
304	  fi
305	  local all_url
306	  all_url="$(__net_all_proxy_url)"
307	  http_proxy="$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
308	  https_proxy="$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
309	  HTTP_PROXY="$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
310	  HTTPS_PROXY="$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
311	  ALL_PROXY="$all_url" \
312	  all_proxy="$all_url" \
313	    "$@"
314	}
315	
316	# Run direct first; on non-zero exit, retry via proxy if one is available.
317	try_direct_then_proxy() {
318	  "$@" && return 0

322	    return $rc
323	  fi

325	  withproxy "$@"

328	# Export proxy env vars to the current shell (all downstream commands inherit).

342	         HTTP_PROXY="$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
343	         HTTPS_PROXY="$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
344	         ALL_PROXY="$all_url" \
345	         all_proxy="$all_url"

362	# Report current proxy state: active / available / unavailable.

384	  [[ -n "$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL" ]] && all_source="LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL env"
385	
386	  printf '%s\n' "proxy: $state http=$_NET_PROXY_CACHE  source=$source  $hint"
387	  if [[ -n "$all_url" && "$all_url" != "$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" ]]; then
388	    printf '%s\n' "  socks=$all_url  source=$all_source"
389	  fi
390	}
391	
392	# Validate that the detected proxy can actually reach the public internet.
393	# ICMP ping does not honor proxy env vars, so use Google's HTTP 204 endpoint.
394	proxy-test() {
395	  local url="${1:-https://www.google.com/generate_204}"
396	  if ! command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
397	    printf '%s\n' "proxy-test: curl not found" >&2
398	    return 127
399	  fi
400	
401	  __net_detect_proxy
402	  if [[ "$_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]]; then
403	    printf '%s\n' "proxy-test: no proxy detected (set \$LOCAL_PROXY_URL or start your proxy, then \`proxy-refresh\`)" >&2
404	    return 1
405	  fi
406	
407	  local all_url
408	  all_url="$(__net_all_proxy_url)"
409	  printf '%s\n' "proxy-test: http=$_NET_PROXY_CACHE  all=$all_url  url=$url"
410	  withproxy curl -sS -o /dev/null \
411	    -w 'proxy-test: http=%{http_code} remote=%{remote_ip} total=%{time_total}s\n' \
412	    --max-time 10 "$url"
413	}
414	
415	# Clear the cached detection and re-probe; call after toggling your proxy.
416	proxy-refresh() {
417	  __net_clear_proxy_cache
418	  __net_detect_proxy
419	  proxy-status
420	}
421	
422	# Optional auto-activation: when $LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1 is set before
423	# this file is sourced, silently call `proxy-on` if a proxy is detected.
424	# Set the env var in a machine-local shell file (or ~/.zshenv / ~/.profile) on
425	# machines that should always route through the loopback proxy.
426	if [[ "$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE" == "1" ]]; then
427	  proxy-on -q
428	fi
429	
430	# --- Rootless Docker socket ---
431	# Point the Docker CLI at the user-scoped socket when rootless Docker is
432	# installed. Without this, `docker` defaults to /var/run/docker.sock (the
433	# rootful path) and fails with "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon".
434	# Guarded on socket existence so this is a no-op on:
435	#   - macOS (OrbStack / Docker Desktop publish their own sockets, don't need this)
436	#   - Linux boxes still running rootful Docker (the rootful socket is under /var/run)
437	# Respect a pre-existing $DOCKER_HOST so a user-set value wins.
438	# See docs/tools/container-config-map.md for the full install-variant map.
439	if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Linux" && -z "$DOCKER_HOST" ]]; then
440	  _net_xdg_runtime="${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/run/user/$UID}"
441	  if [[ -S "${_net_xdg_runtime}/docker.sock" ]]; then
442	    export DOCKER_HOST="unix://${_net_xdg_runtime}/docker.sock"
443	  fi
444	  unset _net_xdg_runtime
445	fi
446

8	
9	> Standalone > App Store
10	
11	## How this repo installs it (macOS)
12	
13	- **GUI app + daemon** → `cask "tailscale-app"` in [`Brewfile.darwin`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl) — the **macsys standalone** build (`io.tailscale.ipn.macsys`), whose **system extension** is the daemon. Previously `mas "Tailscale"`, but Tailscale was **delisted from the Mac App Store**, so `mas` install now fails; the cask is the supported path.
14	- **CLI on PATH** → **also from the cask**, not a separate formula: the pkg installs `/usr/local/bin/tailscale`, a shell wrapper into the app bundle (`exec /Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/tailscale "$@"`). Do **not** also install the standalone `brew "tailscale"` formula — it's redundant and fights the cask over that same path on every upgrade (ollama-style link conflict) while shipping a `tailscaled` the app already runs.
15	- **Never** `brew services start tailscale` on macOS: the app's system extension already *is* the daemon; a second `tailscaled` would conflict.
16	
17	### "Another Tailscale copy was found on this Mac"
18	
19	If the debug panel reports a conflict at `/Applications/Tailscale.localized/Tailscale.app` (often alongside `DNS Unavailable` / `dns-forward-failing`), that's the **old App Store build left behind** by the `mas → cask` migration (`chezmoi apply` is install-only and won't remove it). Fix:
20	
21	```bash
22	sudo rm -rf /Applications/Tailscale.localized   # deletes only the idle App Store copy
23	```
24	
25	Full detection + root cause: [`pitfalls/tailscale-another-copy-app-store-leftover.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/tailscale-another-copy-app-store-leftover.md).

17	    # subsequent session to the same (host, port, user). The win scales with
18	    # round-trip time and with how many short-lived SSH sessions a workflow
19	    # opens: `fleet` fan-out, git over ssh, rsync loops, and any mobile /
20	    # tethered / cross-continent link.

22	    # ControlPath uses %C (a hash of host+port+user+local host) so no socket
23	    # directory has to exist — sockets land as ~/.ssh/cm-<hash>. That also
24	    # keeps the path short, which matters: a unix socket path over ~104 bytes
25	    # is rejected on macOS.

27	    # Gotchas worth knowing before debugging something weird:
28	    # - Forwarding options (-A, -L, -R, -X) are taken from the FIRST connection
29	    #   that opened the master. A later `ssh -L …` to the same host silently
30	    #   rides the existing master without the forward. Use `-o ControlMaster=no`
31	    #   for that one-off, or drop the master first.
32	    # - `ssh -O check <host>` asks whether a master is live; `ssh -O exit <host>`

Each item carries two tags:

- **Priority**: `P1` (next likely batch) · `P2` (worth doing) · `P3` (someday) · `P?` (needs evaluation first — spike before committing)
- **Effort**: `S` (< 1h) · `M` (half day) · `L` (multi-day) · `XL` (architectural, design doc first)

A trailing `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)` link means the item has accompanying
investigation, design notes, or paused troubleshooting — read that first before
re-investigating. Items without a link are simple enough to act on directly.

with a one-line summary of what shipped.

# Backlog Research

Long-form research, design notes, and paused troubleshooting for items listed in
[`../TODO.md`](../TODO.md). One file per topic, named with a slug that matches
the TODO entry.

## Why this exists

`TODO.md` is the **index** — short titles with priority/effort tags. This folder
is the **knowledge base** — the actual investigation, options considered,
benchmarks, error messages, and decisions that informed the TODO entry. The goal
is **resume-friendliness**: when you (or an agent) come back to an item three
months later, the doc here lets you pick up in 5 minutes instead of re-running
30 minutes of investigation.

This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `backlog/**`) — it
is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.

## When to add a doc here

Add a `backlog/<slug>.md` file when **any** of these apply:

- The TODO item carries a `P?` tag (it requires evaluation; record what was tried)
- You did meaningful troubleshooting but didn't ship a fix (capture the trace
  before it evaporates)
- Multiple options were considered (record the trade-offs, not just the winner)
- An external blocker exists (waiting on upstream release, host availability)
- The implementation is `[L]` or `[XL]` (architectural; needs design before code)

`[S]` items rarely need a doc unless there's surprising context.

## When NOT to add a doc here

- Item is `[S]` and obvious (e.g., "change a TOML key") — just put the file path
  in the TODO entry
- Already covered by a `docs/this_repo/*.md` or `docs/tools/*.md` page
  (cross-link instead, that's user-facing reference)
- Speculation only ("would be cool to...") with no investigation — keep it as a
  one-liner in `TODO.md` first; promote to a doc when you actually look into it
