```text
118	
119	class MiRouter:
120	    def __init__(self, host: str, username: str, password: str, timeout: float = 5.0):
121	        self.base = f"http://{host}"
122	        self.username = username
123	        self.password = password
124	        # LAN device — ignore ambient HTTP(S)/SOCKS proxy env (ALL_PROXY etc.);
125	        # otherwise httpx routes LAN traffic through the proxy and, with a
126	        # socks:// URL, crashes since httpx has no SOCKS support by default.
127	        self.client = httpx.Client(timeout=timeout, follow_redirects=False, trust_env=False)
128	        self.stok: str | None = None
129	
130	    def login(self) -> None:
131	        r = self.client.get(f"{self.base}/cgi-bin/luci/web")
132	        r.raise_for_status()
133	        m_key = KEY_RE.search(r.text)
134	        m_mac = MAC_RE.search(r.text)
135	        if not m_key or not m_mac:
136	            raise RuntimeError("could not parse login key/mac from router page")
137	        key = m_key.group(1)
138	        mac = m_mac.group(1)
139	        nonce = f"0_{mac}_{int(time.time())}_{random.randint(1000, 10000)}"
140	        pwd_key = hashlib.sha1((self.password + key).encode()).hexdigest()
141	        pwd_hash = hashlib.sha1((nonce + pwd_key).encode()).hexdigest()
142	        r = self.client.post(
143	            f"{self.base}/cgi-bin/luci/api/xqsystem/login",
144	            data={
145	                "username": self.username,
146	                "password": pwd_hash,
147	                "logtype": "2",
148	                "nonce": nonce,
149	            },
150	        )
151	        r.raise_for_status()
152	        body = r.json()
153	        if body.get("code") != 0 or not body.get("token"):
154	            raise RuntimeError(f"login failed: {body}")
155	        self.stok = body["token"]
156	
157	    def api(self, endpoint: str) -> Any:
158	        if self.stok is None:
159	            self.login()
160	        url = (
161	            f"{self.base}/cgi-bin/luci/;stok={self.stok}"
162	            f"/api/{endpoint.lstrip('/')}"
163	        )
164	        r = self.client.get(url)
165	        if r.status_code == 404:
166	            return {"_error": "endpoint not registered (404)", "endpoint": endpoint}
167	        r.raise_for_status()
168	        try:
169	            return r.json()
170	        except ValueError:
171	            return {"_unregistered_or_non_json": True, "preview": r.text[:200]}

428	def show_endpoints(r: "MiRouter | None", check: bool) -> None:
429	    title = "Known-good MiWiFi GET endpoints"
430	    if check:
431	        title += " (live-probed)"
432	        assert r is not None  # main() guarantees a logged-in client when check=True
433	
434	    t = Table(title=title)
435	    t.add_column("category", style="bold cyan")
436	    t.add_column("endpoint")
437	    if check:
438	        t.add_column("status")
439	    t.add_column("description")

441	    for cat, ep, desc in ENDPOINTS:
442	        row = [cat, ep]
443	        if check:
444	            try:
445	                url = f"{r.base}/cgi-bin/luci/;stok={r.stok}/api/{ep}"
446	                resp = r.client.get(url, timeout=3)
447	                code = resp.status_code
448	                if code == 200:
449	                    try:
450	                        body = resp.json()
451	                        api_code = body.get("code") if isinstance(body, dict) else None
452	                        if api_code in (None, 0):
453	                            status = f"[green]{code}[/green]"
454	                        else:
455	                            status = f"[yellow]{code}[/yellow] code={api_code}"
456	                    except ValueError:
457	                        status = f"[green]{code}[/green] non-json"
458	                else:
459	                    status = f"[red]{code}[/red]"
460	            except Exception:
461	                status = "[red]err[/red]"
462	            row.append(status)
463	        row.append(desc)
464	        t.add_row(*row)
465	
466	    console.print(t)
467	    console.print()
468	    console.print("[dim]Usage:[/dim] mi-router raw <endpoint>")

480	@dataclass
481	class Args:
482	    """Read-only CLI for MiWiFi routers."""
483	
484	    cmd: Cmd
485	    host: str | None = None
486	    """Router IP / hostname (overrides config + env)."""
487	    username: str | None = None
488	    """Admin username (overrides config + env)."""
489	    password: str | None = None
490	    """Admin password (overrides config + env; will prompt if missing)."""
491	    timeout: float = 5.0
492	    """HTTP timeout in seconds."""
493	
494	
495	def main() -> None:
496	    args = tyro.cli(Args, config=(tyro.conf.OmitSubcommandPrefixes,))
497	    cmd = args.cmd
498	
499	    # `endpoints` without --check is a static catalog — no router round-trip
500	    # (and no credential prompt) needed.
501	    needs_router = not (isinstance(cmd, Endpoints) and not cmd.check)
502	
503	    r: MiRouter | None = None
504	    if needs_router:
505	        creds = resolve_creds(args.host, args.username, args.password)
506	        r = MiRouter(creds["host"], creds["user"], creds["password"], timeout=args.timeout)
507	        try:
508	            r.login()
509	        except Exception as e:
510	            die(f"login failed: {e}")
511	
512	    if isinstance(cmd, Info):
513	        show_info(r)
514	    elif isinstance(cmd, Wifi):
515	        show_wifi(r, cmd.show_passwords)
516	    elif isinstance(cmd, Devices):
517	        show_devices(r, cmd.online_only)
518	    elif isinstance(cmd, Mdns):
519	        show_mdns(r)
520	    elif isinstance(cmd, All):
521	        show_info(r)
522	        console.print()
523	        show_wifi(r, False)
524	        console.print()
525	        show_devices(r, True)
526	        console.print()
527	        show_mdns(r)
528	    elif isinstance(cmd, Raw):
529	        show_raw(r, cmd.endpoint)
530	    elif isinstance(cmd, Endpoints):
531	        show_endpoints(r, cmd.check)
532	    elif isinstance(cmd, LoginTest):
533	        show_login_test(r)
534	
535	
536	if __name__ == "__main__":
537	    main()
538
```

```text
262	    """Route `fleet chezmoi <action> [args...]` to the chezmoi-backend helpers.

264	    The top-level `apply`/`status`/`diff`/`tail`/`kill`/`compact` subcommands
```

```text
18	# Operates on the config tree rooted at ${SSH_CFG_ROOT:-~/.ssh/config}, following
19	# `Include` directives RECURSIVELY (glob + ~/relative/absolute), so a Host defined in a
20	# config.d/ drop-in is found and edited in the file it actually lives in. Returns 127 when
21	# python3 is absent so callers can fall back to a plain append.
22	#

24	#   find <alias> [keypath]                 stdout: kv lines, then "---BLOCK---", then the
25	#                                          matched block. rc 0 = found, 3 = not found.
26	#   insert <file> <alias> <key> <action> [--identities-only]
27	#                                          action: insert | replace | add. Edits the block
28	#                                          in <file> in place (atomic, mode 0600).
29	#   ensure-include                         rc 0 if ~/.ssh/config.d is reachable via Include,
30	#                                          else rc 1.

33	_ssh_cfg_py() {

36	import os, re, sys, glob, pathlib, tempfile
37	
38	ROOT = pathlib.Path(os.environ.get("SSH_CFG_ROOT") or os.path.expanduser("~/.ssh/config"))
39	SSH_DIR = ROOT.parent
40	HOME = os.path.expanduser("~")
41	
42	HOST_RE  = re.compile(r"(?i)^(\s*)host\s+(.+?)\s*$")
43	BREAK_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)^\s*(host|match)\b")
44	IDF_RE   = re.compile(r"(?i)^(\s*)identityfile\s+(.+?)\s*$")
45	IDO_RE   = re.compile(r"(?i)^\s*identitiesonly\b")

48	
49	def expand(pat):
50	    pat = os.path.expanduser(pat)
51	    if not os.path.isabs(pat):
52	        pat = os.path.join(str(SSH_DIR), pat)
53	    return pat

55	
56	def resolve_includes(start):
57	    seen, files = set(), []
58	
59	    def walk(path):
60	        rp = os.path.realpath(path)
61	        if rp in seen:
62	            return
63	        seen.add(rp)
64	        p = pathlib.Path(path)
65	        if not p.is_file():
66	            return
67	        files.append(p)
68	        for line in p.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
69	            s = line.strip()
70	            if not s or s.startswith("#"):
71	                continue
72	            m = INC_RE.match(line)
73	            if not m:
74	                continue
75	            for pat in m.group(1).split():
76	                for f in sorted(glob.glob(expand(pat))):
77	                    walk(f)

79	    walk(str(start))
80	    return files

83	def norm(path):

93	    pats = host_patterns(line)
94	    if not pats:

96	    return any(p == alias and not re.search(r"[*?!]", p) for p in pats)

99	def find_block(alias, files):
100	    for f in files:
101	        lines = f.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
102	        i = 0

104	            if block_matches(lines[i], alias):

113	def tildify(path):

115	    rel = os.path.relpath(ap, HOME)
116	    if not rel.startswith(".."):
117	        return "~/" + rel
118	    return path

121	def write_atomic(f, lines):
122	    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(f.parent))
123	    try:
124	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as fh:
125	            fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
126	        os.replace(tmp, str(f))
127	        os.chmod(str(f), 0o600)
128	    except BaseException:
129	        try:
130	            os.unlink(tmp)
131	        except OSError:
132	            pass
133	        raise
134	
135	
136	def configd_reachable():
137	    target = os.path.realpath(str(SSH_DIR / "config.d"))
138	    for f in resolve_includes(ROOT):
139	        for line in f.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
140	            s = line.strip()
141	            if not s or s.startswith("#"):
142	                continue

144	            if not m:

146	            for pat in m.group(1).split():
147	                if os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(expand(pat))) == target:
148	                    return True
149	    return False

152	def cmd_find(alias, keypath):
153	    res = find_block(alias, resolve_includes(ROOT))
154	    if not res:
155	        print("found=0")
156	        return 3
157	    f, lines, i, j = res
158	    block = lines[i:j]
159	    idf = [m for m in (IDF_RE.match(b) for b in block) if m]
160	    keyn = norm(keypath) if keypath else ""
161	    present = bool(keyn) and any(norm(m.group(2)) == keyn for m in idf)
162	    print("found=1")
163	    print("file=%s" % f)
164	    print("has_identityfile=%d" % (1 if idf else 0))
165	    print("has_identitiesonly=%d" % (1 if any(IDO_RE.match(b) for b in block) else 0))
166	    print("key_present=%d" % (1 if present else 0))
167	    print("---BLOCK---")

172	def cmd_insert(file, alias, keypath, action, identities_only):
173	    f = pathlib.Path(file)
174	    lines = f.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()

182	    indent = "    "

536	      local confirm
537	      read -r confirm
538	      if [[ ! "$confirm" =~ ^[Nn] ]]; then
539	        printf '%s\n' "$config_block" >> "$config_file"
540	        chmod 600 "$config_file"
541	        printf 'Config written.\n'
542	
543	        # If we wrote into config.d/ but the entry-point config never Includes
544	        # it, the drop-in silently won't load. Offer to wire it up.
545	        if [ "$wrote_configd" = "1" ] && command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
546	          if ! _ssh_cfg_py ensure-include; then
547	            printf '\nNote: ~/.ssh/config has no `Include` for config.d/* — this entry will not load.\n'
548	            printf 'Add `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` to ~/.ssh/config now? [Y/n] '
549	            local do_inc
550	            read -r do_inc
551	            if [[ ! "$do_inc" =~ ^[Nn] ]]; then
552	              _ssh_cfg_py add-include && printf 'Include directive added.\n'
553	            fi
554	          fi
555	        fi
556	      fi
557	    fi
558	  fi
559	
560	  # ── Done ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
561	  printf '\n=== Done! ===\n'
562	  printf 'Test with: ssh %s\n' "${host_alias:-$target}"
563	  if [[ "$do_scp" =~ ^[Yy] ]]; then
564	    printf "Test GitHub: ssh %s 'ssh -T git@github.com'\n" "${host_alias:-$target}"
565	  fi
566	}
567
```

```text
16	# so a dropped connection resumes instead of losing the shell. That lives in

18	# cable or the two will drift. See docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md.
```

```text
1	# Custom SSH config channel for television (tv)
2	# Parses Host entries from ~/.ssh/config AND ~/.ssh/config.d/* (Include support).
3	# The community ssh-hosts channel only reads ~/.ssh/config directly.
4	#
5	# Each entry shows which file the host is defined in, so duplicates across
6	# config.d/* are easy to spot. The output (what gets passed to ssh / actions)
7	# is just the bare hostname.
8	#
9	# Usage:
10	#   tv ssh-config
11	#
12	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
13	#   Enter      SSH into selected host
14	#   Alt+T      Online probe: BatchMode=yes test (does pubkey login actually work?)
15	#   Alt+A      Offline batch scan: list every host + whether a local key file exists
16	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
17	#
18	# Preview shows resolved config via `ssh -G` plus a local-key existence check
19	# (no network — just stat the IdentityFile paths).
20	
21	[metadata]
22	name = "ssh-config"
23	description = "SSH hosts (with Include config.d/* support)"
24	requirements = ["ssh", "awk", "sort"]
25	
26	[source]
27	# Emit "<source-file>\t<hostname>" so the picker shows the origin file but
28	# actions still receive a clean hostname via {split:\t:1}.
29	command = """
30	for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
31	  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
32	  rel=${f#$HOME/}
33	  awk -v src="$rel" '
34	    /^[[:space:]]*Host[[:space:]]/ {
35	      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
36	        if ($i !~ /[*?]/) printf "%s\\t%s\\n", src, $i
37	      }
38	    }' "$f"
39	done | sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2
40	"""
41	display = "{split:\\t:1}  ({split:\\t:0})"
42	output = "{split:\\t:1}"
43	
44	[preview]
45	command = """
46	host='{split:\\t:1}'
47	src='{split:\\t:0}'
48	echo "# defined in: $src"
49	echo
50	ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^(host|hostname|user|port|identityfile|proxycommand|proxyjump|forwardagent|identityagent|localforward|remoteforward)[[:space:]]'
51	echo
52	echo '--- local key check (offline) ---'
53	found=0
54	while IFS= read -r f; do
55	  [ -z "$f" ] && continue
56	  case "$f" in '~/'*) f="$HOME/${f#'~/'}";; '~') f="$HOME";; esac
57	  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
58	    echo "  [OK]   $f"
59	    found=1
60	  else
61	    echo "  [miss] $f"
62	  fi
63	done <<EOF
64	$(ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^identityfile / {print $2}')
65	EOF
66	if [ "$found" -eq 0 ]; then
67	  echo
68	  echo '  => no IdentityFile present locally — password login likely required'
69	  echo '     (or relies on ssh-agent / IdentityAgent — try Alt+T to probe)'
70	fi
71	"""
72	
73	[keybindings]
74	enter = "actions:connect"
75	alt-t = "actions:probe"
76	alt-a = "actions:scan_all"
77	
78	[actions.connect]
79	description = "SSH into the selected host"
80	command = "ssh '{split:\\t:1}'"
81	mode = "execute"
82	
83	[actions.probe]
84	description = "Probe selected host with BatchMode (no password prompt allowed)"
85	command = """
86	host='{split:\\t:1}'
87	echo "# Probing $host with BatchMode=yes (ConnectTimeout=3)"
88	echo "# Exit 0 = passwordless login works; non-zero = needs password / unreachable / key not authorized"
89	echo
90	ssh -o BatchMode=yes \\
91	    -o ConnectTimeout=3 \\
92	    -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \\
93	    -o PreferredAuthentications=publickey,hostbased,gssapi-with-mic \\
94	    "$host" true
95	rc=$?
96	echo
97	case $rc in
98	  0)   echo "[OK] passwordless login works for '$host'" ;;
99	  255) echo "[FAIL] connection / auth error (exit 255) — needs password, key not authorized, or host unreachable" ;;
100	  *)   echo "[FAIL] remote command failed (exit $rc) — auth probably OK but 'true' failed" ;;
101	esac
102	echo
103	echo '[Press Enter to exit]'
104	read -r _
105	"""
106	mode = "execute"
107	
108	[actions.scan_all]
109	description = "Offline scan: for every host, check if any IdentityFile exists locally"
110	command = """
111	echo "# Scanning all hosts (offline — no network) ..."
112	echo "# Legend: [OK] = at least one IdentityFile present locally"
113	echo "#         [--] = no key file on disk (password / agent / unconfigured)"
114	echo
115	for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
116	  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
117	  rel=${f#$HOME/}
118	  awk -v src="$rel" '
119	    /^[[:space:]]*Host[[:space:]]/ {
120	      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
121	        if ($i !~ /[*?]/) printf "%s\\t%s\\n", src, $i
122	      }
123	    }' "$f"
124	done | sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2 | while IFS=$'\\t' read -r src host; do
125	  keyline=""
126	  found=0
127	  while IFS= read -r kf; do
128	    [ -z "$kf" ] && continue
129	    case "$kf" in '~/'*) kf="$HOME/${kf#'~/'}";; '~') kf="$HOME";; esac
130	    if [ -f "$kf" ]; then
131	      keyline="$kf"
132	      found=1
133	      break
134	    fi
135	  done <<EOF
136	$(ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^identityfile / {print $2}')
137	EOF
138	  if [ "$found" -eq 1 ]; then
139	    printf '  [OK] %-28s %-22s -> %s\\n' "$host" "($src)" "$keyline"
140	  else
141	    printf '  [--] %-28s %-22s    (no local key)\\n' "$host" "($src)"
142	  fi
143	done
144	echo
145	echo '[Press Enter to exit]'
146	read -r _
147	"""
148	mode = "execute"
149
```

<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>

```text
1	# 47_mi_router.sh - mi-router tab completion (auto-generated by tyro).
2	#
3	# Class A: lazy autoload — writes to the shell's standard completion dir,
4	# letting compinit (zsh) / bash-completion v2 (bash) load on first TAB.
5	#   zsh:  ~/.zfunc/_mi-router                       (in fpath via dot_zshrc.tmpl:68)
6	#   bash: ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/bash-completion/completions/mi-router
7	#
8	# Generator: `mi-router --tyro-write-completion {bash,zsh}` — runs the Python
9	# CLI as a subprocess (~500ms cold), so we mtime-check vs the binary and only
10	# regenerate when mi-router itself is newer than the cache. Force refresh:
11	# `mi-router-update-completion` (in dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh).
12	#
13	# Sourced by both ~/.zshrc and ~/.bashrc via load_modular_dir.
14	
15	command -v mi-router >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
16	
17	if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
18	    _mr_cache="${HOME}/.zfunc/_mi-router"
19	    _mr_shell=zsh
20	elif [ -n "$BASH_VERSION" ]; then
21	    _mr_cache="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/mi-router"
22	    _mr_shell=bash
23	else
24	    return 0
25	fi
26	
27	_mr_bin="$(command -v mi-router)"
28	if [ ! -f "$_mr_cache" ] || [ "$_mr_bin" -nt "$_mr_cache" ]; then
29	    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$_mr_cache")"
30	    if [ "$_mr_shell" = "zsh" ]; then
31	        # tyro emits `#compdef <fullpath>` — rewrite to the short name so
32	        # `mi-router<TAB>` (not `/full/path/mi-router<TAB>`) triggers compinit.
33	        _mr_tmp="$(mktemp)"
34	        if mi-router --tyro-write-completion zsh "$_mr_tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
35	            { echo "#compdef mi-router"; tail -n +2 "$_mr_tmp"; } > "$_mr_cache"
36	        fi
37	        rm -f "$_mr_tmp"
38	        unset _mr_tmp
39	    else
40	        # tyro's bash output already binds basename via `complete -F`.
41	        mi-router --tyro-write-completion bash "$_mr_cache" >/dev/null 2>&1
42	    fi
43	fi
44	
45	unset _mr_cache _mr_shell _mr_bin
46
```

```text
39	**Three-tier file placement** for new shell helpers:
40	
41	| Tier | Dir | When |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| Shared | `dot_config/shell/` | POSIX subset, both shells source. `$ZSH_VERSION`/`$BASH_VERSION` source-time dispatch is OK; ZLE widgets / `compdef` / `bindkey` / `setopt` / `read -q` / `${m:t}` / glob qualifiers are NOT (bash would error on source). |
44	| Zsh-only | `dot_config/zsh/` | ZLE widgets, `compdef`, `bindkey`, `setopt`, zsh-vi-mode hooks. |
45	| Bash-only | `dot_config/bash/` | `bind -x` / `ble-bind`, OMB plugin arrays, bash-specific `shopt`s. |
46	
47	When porting a zsh-only helper to bash via ble.sh, extract the shell-agnostic backend into `dot_config/shell/` and keep each shell's widget binding in its own dir.
48	
49	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
50	
51	The `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism spans **6 surfaces that must move together** — devtools install, `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml`, `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`, `dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl` hooks, `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` (+ its `modify_package.json`), and `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`'s producers API. Exact contents: [workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md) § Status icon mechanics; why it leaks: [workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md).
52	
53	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (writes parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears). The workmux hook entries are **unconditional** — the `agentSounds` prompt gates only the notify.sh / peon-ping entries in the same file. `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux) stay distinct tools.
54	
55	### Long-term backlog + past pitfalls → use the `project-knowledge-harness` skill
56	
57	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` agent skill (restored on every `chezmoi apply`; see [agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md)). **Load the skill** for the template and disambiguation table.
58	
59	**Fallback rules**, so this still binds when the skill can't be loaded:
60	
61	- Three repo-root surfaces, all chezmoi-ignored, all NOT auto-redacted: [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) (tags `P1`/`P2`/`P3`/`P?` × `S`/`M`/`L`/`XL`), [`backlog/`](backlog/README.md) (notes for `P?` / `[L]` / `[XL]` / multi-option), [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/README.md) (debugged traps — **title by symptom, not root cause**, verbatim error messages, never paraphrase).
62	- Capture triggers — future work: "maybe later", "nice to have", "工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來". Pitfalls: >~15 min debugging, not googleable, non-obvious fix, silent failure.
63	- Do **not** spawn `ROADMAP.md` / `IDEAS.md` / `LESSONS.md` / `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`. Three surfaces, always.
64	- A pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant below when it recurs across machines, silently corrupts state, or has a non-obvious workaround. Link back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md`.
65	
66	## Chezmoi templating conventions
67	
68	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask whether the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` (`darwin`/`linux`) / `.chezmoi.arch` (`arm64`/`amd64`) / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for **user-role choices only**, and its values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts. `.profile` is still the right knob for desktop-vs-headless.
69	
70	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
71	
72	Predicate table, examples, the `macos_intel` migration: [chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
73	
74	## Hard repo invariants
75	
76	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
77	
78	YAML / TOML / JSON syntax and template rendering are not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (`codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is only a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
79	
80	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
81	
82	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
83	
84	**Hard rules**:
85	
86	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
87	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
88	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
89	
90	The ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be last before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions`/`syntax-highlighting`/`history-substring-search` MUST be excluded (double-init flicker). [bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
91	
92	### Three-tier user-local override layer
93	
94	User overrides live in **six** untracked files, all in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). Default target: shared; drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
95	
96	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl` — `managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc`. Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
97	
98	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
99	
100	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
101	
102	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templates + 2 first-seed files: [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
103	
104	**Hard rules**:
105	
106	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
107	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/`, `dot_config/opencode/`, `dot_cursor/`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
108	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
109	- The `minimal` bundle forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without an explicit request.
110	- New vim-touched file → follow the gate-it-or-not flow in [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md) → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table there.
111	
112	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
113	
114	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
115	
116	**Hard rules**:
117	
118	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
119	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
120	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a *single* tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it genuinely needs a newer one (`python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5`). It MUST detect the install style and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (silent no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors when it isn't a formula). The dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and the role. See [uv-bootstrap](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
121	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`, or the install guard short-circuits and entry-point shims are never written (silently missing `jupyter` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit command: [uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
122	- New upgrade category: [upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) § Adding a new category. Tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise → do nothing, generic `upgrade` picks it up.
123	- **Probe `brew` by output, never exit status** — `[[ -n "$(brew --prefix 2>/dev/null)" ]]`. A stub `brew` passes `command -v brew` and returns 0 with empty output for *every* subcommand: `brew bundle` silently installs nothing and `community.general.homebrew` dies on `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`. [ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md](pitfalls/ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md)
124	
125	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
126	
127	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
128	
129	**Hard rules**:
130	
131	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
132	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
133	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
134	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
135	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
136	
137	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**: `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top → set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag → `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"` and branch on its return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason` → run privileged commands via `sudo_run …` (or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible).
138	
139	For **non-interactive** injection (`scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH), `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (0600) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty` — **never** read that variable directly, always go through the helper. Full API + state + cleanup model: [sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
140	
141	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
142	
143	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
144	
145	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked; hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let the template win.
146	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (`chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`), so ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for those.
147	- **`--branch BRANCH` is a no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS your editor working tree): they warn and run against the working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
148	- **Install-only by design.** `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
149	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
150	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint; anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without an explicit request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
151	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse. `just fleet-status` is the **pre-flight readiness probe** (13 states; always exits 0 — use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates; `fleet-status-quick` skips the remote `git fetch`). `just fleet-apply-status` is a **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`, run during/after, pairing with `fleet-apply-tail`/`-watch`/`-kill`. State meanings incl. `toml-mismatch`: [fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md).
152	- **`fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving** (auto-seed / exit 0 with a hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
153	
154	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
155	
156	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes the current target contents to stdin and expects the new contents on stdout. Used wherever a *foreign writer* also owns part of the file — `~/.claude/settings.json`, editor `settings.json`, the agent CLI configs, `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`, `~/.gitconfig` (preserves the `[credential]` blocks `gh auth setup-git` injects). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it overwrites the script with the live file.
157	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches the contents after (`~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json`, editor `keybindings.json`). Refresh the baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"` — `chezmoi add` strips the prefix and `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
158	
159	Per-file case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). The three agent CLI overlays, incl. the Claude hook merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland) without ping-ponging: [agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
160	
161	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
162	
163	The popup menu (`prefix + Space` / `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two tmux quirks force that: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) instead of clamped — the `devtools` role auto-upgrades Debian/Ubuntu past it — and `display-menu` does **not** paginate, so a menu taller than the terminal is suppressed entirely, with no error anywhere.
164	
165	**Hard rules**:
166	
167	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
168	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
169	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
170	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
171	
172	Full story incl. the red herrings: `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`, `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
173	
174	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
175	
176	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
177	
178	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps. **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
179	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
180	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
181	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
182	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
183	
184	Full breakdown / themes / keybindings / troubleshooting: [](docs/tools/tmux/).
185	
186	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
187	
188	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` sets `default_mode "locked"` on purpose — all keys pass through to inner apps, `Ctrl+G` unlocks Zellij's own. Do **not** change it. Fresh box → pick the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" preset. [keyboard-shortcuts.md](docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)
189
```

```text
**Dynamic candidates wired up:**

- `fleet` host names — `_fleet_hosts_one` / `_fleet_hosts_csv` shell out to `fleet hosts --list`. Used for the positional `fleet hosts NAME`, `fleet chezmoi diff HOST`, `fleet chezmoi tail HOST`, and the `--hosts=foo,bar,baz` CSV flag everywhere.
- `pqsum -g <GROUP>` — `_pqsum` shells out to `pueue status --json | jq '.groups | keys[]'`.
- `mlf` ids (run-id, experiment-id, model-name) — **not** auto-completed (would round-trip MLflow tracking server, possibly auth-required). Use `tv mlflow` for fuzzy id picking instead.
- `yth` video ids — **not** auto-completed (opaque 11-char ids; enumerating the whole history on every TAB is wasteful). Use `tv yth` or `yth search <query>` instead.
- `wake` host names — `_wake` shells out to `wake --list-names` (reads `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`), same pattern as `_fleet_hosts_one`.
- `appsrc which <name>` / `appsrc size <name>` — `_appsrc_names` shells out to `appsrc scan --list-names` (installed GUI app names) and adds `_command_names -e` / `compgen -c` (PATH commands), so both a GUI app name and a shell command complete. Same shell-out pattern as `_wake` / `_fleet_hosts_one`.

**Adding a new in-house CLI** (decision flow):

1. **Does it use tyro?** → Use Strategy A. Mirror `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh`. Add a `<tool>-update-completion` helper to `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. Don't forget to rewrite `#compdef` in zsh post-gen.
2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).
3. **Hand-rolled / shell script** → Strategy B hand-written. One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers.
4. **Update this table + `docs/shells/aliases.md`** in the same commit (per the cross-file maintenance rule in `CLAUDE.md`).

## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi

**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:

1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.

### What we DO track

- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`

## Generating Completions After Fresh Install

**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).

The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
```

```text
===MAIN===
---
# Networking CLI tools role
# Tools: nmap, arp-scan, mtr, iperf3, doggo, httpie, gping, trippy, bandwhich, speedtest, rustscan

# =============================================================================
# macOS - all via Homebrew
# =============================================================================

- name: Install networking tools (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name:
      - nmap
      - arp-scan
      - mtr
      - iperf3
      - doggo
      - httpie
      - gping
      - trippy
      - bandwhich
      - rustscan
      - wakeonlan
    state: present

- name: Install Ookla Speedtest CLI (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  block:
    - name: Check if teamookla/speedtest tap is present
      ansible.builtin.command: brew tap
      register: speedtest_taps
      changed_when: false

    - name: Tap teamookla/speedtest
      ansible.builtin.command: brew tap teamookla/speedtest
      when: "'teamookla/speedtest' not in speedtest_taps.stdout_lines"

    - name: Check trust state of teamookla/speedtest tap (Homebrew >= 6.0 trust gate)
      ansible.builtin.command: brew tap-info teamookla/speedtest
      register: speedtest_tap_info
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false

    - name: Trust teamookla/speedtest tap when Homebrew marks it untrusted
      when: "'Untrusted' in speedtest_tap_info.stdout"
      ansible.builtin.command: brew trust teamookla/speedtest

# =============================================================================
# Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)

# --- system-level packages (apt) ---
- name: Install networking tools from apt (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name:
      - nmap
      - arp-scan
      - mtr
      - iperf3
      - httpie
      - tcpdump
      - wakeonlan
    state: present

# --- system-level packages (yum/CentOS 7+) ---
# yum CLI for CentOS 7 compat — see pitfalls/centos7-ansible-yum-dnf-backend.md
- name: Install networking tools from yum (RedHat/CentOS) — yum CLI for CentOS 7 + Rocky/Alma compat
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "RedHat"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    set -e
    missing=()
    for p in nmap arp-scan mtr iperf3 tcpdump; do
      rpm -q "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
    done
    # NOTE: httpie is in EPEL on CentOS 7 and pip-installed via uv elsewhere
    # if missing, so we skip it here to avoid hard-requiring EPEL.
    if [ -z "${missing[*]:-}" ]; then
      echo "ALL_INSTALLED"
      exit 0
    fi
    yum install -y "${missing[@]}"
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
  register: networking_yum_result
  changed_when: "'ALL_INSTALLED' not in networking_yum_result.stdout"
  ignore_errors: true

# --- Architecture mapping for GitHub release downloads ---
- name: Set networking tools release architecture
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    net_arch_deb: >-
      {{
        'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
        else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
        else target_architecture
      }}

: Install ngrok GPG key
          ansible.builtin.shell: |
            gpg --dearmor < /tmp/ngrok.asc > /etc/apt/keyrings/ngrok.gpg
            chmod 0644 /etc/apt/keyrings/ngrok.gpg
          args:
            creates: /etc/apt/keyrings/ngrok.gpg

        - name: Add ngrok apt source
          ansible.builtin.copy:
            content: "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/ngrok.gpg] https://ngrok-agent.s3.amazonaws.com buster main\n"
            dest: /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ngrok.list
            mode: '0644'

        - name: Install ngrok from apt
          ansible.builtin.apt:
            name: ngrok
            update_cache: true
            state: present

    - name: Re-check ngrok after apt install
      ansible.builtin.command: ngrok version
      register: ngrok_recheck
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false

    - name: Install ngrok from tgz (user-level fallback)
      when: ngrok_recheck.rc != 0
      block:
        - name: Set ngrok tgz architecture
          ansible.builtin.set_fact:
            ngrok_tgz_arch: >-
              {{ 'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
                 else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
                 else '' }}

        - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists
          ansible.builtin.file:
            path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
            state: directory
            mode: '0755'

        - name: Download ngrok tgz (user-level)
          ansible.builtin.get_url:
            url: "https://bin.equinox.io/c/bNyj1mQVY4c/ngrok-v3-stable-linux-{{ ngrok_tgz_arch }}.tgz"
            dest: /tmp/ngrok.tgz
            timeout: 120
          when: ngrok_tgz_arch != ''

        - name: Extract and install ngrok (user-level)
          ansible.builtin.shell: |
            set -e
            tar -xzf /tmp/ngrok.tgz -C /tmp/
            install -m 0755 /tmp/ngrok "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/ngrok"
          args:
            executable: /bin/bash
            creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/ngrok"
          changed_when: true

        - name: Clean up ngrok tgz
          ansible.builtin.file:
            path: /tmp/ngrok.tgz
            state: absent

  rescue:
    - name: Warn ngrok installation failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "ngrok installation failed — skipping. Error: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown') }}"

    - name: Clean up ngrok temp files (rescue)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/ngrok.tgz
        - /tmp/ngrok
        - /tmp/ngrok.asc

- name: Install ngrok (RedHat/CentOS — tgz user-level)
  tags: [tunnel_tools]
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "RedHat"
  block:
    - name: Check if ngrok is installed (RedHat)
      ansible.builtin.command: ngrok version
      register: ngrok_rh_check
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false

    - name: Set ngrok tgz architecture (RedHat)
      when: ngrok_rh_check.rc != 0
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        ngrok_rh_arch: >-
          {{ 'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
             else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
             else '' }}

    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (RedHat)
      when: ngrok_rh_check.rc != 0 and ngrok_rh_arch | default('') != ''
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Download and install ngrok tgz (RedHat)
      when: ngrok_rh_check.rc != 0 and ngrok_rh_arch | default('') != ''
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        set -e
        curl -fsSL "https://bin.equinox.io/c/bNyj1mQVY4c/ngrok-v3-stable-linux-{{ ngrok_rh_arch }}.tgz" -o /tmp/ngrok.tgz
        tar -xzf /tmp/ngrok.tgz -C /tmp/
        install -m 0755 /tmp/ngrok "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/ngrok"
        rm -f /tmp/ngrok.tgz /tmp/ngrok
      args:
        executable: /bin/bash
        creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/ngrok"
      changed_when: true

  rescue:
    - name: Warn ngrok installation failed (RedHat)
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "ngrok installation failed on RedHat — skipping."

    - name: Clean up ngrok temp files (RedHat rescue)
      ansible.builtin.shell: rm -f /tmp/ngrok.tgz /tmp/ngrok
      args:
        executable: /bin/bash
      changed_when: false
```

```text
    - name: Remove legacy Steam apt source list files
      become: true
      tags: [sudo]
      ansible.builtin.file:

    - name: Add Valve Steam apt repository
      become: true
      tags: [sudo]
      ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
        name: steam
        types: deb
        uris: https://repo.steampowered.com/steam/
        suites: stable
        components: steam
        architectures:
          - amd64
          - i386
        signed_by: /usr/share/keyrings/steam.gpg

    # Refresh ONLY the Steam source, not the whole apt config. A plain
    # `apt-get update` re-fetches every third-party source (vscode, cursor,
    # azure, hashicorp, ngrok, tailscale, …); on a flaky network/proxy any one
    # of them can make the update exit non-zero and (via the block rescue)
    # leave the just-added Valve repo unindexed → `steam-launcher` unresolvable.
    # Scoping to sources.list.d/steam.sources keeps this immune to sibling
    # sources. (No ansible.builtin.apt equivalent — it can't target one source.)
    # cache_valid_time is irrelevant here too: base already refreshed the cache
    # at play start, so an unscoped module call would skip and never index Steam.
    - name: Refresh apt cache for the Steam source only
      become: true
      tags: [sudo]
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: >-
          apt-get update
          -o Dir::Etc::sourcelist=sources.list.d/steam.sources
          -o Dir::Etc::sourceparts=-
          -o APT::Get::List-Cleanup=0
      changed_when: false

    - name: Install Steam launcher
      become: true
      tags: [sudo]
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name: steam-launcher
        state: present
        install_recommends: true
        update_cache: false
  rescue:
    - name: Warn Steam install failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: >-
          Steam install failed. Manual fallback: follow Valve's apt repo
          instructions at https://repo.steampowered.com/steam/ or install the
          latest launcher package from
          https://repo.steampowered.com/steam/archive/stable/steam_latest.deb.
```

```text
      args:
        executable: /bin/bash
      changed_when: false
  rescue:
    - name: Warn rustscan installation failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "rustscan installation failed — skipping. Error: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown') }}"

    - name: Clean up rustscan temp files (rescue)
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        rm -f /tmp/rustscan.zip /tmp/rustscan /tmp/x86_64-linux-rustscan.tar.gz /tmp/aarch64-linux-rustscan
      args:
        executable: /bin/bash
      changed_when: false

# =============================================================================
# Tunnel tools — ngrok + cloudflared
# Tags: tunnel_tools (gated by installTunnelTools chezmoi flag)
# =============================================================================

# --- ngrok ---

- name: Install ngrok (macOS)
  tags: [tunnel_tools]
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  block:
    # Skip the install when the binary is already on PATH — ngrok cask downloads
    # from bin.ngrok.com which periodically returns HTTP 52 "empty reply from
    # server" (Heroku-fronted, transient). Pre-checking lets re-applies short-
    # circuit instead of paying a 1-2 min download attempt that may fail.
    - name: Check if ngrok is already installed (macOS)
      ansible.builtin.command: which ngrok
      register: ngrok_present_macos
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false

    - name: Install ngrok via Homebrew (with retries for flaky bin.ngrok.com CDN)
      when: ngrok_present_macos.rc != 0
      community.general.homebrew:
        name: ngrok
        state: present
      register: ngrok_brew_install
      until: ngrok_brew_install is succeeded
      retries: 3
      delay: 15

  rescue:
    # Most common failure: `Download failed: ... curl: (52) Empty reply from
    # server` from bin.ngrok.com (Heroku CDN). Transient — retrying minutes
    # later usually works. We don't fail the whole apply over it; user can
    # re-run `chezmoi apply --tag tunnel_tools` or `brew install --cask ngrok`
    # later. See pitfalls/ngrok-cask-download-flaky.md for the full story.
    - name: Warn ngrok installation failed (macOS)
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: |-
          ngrok macOS installation failed after 3 retries — skipping. Re-run
          `brew install --cask ngrok` later. Error: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown') }}

- name: Install ngrok (Debian/Ubuntu)
  tags: [tunnel_tools]
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  block:
    - name: Check if ngrok is installed
      ansible.builtin.command: ngrok version
      register: ngrok_check
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false

    - name: Install ngrok via official apt repo (Debian/Ubuntu)
      when: ngrok_check.rc != 0
      become: true
```

```text
4	# Keep this file tiny. No bats-assert / bats-file / bats-support — plain

7	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/.." && pwd)"
8	if [ "$(basename "$REPO_ROOT")" = "tests" ]; then
9	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$REPO_ROOT/.." && pwd)"
10	fi

12	
13	_BATS_STUB_DIRS=()
14	
15	# Create a temp directory and prepend it to PATH. Exposes the path via
16	# $BATS_STUB_DIR (not via stdout) so the PATH export actually sticks — using
17	# command substitution would run this in a subshell and discard the export.
18	setup_path_stub() {
19	  BATS_STUB_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bats-stub.XXXXXX")"
20	  _BATS_STUB_DIRS+=("$BATS_STUB_DIR")
21	  PATH="$BATS_STUB_DIR:$PATH"
22	  export PATH BATS_STUB_DIR
23	}
24	
25	# Cleanup function. Call from your own teardown() if you override it:
26	#   teardown() { your_cleanup; cleanup_path_stubs; }
27	cleanup_path_stubs() {
28	  local dir
29	  for dir in "${_BATS_STUB_DIRS[@]:-}"; do
30	    [ -n "$dir" ] && [ -d "$dir" ] && rm -rf "$dir"
31	  done
32	  _BATS_STUB_DIRS=()
33	}
34	
35	# Default teardown — fires only if the .bats file does not define its own.
36	teardown() { cleanup_path_stubs; }
```

109	
110	## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)
111	
112	Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`, or read `docs/tools/<name>.md`. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.
113	
114	- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
115	- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
116	- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
117	- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
118	- **`view-office`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) in the terminal; also powers the yazi Office previewer. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`.
119	- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
120	- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
121	- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
122	- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
123	- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
124	- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
125	- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
126	- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.
127

129	
130	There are ~40 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)

136	tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue

```text
"""fleet exec — cross-host ad-hoc command runner.

Fan-out an argv-list command (or shell string) over the fleet inventory:

  1. Default: argv list after `--`, no shell expansion (safe by construction).
     `fleet exec -- pueue --version` runs `pueue --version` literally on each
     host via asyncssh; per-arg shlex.quote keeps it injection-safe.
  2. `--shell <bin>` opt-in: wraps in `<bin> -c '<argv joined>'` so the user
     can use pipes / globs / redirects / env-prefixes.
  3. `--login` opt-in: wraps in `<shell> -lc '...'` so the remote rc files
     load (gives access to nvm / mise / conda / aliases). Slower per host.
  4. `--ai` summarises results into succeeded/differed/failed tiers via the
     copy-pasted AICAP block (4th Python consumer of `04_ai_agents.sh`;
     extraction TODO is the next priority — see `backlog/fleet-exec.md`).

Per-host failures (SSH timeout, command exit ≠ 0) never abort the run; each
shows up as its own row with rc + first line of stderr.

Output: Rich table by default; `--json` for piping; `--out-dir DIR` writes
per-host stdout/stderr/json files; `--full-output` expands the table into
per-host blocks.

This module is invoked by `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet exec ...` and
shares its inventory + asyncssh plumbing with `scripts/fleet/apply.py` via
`from scripts.fleet import ...`.

Argparse (not tyro) is used here because the `--` separator + REMAINDER-style
positional argv list maps cleanly onto argparse's native option-parser stop
behaviour. The other fleet modules use tyro because they don't have a
positional argv list.
"""
```

```text
# ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — fleet_apply.py host inventory
#
# Seeded ONCE by chezmoi (`create_` prefix) so your edits are never overwritten.
# To reset to this template: `rm ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml && chezmoi apply`.
# File mode is 0600 (chezmoi `private_` prefix) — safe for plaintext passwords,
# but Bitwarden / interactive prompt sources are still preferred.
#
# IMPORTANT: `password_source` is for the REMOTE `sudo` password ONLY (fed to
# chezmoi via CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE for `run_*` scripts). It does NOT
# authenticate the SSH login itself — fleet always tries key/agent auth
# FIRST for SSH login. If `ssh <host>` prompts you for a password, the host
# will show as `unreachable` in `just fleet-status`. Fix with `ssh-copy-id`
# where possible. If the remote flatly disallows pubkey auth (e.g. corporate/
# IDC sshd with `PubkeyAuthentication no`), set the separate, opt-in
# `ssh_login_password_source` field (example 6 below) — independent of
# `password_source`, since a host's SSH login password may differ from its
# sudo password. See `pitfalls/fleet-apply-password-source-not-for-ssh-login.md`
# for context.
#
# Schema reference: docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md
# Run: `just fleet-apply` (parallel) | `just fleet-apply-dry-run` (chezmoi diff)

[defaults]
chezmoi_path    = "auto"           # "auto" → augment remote PATH with common install dirs
                                   # (~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin,
                                   #  /usr/local/bin, /snap/bin) before invoking `chezmoi`.
                                   # Override per-host with an absolute path (e.g.
                                   # "/snap/bin/chezmoi") to pin a specific binary.
connect_timeout = 15
command_timeout = 1800

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Default: apply to THIS machine (local execution, no SSH).
# Seeded once on `chezmoi apply`; edit freely — chezmoi won't overwrite.
# `no_root_machine` mirrors the chezmoi `.noRoot` prompt from
# .chezmoi.toml.tmpl so this entry stays consistent with how the rest of
# the dotfiles were initialised on this host.
# `password_source` is intentionally omitted: for `local = true` hosts
# fleet_apply.py skips its password gate (chezmoi inherits the parent
# terminal's TTY and prompts for sudo there if needed).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[[hosts]]
name            = "self"
local           = true
no_root_machine = {{ .noRoot }}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Templates for adding REMOTE hosts — uncomment and edit as needed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1) Preferred: ssh_config alias. Inherits ProxyJump, IdentityAgent (e.g.
#    1Password SSH agent), Match blocks — everything you'd get from `ssh lab-box`.
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "lab-box"
# ssh_alias       = "lab-box"
# no_root_machine = false                                   # remote was init'd with noRoot=false
# password_source = { type = "bitwarden", item = "ssh-lab-box-sudo" }

# 2) Explicit connection (no ssh_config entry).
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "vps-tokyo"
# hostname        = "203.0.113.42"
# user            = "dwlee"
# port            = 22
# identity_file   = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
# no_root_machine = true                                    # remote was init'd with noRoot=true
# # password_source omitted → no sudo phase; chezmoi runs as the SSH user only.

# 3) Interactive prompt (asked once at startup, never persisted).
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "office-mac"
# ssh_alias       = "office-mac"
# no_root_machine = false
# password_source = { type = "prompt" }

# 4) Plaintext password (last resort — relies on file mode 0600).
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "throwaway-vm"
# ssh_alias       = "throwaway-vm"
# no_root_machine = false
```

===TUNNELS===
# Tunnel Tools (ngrok / cloudflared)

Expose a local port or service to the internet — useful for webhook testing, sharing a dev server, SSH reverse tunnels, and Cloudflare-native access policies.

Optional role (`installTunnelTools`). Enable at `chezmoi init --force` or set `installTunnelTools = true` in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`.

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose | Account required? | Free tier |
|------|---------|-------------------|-----------|
| [ngrok](https://ngrok.com/) | HTTP/TCP/TLS tunnels, traffic inspection UI | Yes (free plan available) | 1 agent, 1 endpoint, random subdomain |
| [cloudflared](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/) | Cloudflare Tunnel — production-grade, no port forwarding needed | Yes (Cloudflare account, free) | Unlimited named tunnels, custom domains via Cloudflare DNS |

## Installation

Managed by the `networking_tools` Ansible role under the `tunnel_tools` tag.

| Platform | ngrok | cloudflared |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| macOS | `brew install ngrok/ngrok/ngrok` | `brew install cloudflared` |
| Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) | apt repo (official) → tgz fallback | `.deb` from GitHub releases → binary fallback |
| Linux (CentOS/RHEL) | tgz from equinox.io → `~/.local/bin` | `.rpm` from GitHub releases |

---

## ngrok

### Initial setup

```bash
# Authenticate (one-time, token stored in ~/.config/ngrok/ngrok.yml)
ngrok config add-authtoken <YOUR_TOKEN>
```

Get your token from <https://dashboard.ngrok.com/get-started/your-authtoken>.

### Expose a local HTTP server

```bash
# Forward localhost:3000 to a random ngrok HTTPS URL
```

```text
# Custom listening ports cable channel for television (tv)
# Shows all listening TCP/UDP ports with PID, process name, and address.
#
# Usage:
#   tv ports
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Show process details
#   Ctrl+K     Kill the selected process (stays in picker to kill more)
#   Ctrl+D     Force kill (kill -9)
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Preview shows full process details via `ps`.
# Cross-platform: uses lsof (macOS) or ss (Linux).

[metadata]
name = "ports"
description = "Listening ports: PID, process, address"

[source]
command = """
if command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  lsof -i -P -n 2>/dev/null | grep LISTEN | awk '{printf "%-6s  %-20s  %s\\n", $2, $9, $1}' | sort -u
elif command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | awk '{
    addr=$4; pid=$7;
    gsub(/.*pid=/,"",pid); gsub(/,.*$/,"",pid);
    gsub(/.*users:\\(\\("/,"",pid);
    printf "%-6s  %-20s  %s\\n", pid, addr, $7
  }' | sort -u
fi
"""

[preview]
command = "ps -p '{split: :0}' -o pid,ppid,%cpu,%mem,etime,command 2>/dev/null"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:details"
ctrl-k = ["actions:kill", "reload_source"]
ctrl-d = ["actions:force_kill", "reload_source"]
```

```text
# --- mi-dhcp-bind (tyro) completion regen ----------------------------------
# Force-regenerate the lazy-autoload completion file used by 46_mi_dhcp_bind.sh
# (sister to mi-router-update-completion below; mi-dhcp-bind is the WRITE tool).
function mi-dhcp-bind-update-completion {
	command -v mi-dhcp-bind >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
		echo "mi-dhcp-bind-update-completion: mi-dhcp-bind not installed" >&2
		return 1
	}
	if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
		local _tmp
		_tmp=$(mktemp)
		if mi-dhcp-bind --tyro-write-completion zsh "$_tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
			mkdir -p "${HOME}/.zfunc"
```

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I'm working through the key design decisions for the SSH config parsing approach, weighing whether to shell out to an existing script, reimplement the logic, or extract it into a reusable module.

Shelling out to `_ssh_cfg_py` would be expensive (~80ms per call) and only covers basic operations like finding and inserting entries, leaving me to reimplement the harder parts like rendering managed blocks and detecting conflicts across the include tree. Reimplementing the Include-resolution logic would be a third copy of the same code. Extracting into a shared module in `scripts/ssh_config.py` is more natural, and `tsnet` can already import from the source directory using the fleet trick, so that approach could work.

The catch is that `96_ssh_setup.sh` is a deployed shell file that can't import Python modules directly — it would need to embed a heredoc or call out to the source directory, which creates a dependency on the source dir existing. That's a regression for `ssh-setup-remote`, which currently just falls back to plain append if something fails. But since this is a "first 5 minutes on a new box" tool and the source dir will be freshly cloned by chezmoi anyway, that tradeoff is actually acceptable.

So I'm going with option B': reimplement the reader logic inside `tsnet` itself and make it the sole writer of its managed block, leaving `_ssh_cfg_py` untouched. The two tools do fundamentally different things — `_ssh_cfg_py` does surgical edits to existing user-authored blocks, while `tsnet` owns an entire delimited region that humans never touch. Coupling them just to avoid duplicating ~60 lines of Include glob-walking logic isn't worth the architectural entanglement. Plus `tsnet` needs capabilities that `_ssh_cfg_py` doesn't expose.

I'm mitigating the cost of having a third implementation by keeping the shared piece minimal — just one function `_resolve_includes()` that I'll copy verbatim with attribution from `_ssh_cfg_py` and mark clearly in comments. I'll also add a cross-file row to CLAUDE.md documenting all three copies, and write a bats test that verifies `tsnet ssh-config --detect-include-json` and the corresponding `_ssh` behavior stay in sync.

For the legacy fallback's "add the Include line" action, I'm delegating to `_ssh_cfg_py add-include` since that's already a tested, atomic, idempotent write to the root config — `tsnet` reads with its own code but shells out for the dangerous write, with a pure-python fallback if the shell setup isn't present.

But I'm second-guessing whether that subprocess coupling is worth it. The `add-include` logic itself is only 8 lines — find the insertion point after leading comments, insert two lines, atomic write with 0600 permissions — so I could just implement it directly in `tsnet` and have the bats test verify both implementations produce identical output on the same fixture. That avoids the weird dependency direction of a Python binary shelling out to a bash function.

Actually, I think the cleaner approach is to have `tsnet` handle everything itself and let the bats test serve as the guard against divergence. I'll mention the alternative — delegating to a `managed-block` subcommand in `_ssh_cfg_py` so there's one writer and one parser — but acknowledge that costs an extra subprocess per call and makes `ssh-setup-remote` much heavier. Since the user asked me to argue my choice, I should lay out why I'm picking the self-contained approach.

Now for the HostName decision: I'm leaning toward defaulting to the MagicDNS FQDN without a trailing dot, like `david-ubuntu.tail7f7fc5.ts.net`. It survives node re-registration since the 100.x IP can shift if the node gets removed and re-added, it's human-readable, it works with `tailscale serve` URLs, and it matches what `tailscale ssh` displays. The tradeoff is that it requires MagicDNS and the tailnet DNS resolver to be active on the client side, but `CurrentTailnet.MagicDNSEnabled` is already true in this context.

However, MagicDNS can fail when DNS settings are disabled or when `--accept-dns=false` is set — a real and common failure mode that's already documented as a pitfall on this Mac. So I'm thinking of adding a `--hostname-style` flag with options like `magicdns`, `ip`, `short`, and `auto`, defaulting to `auto`. The `auto` mode would try the MagicDNS FQDN first if `MagicDNSEnabled` is true and a local resolution probe succeeds within a timeout, then fall back to the first available IPv4 address if that fails.

I'd emit both the attempted FQDN and the fallback IP as comments in the config block so users can manually swap them if needed. The `short` option would use just the bare hostname from the MagicDNS short name, though that only works reliably when the tailnet search domain is in resolv.conf.

For the `User` field, Tailscale's `UserID` actually refers to the tailnet account owner, not the remote POSIX login, so I need a resolution order: first check for an explicit `--user` flag, then look at any existing ssh config for that alias to see if a user is already specified there. For non-TTY environments, I'll skip the `User` line entirely and add a comment instead, letting ssh default to `$USER` rather than baking in a potentially wrong value. The `--user` flag is also required for `--json` mode since there's no interactive prompting available. Then I need to define the managed block markers that will wrap the generated config sections — they need to be stable and greppable so edits inside get overwritten cleanly.

Now I'm working through the core algorithm: first resolve the output path (defaulting to `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`), then perform an include-reachability check by building the include closure from the main ssh config and verifying whether the target output file is reachable through that closure using glob pattern matching.

If the path isn't reachable, I need to handle the legacy case by presenting options to the user: either add an Include directive at the top of the config (with a warning that this changes precedence and could flip which values ssh uses), or abort with an exit code and remediation steps. The Include position should be configurable via a flag, defaulting to top.

Alternatively, I can write the managed block inline at the end of the root config file instead, which is safer since it doesn't change precedence but means the block lives in the monolith. Then I ensure the output directory exists with proper permissions and render the config block itself—a pure function that generates the Host entry with the tailnet hostname and metadata comment.

For the actual splice operation, I read the existing output file and look for the BEGIN/END marker pair. If there's exactly one pair, I replace just that span while preserving everything else byte-for-byte. If there are no markers, I append the new block with a blank line separator at the end. But if there are multiple pairs or the markers are malformed, I refuse and exit with an error.

The key insight for idempotency is that I should only update the timestamp when the actual body content changes. I'm dropping the timestamp from the block entirely and instead putting the tailnet name and format version on the BEGIN line, then excluding that line from the comparison. This way, if nothing substantive changed, the file stays byte-identical and doesn't churn the modification time.

# Implementation Plan — `tsnet` CLI + `tailnet` tv channel

## 0. Live findings that change the design

Two things I verified on this Mac that you should read before the plan:

**(a) This Mac IS the legacy no-`Include` case — and it is already silently broken.**
```
~/.ssh/config          308 lines, zero `Include` directives (grep -in include → nothing)
~/.ssh/config.d/       00-defaults, 01_git   ← never loaded
~/.ssh/config.d/01_git sets `Host github.com` → `User git`
ssh -G github.com      → `user david`        ← proof the drop-in is dead
```
So the fallback you asked for is not hypothetical; it is the *default* path on your primary machine, and `tsnet` will hit it on the very first run. This also makes the legacy branch fully verifiable today.

**(b) `tailscale debug prefs` has no `OperatorUser` key on this Mac.** The field is `json:",omitempty"` in `ipn.Prefs`, so *absent* means unset. The operator check must treat "key missing" as "not set", and must be skipped entirely on Darwin (macOS has no operator concept — the CLI authenticates through the app's local API).

Other confirmations: `tailscale serve status --json` → `{}` rc 0 when unconfigured (clean sentinel); `CertDomains` is `null`; `tailscale 1.98.9`; `Peer` has 14 entries; `Self` has no `Tags` key when untagged; `serve --bg` and `--https value` both exist.

**One simpler option, stated once as required:** you could skip the new CLI entirely — `tsnet serve` is ~15 lines of shell around `tailscale serve --bg`, and `ssh-config` is `tailscale status --json | jq -r` piped into a heredoc. I'm not planning that, because the preflight/verify logic and the `Include`-reachability walk are exactly the parts that don't survive being shell, and (a) above proves the silent-failure mode is real. Planning what you asked for.

**Naming caveat (one line):** `tsnet` is also the name of Tailscale's own embeddable Go library (`tailscale.com/tsnet`). Cosmetic only — no binary collision — but expect the occasional confusing search result. Keeping the name.
